knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a class of smooth, possibly nonconvex minimization instances, let \(\mathcal O\) be an oracle specification, and let \(\tau_\varepsilon:\mathcal P\times\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}\) be a prescribed approximate-criticality test. An algorithm \(A\) generates an oracle transcript \(\mathcal T=(e_1,e_2,\ldots)\), and \(R(\mathcal T_t)\in\mathbb R_+^m\) records the resources consumed by its first \(t\) events.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic, finite-dimensional worst-case complexity for smooth nonconvex minimization; the definition does not assert that any particular method attains a finite bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(P\in\mathcal P\), define the first certified stopping index by \[T_A(P,\varepsilon):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\tau_\varepsilon(P,x_t)=1\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). The resource complexity of \(A\) at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is the componentwise worst-case vector \[\mathcal C_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal P,\mathcal O):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}R(\mathcal T_{T_A(P,\varepsilon)}).\] A scalar complexity convention is obtained only after fixing a monotone cost map \(c:\mathbb R_+^m\to\mathbb R_+\), giving \(C_A^c(\varepsilon):=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}c(R(\mathcal T_{T_A(P,\varepsilon)}))\). Thus a nonconvex complexity statement is defined by the quadruple consisting of the problem class, oracle, termination certificate, and resource accounting rule; changing any member changes the complexity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic nonconvex complexity framework fixes a problem class \(\mathcal P\), an information oracle \(\mathcal O\), an approximate-criticality test \(\tau_\varepsilon\), and a resource measure \(R\). For each instance, the stopping time is the first transcript index at which the criticality test succeeds, with value \(+\infty\) if this never occurs. Worst-case complexity is the componentwise supremum, over all admitted instances, of the resources consumed through that stopping time. A scalar bound is meaningful only after a monotone aggregation rule for the resource vector has also been fixed.
assumptions_latex: Every instance \(P\in\mathcal P\) has the common ambient decision space \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) or an explicitly dimension-indexed analogue.
The transcript records every information request and every resource event counted by \(R\).
The certificate \(\tau_\varepsilon\) and tolerance domain are fixed before taking the supremum over \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal P,\mathcal O)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}R(\mathcal T_{T_A(P,\varepsilon)})\), where \(T_A(P,\varepsilon)=\inf\{t:\tau_\varepsilon(P,x_t)=1\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A component bound \(\mathcal C_{A,i}(\varepsilon)\le B_i(\varepsilon)\) means that every \(P\in\mathcal P\) reaches the prescribed certificate after at most \(B_i(\varepsilon)\) units of resource \(i\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(R=N_f\) gives objective-evaluation complexity; taking \(R=(N_0,\ldots,N_p)\) gives derivative-order evaluation complexity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two rates cannot be compared without holding fixed \(\mathcal P\), \(\mathcal O\), \(\tau_\varepsilon\), and the cost aggregation convention.
boundary_notes: Randomized and stochastic algorithms require an additional probabilistic quantifier, such as expectation or a high-probability guarantee.
The available local source hints did not expose a full-text locator supporting this exact four-part framework.

notation.meaning: First index at which algorithm A certifies the requested tolerance on instance P.
Vector of resources consumed by the transcript prefix through event t.

review_flags: No inspected source gave an exact locator for the complete problem-class/oracle/certificate/resource quadruple.

children.title: Computational Cost and Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Separates evaluation, derivative-access, inner-solve, and arithmetic views of computational effort.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transcript-Based Computational Cost and Oracle Taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\) interact with an oracle through a finite transcript \(\mathcal T=(e_i)_{i=1}^M\). Each event has a type in a fixed alphabet \(\mathfrak E\) containing value evaluations, full derivatives, derivative products, arithmetic operations, memory events, and iterations of auxiliary solvers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic accounting for smooth finite-dimensional algorithms; it separates information access from the work used to process that information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computational cost-oracle taxonomy is a pair \((\kappa,R)\), where \(\kappa:\mathfrak E\to\mathbb R_+^m\) assigns a nonnegative resource vector to each event and \[R(\mathcal T):=\sum_{i=1}^M\kappa(e_i).\] Coordinates are partitioned as \[R(\mathcal T)=\bigl(R_{\mathrm{eval}},R_{\mathrm{der}},R_{\mathrm{prod}},R_{\mathrm{inner}},R_{\mathrm{arith}},R_{\mathrm{mem}}\bigr),\] representing objective evaluations, full derivative evaluations by order, derivative contractions, auxiliary-solver work, arithmetic work, and storage or communication. Two transcripts satisfy \(\mathcal T\preceq\mathcal T'\) exactly when \(R_i(\mathcal T)\le R_i(\mathcal T')\) for every coordinate. A scalar cost is a declared monotone functional \(c(R)\); it is not intrinsic to the oracle transcript. An oracle model is therefore identified by the information returned by each query, whereas a cost model is identified by \(\kappa\) and any chosen aggregation \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy assigns every event in an algorithm's transcript a nonnegative resource vector and sums these vectors. Separate coordinates record value evaluations, full derivatives, derivative products, inner-solver iterations, arithmetic, and memory or communication. Transcript cost is naturally compared componentwise. Any single-number cost requires an explicitly declared monotone aggregation rule. Consequently, two algorithms may use the same oracle while having different processing costs, or have the same evaluation count while using different derivative information.
assumptions_latex: The event alphabet \(\mathfrak E\) and the charge map \(\kappa\) are fixed independently of the problem instance.
Cached information is represented either by a zero-cost reuse event or by no new oracle event.
Every charged auxiliary computation is assigned to at least one resource coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\mathcal T)=\sum_{e\in\mathcal T}\kappa(e)\), with oracle information and computational charging represented by distinct specifications.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Weighted accounting has \(c_w(R)=w^{\mathsf T}R\) for a declared vector \(w\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
Componentwise accounting is equivalent to retaining the complete event-count vector before choosing prices.
special_cases_latex: The unit-cost RAM convention charges elementary arithmetic uniformly while retaining oracle calls as separate coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: An evaluation-complexity bound alone need not control inner Krylov iterations, factorization work, or storage.
boundary_notes: The taxonomy does not prescribe hardware-dependent prices.
The inspected sources discuss several members of this taxonomy but do not state this exact unified definition.

notation.meaning: Resource charge assigned to event e.
Cumulative resource vector of a transcript.

review_flags: Unified taxonomy is not directly supported by an inspected exact source locator.
Requires a source explicitly separating oracle information, evaluation counts, inner work, arithmetic, and storage.

children.title: Evaluation Cost Accounting
children.top_down_role: Deterministic accounting by objective and derivative evaluations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) possess derivatives through order \(p\). A deterministic algorithm produces a finite transcript \(\mathcal T=(e_i)_{i=1}^M\), whose events identify whether new values of \(f\) or \(D^j f\) are computed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts newly executed exact objective and full-derivative evaluations; it excludes derivative-product, arithmetic, and inner-iteration costs unless separately charged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(j=0,1,\ldots,p\), let \(I_j(\mathcal T)\) be the indices at which the algorithm newly evaluates \(D^j f(x_i)\), with \(D^0f=f\). The order-\(j\) evaluation count and joint evaluation vector are \[N_j(\mathcal T):=|I_j(\mathcal T)|,\qquad N_{0:p}(\mathcal T):=(N_0,\ldots,N_p).\] Recomputing the same quantity is a new evaluation, while retrieving an explicitly cached result is not. If one oracle call returns several derivative orders simultaneously, the convention must declare either a single joint-event count or one unit in every returned coordinate. For a stopping certificate with stopping transcript \(\mathcal T_\varepsilon(P)\), a worst-case evaluation bound is \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}N_j(\mathcal T_\varepsilon(P))\le B_j(\varepsilon).\] A weighted total \(N_w=\sum_{j=0}^p w_jN_j\) is defined only after the nonnegative prices \(w_j\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-\(j\) evaluation cost is the number of transcript events that newly compute the objective when \(j=0\), or the full derivative of order \(j\) when \(j\ge1\). Repeated computations count again, but cached retrievals do not. Joint oracle calls require an explicit convention. Worst-case evaluation complexity takes the supremum of these counts over the admitted problem class before the requested stopping certificate is reached.
assumptions_latex: The oracle interface identifies which derivative orders are newly produced by every event.
The stopping certificate and the treatment of joint evaluations are fixed in advance.
The count concerns full derivative objects, not directional contractions, unless those are expressly designated as evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_j(\mathcal T)=|I_j(\mathcal T)|\) and \(N_{0:p}(\mathcal T)=(N_0,\ldots,N_p)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For unit prices, \(N_{\mathrm{joint}}=\sum_{j=0}^pN_j\), provided a joint oracle response is charged once in each returned coordinate.
special_cases_latex: A first-order method is commonly reported using \((N_f,N_g)=(N_0,N_1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Separate component bounds retain information that is lost in a weighted total.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time and the cost of forming a derivative are not determined by the count.
No inspected source stated the complete cache and joint-call convention used here.

notation.meaning: Indices of newly executed order-j evaluations.
Declared weighted aggregate of evaluation counts.

review_flags: Exact accounting conventions require an authoritative source.
Nearby local material discusses computational work but not this full transcript definition.

children.title: Function Evaluation Counts
children.top_down_role: Coverage of deterministic objective-evaluation accounting across regularization frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Function Evaluation Counts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts objective-value oracle calls in a finite algorithmic execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an execution generate a finite oracle transcript \(Q=(q_1,\ldots,q_T)\), where each query has a type \(\tau(q_i)\). The function-evaluation count is \[N_f(Q):=\sum_{i=1}^{T}\mathbf{1}\{\tau(q_i)=f\}.\] A query is counted whenever the algorithm requests a value \(f(x)\), including requests at rejected trial points. Repeated requests at the same point count separately unless the computational model explicitly provides caching at zero cost. Values returned jointly with derivatives are counted according to the declared joint-accounting convention rather than being silently treated as free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function-evaluation count is the number of requested objective values, including rejected trials and repeated uncached requests.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle query in \(Q\) has a declared type.

notation.meaning: type of the ith oracle query

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this evaluation-accounting convention.
A source specifying treatment of rejected trials, repeated queries, and caching is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the mathematics is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the conventions for rejected trials, repeated uncached requests, caching, or joint returns.

children.title: Derivative Evaluation Counts
children.top_down_role: Coverage of gradient, Hessian, plus higher-derivative evaluation accounting.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Evaluation Counts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates derivative-oracle calls by derivative order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) possess derivatives through order \(p\), and let \(Q=(q_1,\ldots,q_T)\) be an execution transcript. For \(j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), define \[N_j(Q):=\sum_{i=1}^{T}\mathbf{1}\{q_i\text{ requests }D^j f(x_i)\}.\] Thus \(N_1\) counts gradient evaluations, \(N_2\) counts Hessian evaluations, and higher components count the corresponding derivative tensors. If one oracle call returns several orders jointly, each marginal counter is incremented only when marginal accounting is declared; otherwise that call belongs to a separate joint-query class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative evaluations are counted by order, with joint derivative returns handled by an explicitly declared marginal or joint convention.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(p\)-times differentiable at every queried point.
Each derivative request declares its returned orders.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_j(Q)=\sum_{i=1}^{T}\mathbf{1}\{q_i\text{ requests }D^j f(x_i)\}\) for \(1\le j\le p\).

notation.meaning: jth Fréchet derivative of f at x

review_flags: The supplied gradient-information locator does not establish derivative-order evaluation accounting.
A complexity source defining marginal versus joint derivative counts is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-indexed definition fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no source with a specific locator supports the marginal-versus-joint derivative-counting convention.

children.title: Joint Evaluation Accounting
children.top_down_role: Coverage of complexity comparisons that charge function information separately from derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Evaluation Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a cost convention for oracle calls returning several quantities together.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{S}\) be the collection of nonempty subsets of \(\{0,1,\ldots,p\}\), where order \(0\) denotes the function value. If \(N_S(Q)\) is the number of calls in transcript \(Q\) that jointly return exactly \(\{D^j f(x):j\in S\}\), then a weighted joint evaluation cost is \[C_{m joint}(Q):=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}}w_S N_S(Q),\qquad w_S\ge0.\] Marginal accounting is recovered by assigning each joint call to every returned order; call accounting instead increments only \(N_S\). A complexity claim must state which convention and weights it uses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint calls are classified by the exact set of returned derivative orders and aggregated using declared nonnegative costs.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle call declares the exact set of quantities returned.
The weights \(w_S\) are fixed independently of the execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\rm joint}(Q)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal{S}}w_S N_S(Q)\).

notation.meaning: set of derivative orders returned by one call
number of calls returning exactly the orders in S
declared cost of one joint call of class S

review_flags: No supplied source locator defines joint-oracle evaluation accounting.
The admissible cost weights and marginal-counting convention require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted joint-call definition fits the terminal container, but the classification by exact returned-order sets, admissible weights, and relationship to marginal accounting are unsupported by cited evidence.

children.title: Derivative-Order Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Comparisons indexed by the highest available derivative order.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Order Oracle Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies exact local oracles by their highest available derivative order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\ge0\) and a function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) that is \(p\)-times differentiable, an exact order-\(p\) local oracle is the mapping \[\mathcal{O}_p(x)=\bigl(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^p f(x)\bigr).\] An algorithm is an order-\(p\) oracle method if each new query point is determined from its internal state and previously returned values of \(\mathcal{O}_p\). Its oracle complexity at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is the worst-case number of oracle calls required to output a point satisfying the declared accuracy predicate. Comparisons across derivative orders are meaningful only for the same function class, accuracy predicate, and joint-call convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-p oracle returns all derivatives through order p; its complexity counts calls needed to meet a fixed accuracy criterion.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has derivatives through order \(p\) at every queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_p(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^p f(x))\).

notation.meaning: exact local oracle through derivative order p
accuracy tolerance in the declared output predicate

review_flags: No supplied locator establishes this formal oracle model.
A nonconvex oracle-complexity source is required for the information and adaptivity conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the topic's derivative-order comparison role, but no source establishes the exact local-oracle information, adaptive-query, joint-call, and worst-case complexity conventions used here.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Derivative Oracle of Maximum Order
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb N_0\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, and let \(f\in C^p(U)\). For \(j\ge1\), \(D^jf(x)\) is regarded as a symmetric \(j\)-linear form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic full-tensor oracle access in finite dimensions; product-only and noisy access are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The full derivative oracle of maximum order \(p\) is the map \[\mathcal O_p^f:U\to\prod_{j=0}^p\mathcal L_s^j(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathcal O_p^f(x)=\bigl(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^pf(x)\bigr),\] where \(\mathcal L_s^0(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R\). An algorithm is an order-\(p\) derivative-oracle method if every dependence on the unknown objective is measurable with respect to the finite sequence of responses \(\mathcal O_p^f(x_0),\ldots,\mathcal O_p^f(x_k)\) and no response containing \(D^jf\) for \(j>p\) is available. An individual-order interface may instead return only \(D^jf(x)\); its transcript must retain the order label. The oracle order is the largest derivative order available, not the largest order actually queried on every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-\(p\) full derivative oracle returns the objective and every derivative through order \(p\) at a requested point. An order-\(p\) method may base its decisions only on its previous queries, these responses, and declared problem data, and it receives no derivative above order \(p\). The label records available information and does not require the method to request the highest derivative at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^p(U)\) so every returned derivative is defined and continuous.
Oracle responses are exact full multilinear forms.
Declared side information does not encode undeclared higher-order derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_p^f(x)=(D^jf(x))_{j=0}^p\), and an order-\(p\) oracle transcript contains no derivative information of order exceeding \(p\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In coordinates, \(D^1f(x)\) is the gradient and \(D^2f(x)\) is the Hessian, after identifying linear forms with their Euclidean representations.
special_cases_latex: \(p=0\) is a value oracle, \(p=1\) a first-order oracle, and \(p=2\) a second-order oracle.
immediate_consequences_latex: Complexity comparisons indexed by \(p\) compare different information classes unless the oracle convention is held fixed.
boundary_notes: A Hessian-vector product oracle is weaker than a full Hessian oracle under this definition.
No exact inspected source locator was found for this information-based formulation.

notation.meaning: Space of symmetric j-linear real-valued forms.
Exact full derivative oracle through order p.

review_flags: Requires an authoritative oracle-complexity source distinguishing full tensors from derivative products.
The definition is standard in form but the exact information restriction lacks inspected source support.

children.title: Derivative-Product Oracle Family
children.top_down_role: Access models based on derivative products and directional contractions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^p(U)\) on an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For \(1\le j\le p\), \(D^jf(x)\) is a symmetric \(j\)-linear form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact matrix-free access by contractions; the fully assembled derivative tensors are not returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le r\le j\le p\), the \((j,r)\)-contraction oracle is \[\mathcal O_{j,r}^f(x;v_1,\ldots,v_r):=D^jf(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_r,\,\cdot\,,\ldots,\,\cdot\,],\] an element of \(\mathcal L_s^{j-r}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)\). A derivative-product oracle family is any declared collection \(\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{prod}}\subseteq\{\mathcal O_{j,r}^f:1\le r\le j\le p\}\), with one query charged for each requested contraction and its direction arguments. The case \(j=2,r=1\) returns the linear form represented by the Hessian-vector product \(\nabla^2f(x)v\); the case \(r=j\) returns the scalar directional derivative \(D^jf(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_j]\). Access to contractions does not, by definition, include storage or formation of the full tensor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-product oracle receives a point and one or more directions and returns the corresponding partial contraction of a derivative tensor. Contracting a Hessian once gives a Hessian-vector product; contracting every slot gives a scalar directional derivative. The available contraction types must be declared, and each request is counted separately. The oracle is matrix-free or tensor-free because it does not return the complete derivative object.
assumptions_latex: All requested directions lie in \(\mathbb R^n\), and \(x\in U\).
The response contains only the declared contraction, not an implicitly assembled full tensor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_{j,r}^f(x;v_1,\ldots,v_r)=D^jf(x)[v_1,ldots,v_r,\cdot^{\,j-r}]\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under the Euclidean identification, \(\mathcal O_{2,1}^f(x;v)\) is the vector \(\nabla^2f(x)v\).
special_cases_latex: Hessian-free Newton-CG uses \(\mathcal O_{2,1}^f\) within its inner conjugate-gradient iteration.
immediate_consequences_latex: Product-query complexity can differ substantially from full-Hessian evaluation complexity.
boundary_notes: Finite-difference approximations to products constitute an inexact oracle and are outside the exact definition.

notation.meaning: Oracle returning an r-fold contraction of the jth derivative.
Declared family of available contraction queries.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7, discussion immediately before equation (7.10): Hessian-free Newton methods require Hessian-vector products rather than an explicitly known Hessian

review_flags: The source directly supports the Hessian-vector special case; the higher-order contraction-family generalization should receive an additional source.

children.title: Matrix-Free Derivative Access
children.top_down_role: Coverage of derivative access without explicit matrix formation.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Derivative Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Hessian access through products rather than explicit matrix formation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable. A matrix-free Hessian-product oracle accepts \((x,v)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\) and returns \[\mathcal{O}_{Hv}(x,v)=\nabla^2 f(x)v,\] without returning or requiring storage of the full matrix \(\nabla^2 f(x)\). An algorithm using only such products may form linear combinations of returned vectors and choose later directions adaptively. Its derivative-product complexity is the number of calls to \(\mathcal{O}_{Hv}\); arithmetic used to generate directions or solve an inner problem is accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free Hessian access returns Hessian-vector products without forming the Hessian, and each requested product counts as one oracle call.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice differentiable at queried points.
The oracle returns exact Hessian-vector products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{Hv}(x,v)=\nabla^2 f(x)v\) without explicit formation of \(\nabla^2 f(x)\).
review_flags: The supplied matrix-norm and matrix-modification locators do not define matrix-free oracle access.
A source specifying the product-oracle cost model is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hessian-vector oracle definition and definition content kind fit the leaf. An authoritative locator is still required for the matrix-free information model, unit call count, and separation of product-oracle work from inner arithmetic.

children.title: Tensor-Product Oracle Access
children.top_down_role: Coverage of higher-derivative contractions supplied through product interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Product Oracle Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends matrix-vector access to products with higher-order derivative tensors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(q\)-times differentiable, with \(q\ge2\), and identify vectors with linear functionals through the Euclidean inner product. A tensor-product oracle receives \((x,v_1,\ldots,v_{q-1})\) and returns the unique vector \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \[\langle u,w\rangle=D^q f(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_{q-1},w]\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] One oracle call reveals this contracted vector, not the full coefficient array of \(D^q f(x)\). For \(q=2\), the definition reduces to Hessian-vector access.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tensor-product oracle contracts a qth derivative with q−1 directions and returns the remaining vector representation.
assumptions_latex: \(q\ge2\) and \(f\) is \(q\)-times differentiable at the query point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle u,w\rangle=D^q f(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_{q-1},w]\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
review_flags: No supplied locator supports higher-order tensor-product oracle access.
The precise contraction and unit-cost conventions require an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean Riesz-represented contraction is mathematically precise and reduces correctly to Hessian-vector access for q=2, but no cited source supports this higher-order product-oracle model or its information-per-call convention.

children.title: Directional Contraction Oracles
children.top_down_role: Coverage of derivative information restricted to selected directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Contraction Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scalar access to repeated-direction derivative contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(q\)-times differentiable. children.title: Product-Oracle Information Limits
children.top_down_role: Coverage of complexity distinctions caused by restricted derivative access.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Oracle Information Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies nonidentifiability from finitely many scalar tensor contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\ge2\), and let \(T\) be an unknown symmetric \(q\)-linear form on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Its parameter space has dimension \(d=\binom{n+q-1}{q}\). Given directions \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\), a diagonal product oracle reveals only \(T[v_i,\ldots,v_i]\). If \(m<d\), then there exists a nonzero symmetric form \(S\) such that \[S[v_i,\ldots,v_i]=0\quad\text{for all }i=1,\ldots,m.\] Consequently, \(T\) and \(T+S\) produce identical responses to those queries, so the full tensor cannot be uniquely identified without additional structural assumptions or sufficiently many independent contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fewer scalar contractions than the symmetric tensor-space dimension cannot uniquely identify an unrestricted derivative tensor.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is an unrestricted symmetric \(q\)-linear form on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
The oracle returns exact diagonal scalar contractions at \(m\) specified directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m<\binom{n+q-1}{q}\) implies that the queried contractions do not uniquely determine \(T\).

children.title: Operation-Inner-Solve Cost Models
children.top_down_role: Arithmetic, storage, and auxiliary-solver costs hidden by evaluation counts.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider an outer algorithm producing iterates \(x_k\) and invoking an auxiliary solver at outer iteration \(k\). Let \(J_k\) be the number of inner iterations and let \(a_{k\ell}\), \(m_{k\ell}\), and \(q_{k\ell}\) record arithmetic, memory, and derivative-product work at inner iteration \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic implementation-sensitive accounting supplementing outer evaluation counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The operation-inner-solve resource vector through outer iteration \(K\) is \[R_{\mathrm{op}}(K):=\left(\sum_{k=0}^{K}J_k,\ \sum_{k=0}^{K}\sum_{\ell=1}^{J_k}q_{k\ell},\ \sum_{k=0}^{K}\sum_{\ell=1}^{J_k}a_{k\ell},\ \max_{0\le k\le K,\,1\le\ell\le J_k}m_{k\ell}\right).\] Its coordinates respectively measure inner iterations, derivative-product calls, cumulative arithmetic operations, and peak live storage. If \(w\in\mathbb R_+^4\) is a declared price vector, the corresponding scalar work is \(W_w(K)=w^{\mathsf T}R_{\mathrm{op}}(K)\). An inner solve terminates when a declared residual or model condition \(\mathcal R_k(z_{k,J_k})\le\eta_k\) is met, or when another declared stopping event such as boundary intersection or negative curvature occurs. The tolerance sequence \((\eta_k)\) is part of the cost model because it determines \(J_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operation-inner-solve accounting records total inner iterations, derivative-product queries made inside them, cumulative arithmetic, and peak storage. A scalar work estimate requires declared prices. The inner stopping tolerance and alternative stopping events are part of the model because they determine how much auxiliary work is performed. These costs are not recoverable from the number of outer objective evaluations alone.
assumptions_latex: Each inner iteration exposes its charged arithmetic and oracle events.
The residual map \(\mathcal R_k\), tolerance \(\eta_k\), and alternative stopping events are declared.
Peak storage is measured over live data rather than summed over time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{op}}(K)=(N_{\mathrm{inner}},N_{\mathrm{prod}},N_{\mathrm{arith}},M_{\mathrm{peak}})\) with the coordinates defined by the displayed sums and maximum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If one Hessian-vector product is used per Krylov iteration, then \(N_{\mathrm{prod}}=N_{\mathrm{inner}}\).
special_cases_latex: For Newton-CG with finite-difference Hessian-vector products, one new gradient evaluation may be charged per CG iteration.
immediate_consequences_latex: An outer evaluation bound does not imply a comparable arithmetic bound unless the inner work per outer iteration is controlled.

children.title: Arithmetic Operation Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Operation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts elementary arithmetic performed outside explicitly priced oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a computational model with a declared set \(\mathcal{A}\) of unit-cost scalar operations, such as addition, multiplication, division, comparison, and square root. For an execution \(E\), its arithmetic operation complexity is \[C_{\rm arith}(E):=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}N_a(E),\] where \(N_a(E)\) counts executions of operation \(a\). Oracle evaluations, memory transfers, factorizations, and tensor contractions contribute only through their chosen implementations or separately declared costs. A worst-case arithmetic bound is the supremum of \(C_{\rm arith}(E)\) over all admissible problem instances and executions terminating at the prescribed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arithmetic complexity counts declared unit-cost scalar operations, while oracle, memory, and structured-kernel costs require explicit treatment.

Executions terminate under a common accuracy predicate.

children.title: Inner-Solve Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregates work used to solve regularized or trust-region subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer method performs \(K\) iterations and, at iteration \(k\), invokes an inner solver until a declared residual or model-stationarity measure satisfies \(r_k\le\eta_k\). If \(t_k\) is the number of inner iterations and \(c_{k,\ell}\) is the arithmetic or product-oracle cost of inner iteration \(\ell\), then \[T_{\rm inner}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}t_k,\qquad C_{\rm inner}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{t_k}c_{k,\ell}.\] If uniformly \(t_k\le T(\eta_k)\) and \(c_{k,\ell}\le c_k\), then \(C_{\rm inner}\le\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}c_kT(\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total inner-solve work is the sum of inner iterations or their costs across all outer iterations and stopping tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Each inner solve has a declared termination test \(r_k\le\eta_k\).
The per-inner-iteration costs \(c_{k,\ell}\) use one fixed cost model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\rm inner}\le\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}c_kT(\eta_k)\) under the stated uniform bounds.

children.title: Storage Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Storage Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures peak simultaneously live storage during an algorithmic execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite execution \(E\), let \(L_t\) be the collection of scalar memory locations holding live algorithmic data immediately after event \(t\), including iterates, derivative representations, workspaces, and retained oracle outputs. The storage complexity is \[M(E):=\max_t |L_t|.\] An object represented by \(s\) scalars contributes \(s\) locations while live. Matrix-free access excludes storage of a full derivative matrix or tensor but includes all vectors, recurrence data, and cached products actually retained. A worst-case storage bound takes the supremum of \(M(E)\) over admissible instances of the stated dimension.

children.title: Evaluation-to-Operation Translation
children.top_down_role: Coverage of regimes where evaluation guarantees do or do not imply practical cost guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-to-Operation Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts oracle-call bounds into arithmetic bounds under implementation-cost assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an execution use oracle classes \(s\in\mathcal{S}\), with \(N_s\) calls of class \(s\). Suppose one call of class \(s\) costs at most \(c_s(n)\) arithmetic operations, all inner solves cost at most \(C_{\rm inner}\), and remaining algorithmic overhead costs at most \(C_{m over}\). Then the total arithmetic cost satisfies \[C_{\rm arith}\le C_{\rm over}+C_{\rm inner}+\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}N_s c_s(n).\] Hence an evaluation-complexity bound yields an operation-complexity bound only after dimension-dependent oracle implementations, joint returns, product costs, and inner-solve work have been explicitly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-call bounds translate to arithmetic bounds by multiplying each call count by its implementation cost and adding inner-solve and overhead costs.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle class \(s\) has a valid arithmetic upper bound \(c_s(n)\).
Inner-solve and nonoracle overhead costs are bounded separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\rm arith}\le C_{\rm over}+C_{\rm inner}+\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}}N_sc_s(n)\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(q\)-times continuously differentiable, let \(q\ge1\), and define \(T_{f,q}(x,d)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^qD^jf(x)[d]^j/j!\). Let \(\delta\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained, deterministic, finite-dimensional approximate criticality expressed by the best local decrease of an order-q Taylor polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The order-\(q\), radius-\(\delta\) Taylor decrement is \[\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x):=f(x)-\min_{\|d\|\le\delta}T_{f,q}(x,d)=\max_{\|d\|\le\delta}\bigl(T_{f,q}(x,0)-T_{f,q}(x,d)\bigr).\] With \(\chi_q(\delta):=\sum_{j=1}^q\delta^j/j!\), a point \(x\) is an \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-approximate critical point of order \(q\) when \[\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)le\varepsilon\chi_q(delta).\] A multi-tolerance target through order \(q\) requires radii \(\delta_j\in(0,1]\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_j>0\) such that \(\phi_{f,j}^{\delta_j}(x)\le\varepsilon_j\chi_j(\delta_j)\) for every \(j=1,ldots,q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-q criticality measure is the largest decrease predicted by the order-q Taylor polynomial over a ball of radius \(\delta\). A point is approximately critical when this predicted decrease is at most \(\varepsilon\) times the normalization \(\chi_q(delta)\). A target through order \(q\) may impose the corresponding inequality separately at every lower order, with order-dependent tolerances and radii.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^q\) on a neighborhood of the closed ball \(x+\delta\mathbb B\).
The norm used for the Taylor ball and multilinear operator norms is fixed.
The Taylor subproblem minimum exists, as it does in finite dimensions on the compact ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-critical of order \(q\) exactly when \(\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)\le\varepsilon\chi_q(\delta)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)=\max_{\|d\|\le\delta}\{-\sum_{j=1}^qD^jf(x)[d]^j/j!\}\).
special_cases_latex: For \(q=1\) with the Euclidean norm, \(\phi_{f,1}^{\delta}(x)=\delta\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact Taylor criticality at radius \(\delta\) corresponds to \(\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained, gradient-based approximate first-order criticality in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable at \(x\). For a tolerance \(\epsilon_1\ge 0\), the point \(x\) is an \(\epsilon_1\)-approximate first-order critical point of \(f\) when \[\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le \epsilon_1.\] The case \(\epsilon_1=0\) gives exact first-order criticality. This definition measures stationarity only; it does not distinguish local minima, local maxima, or saddle points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is approximately first-order critical when its gradient norm is at most the prescribed tolerance; this condition alone does not identify the type of stationary point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is first-order critical to tolerance \(\epsilon_1\) if and only if \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\epsilon_1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained approximate second-order criticality using gradient size and minimum Hessian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable at \(x\). Given tolerances \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge 0\), the point \(x\) is an \((\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\)-approximate second-order critical point when \[\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\epsilon_1\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\ge-\epsilon_2.\] Thus no unit direction has quadratic curvature below \(-\epsilon_2\). With both tolerances zero, these are the standard first- and second-order necessary conditions for an unconstrained local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate second-order criticality requires both a small gradient and absence of Hessian curvature more negative than the allowed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\epsilon_1\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge-\epsilon_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be three times continuously differentiable near \(x\), and define \(T_{f,j}(x,d)=f(x)+\sum_{\ell=1}^{j}\nabla^\ell f(x)[d]^\ell/\ell!\). knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix \(q\in\mathbb N\), an open set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a function \(f\in C^q(U)\), a point \(x\in U\), and a radius \(\delta>0\) with \(x+\delta\mathbb B\subset U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary finite-order unconstrained Taylor criticality in a fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the order-q Taylor polynomial and its decrement by \[T_{f,q}(x,d):=f(x)+\sum_{ell=1}^q\frac{1}{\ell!}D^ell f(x)[d]^ell,\qquad \Delta T_{f,q}(x,d):=T_{f,q}(x,0)-T_{f,q}(x,d).\] The general Taylor criticality measure is \[\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x):=max_{\|d\|\le\delta}\Delta T_{f,q}(x,d).\] For a declared scale \(s_q(delta)>0\), \(x\) is \((q,varepsilon,delta)\)-Taylor critical when \(\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)le\varepsilon s_q(delta)\). Under the factorial normalization, \(s_q(delta)=\chi_q(delta):=\sum_{ell=1}^q\delta^ell/\ell!\). Exact order-q Taylor criticality means \(\phi_{f,q}^{\delta}(x)=0\). The choice of radius and scale is part of the definition and must remain fixed in a complexity comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any finite order \(q\), form the Taylor polynomial at \(x\) and maximize its predicted decrease over a radius-\(\delta\) ball. This maximum is the Taylor criticality measure. Approximate Taylor criticality requires it to be no larger than \(\varepsilon\) times a declared positive scale, commonly the sum of the factorially normalized powers of \(\delta\). Exact criticality means that the Taylor polynomial predicts no decrease anywhere in the ball.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^q(U)\) and the closed radius-\(\delta\) ball around \(x\) lies in \(U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convexly Constrained Criticality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order criticality measured over feasible displacements in a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(x\in F\), and let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x\). For \(\delta>0\), define \[\chi_{F,\delta}(x)=\max_{\substack{x+d\in F\\\|d\|_2\le\delta}}-\nabla f(x)^\top d.\] Given \(\epsilon\ge0\), the point \(x\) is \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-approximately critical when \(\chi_{F,\delta}(x)\le \epsilon\delta\). Exact criticality, \(\chi_{F,\delta}(x)=0\), is equivalent to \(-\nabla f(x)\in N_F(x)\), where \(N_F(x)\) is the convex normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained criticality bounds the best feasible linearized descent within a neighborhood; exact criticality is equivalent to the gradient normal-cone condition.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, with \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_{F,\delta}(x)\le\epsilon\delta\); when \(\epsilon=0\), this is equivalent to \(-\nabla f(x)\in N_F(x)\).

notation.meaning: Maximum feasible linearized decrease within radius delta.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb N_0\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, and \(f\in C^p(U)\). Let \(T_{f,p}(x,s)=\sum_{j=0}^pD^jf(x)[s]^j/j!\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact \((p,beta,L)\) smoothness regime consists of functions satisfying \[\|D^pf(x)-D^pf(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}le L\|x-y\|^\beta\qquad(x,y\in U).\] Its associated order-p Taylor model has accuracy order \(p+beta\): a model \(m_x(s)\) belongs to the \((p,beta,kappa_m)\) accuracy regime when, for every admissible segment \([x,x+s]subset U\), \[|f(x+s)-m_x(s)|le\kappa_m\|s\|^{p+beta}.\] If \(m_x=T_{f,p}(x,cdot)\), the regime is exact-derivative Taylor accuracy; if \(m_x\ne T_{f,p}\) but obeys the displayed bound, it is an approximate-model regime. More generally, an approximate model is admitted when its value differs from the true objective at a trial point by at most a constant times the step norm to that same order. knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Derivative Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical smoothness condition controlling the remainder of an order-p Taylor model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge1\), let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, and let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(p\)-times continuously differentiable. The order-\(p\) Lipschitz-derivative regime holds with constant \(L_p\ge0\) when \[\|\nabla^p f(x)-\nabla^p f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_p\|x-y\|_2\qquad(x,y\in D).\] Consequently, whenever the segment from \(x\) to \(x+s\) lies in \(D\), the Taylor remainder satisfies \[|f(x+s)-T_{f,p}(x,s)|\le\frac{L_p}{(p+1)!}\|s\|_2^{p+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pth derivative is Lipschitz continuous, which bounds the order-p Taylor remainder by a constant times the step norm raised to p+1.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the pth derivative.
Operator norm of a derivative tensor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Continuity of the Highest Derivative
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb N_0\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, and let \(f")in C^p(U)\). The derivative \(D^pf(x)\) is a symmetric \(p\)-linear form for \(p\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical exact smoothness assumption used for order-p Taylor models in finite-dimensional smooth optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has an \(L_p\)-Lipschitz continuous \(p\)th derivative on \(U\) when \[\|D^pf(x)-D^pf(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}le L_p\|x-y\|\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in U.\] Here \(L_p\in[0,infty)\) is uniform and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=max_{\|v_1\|=cdots=\|v_p\|=1}|A[v_1,ldots,v_p]|\). The corresponding order-p Taylor polynomial is \[T_{f,p}(x,s)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{1}{j!}D^jf(x)[s]^j.\] The Lipschitz-derivative regime includes the norm, domain, derivative order, and constant as part of the problem class; local Lipschitz continuity without a uniform constant on the relevant region is a different regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The \(p\)th derivative is Lipschitz continuous when its operator-norm change between any two points is bounded by a uniform constant times the distance between those points. The definition fixes the derivative order, norm, domain, and constant. The associated Taylor model contains derivatives through order \(p\). A merely pointwise or local condition is not the same as a uniform complexity assumption on the region visited by an algorithm.
assumptions_latex: \(f"):\in C^p(U)\) and \(U\) is convex so line segments used by Taylor models remain in the domain.
A single norm and its induced multilinear operator norm are used throughout.
\(L_p\) is uniform on \(U\) or on an explicitly declared invariant region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|D^pf(x)-D^pf(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_p\|x-y\|\) for every \(x,y\in U\).
special_cases_latex: For \(p=1\), the gradient is Lipschitz; for \(p=2\), the Hessian is Lipschitz.
immediate_consequences_latex: This is the Hölder derivative regime with exponent \(\beta=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Derivative Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional smoothness condition yielding a Taylor remainder of order p plus beta.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\ge1\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), and let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. A function \(f\in C^p(D)\) has a \(\beta\)-Hölder continuous \(p\)th derivative with constant \(L_{p,\beta}\) when \[\|\nabla^p f(x)-\nabla^p f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{p,\beta}\|x-y\|_2^\beta\qquad(x,y\in D).\] For every admissible segment from \(x\) to \(x+s\), this implies \[|f(x+s)-T_{f,p}(x,s)|\le\frac{L_{p,\beta}\Gamma(\beta+1)}{\Gamma(p+\beta+1)}\|s\|_2^{p+\beta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hölder continuity of the pth derivative gives a fractional-order Taylor remainder proportional to the step norm raised to p+beta.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(x+s)-T_{f,p}(x,s)|\le L_{p,\beta}\Gamma(\beta+1)\|s\|_2^{p+\beta}/\Gamma(p+\beta+1)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hölder Continuity of the Highest Derivative
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb N_0\), \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, and \(f\in C^p(U)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fractional-smoothness class for finite-dimensional deterministic Taylor-model methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) has an \((L_{p,beta},beta)\)-Hölder continuous \(p\)th derivative on \(U\) when \[\|D^pf(x)-D^pf(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}le L_{p,beta}\|x-y\|^\beta\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in U.\] The Hölder derivative regime is the class \[\mathcal F_{p,beta}(L_{p,beta};U):=\{f\in C^p(U):D^pf\text{ satisfies the displayed inequality}\}.\] Its parameters include \(p\), \(\beta\), \(L_{p,beta}\), the norm, and the region of uniformity. The endpoint \(\beta=1\) is Lipschitz continuity, whereas \(0<\beta<1\) is fractional smoothness. An algorithm may be analyzed on this class whether or not \(\beta\) and \(L_{p,beta}\) are supplied as inputs; that information distinction must be declared separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A \(p\)th derivative is Hölder continuous with exponent \(\beta\) when its operator-norm change is bounded by a constant times distance raised to \(\beta\). The associated function class fixes the derivative order, exponent, constant, norm, and domain. Exponent one gives the Lipschitz case; smaller positive exponents describe fractional smoothness. Whether the algorithm knows these parameters is separate from whether the objective satisfies the condition.
assumptions_latex: The same vector norm and induced operator norm are used in both sides of the inequality.
The Hölder bound is uniform on the declared region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\in\mathcal F_{p,beta}(L_{p,beta};U)\) exactly when \(\|D^pf(x)-D^pf(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{p,beta}\|x-y\|^\beta\) for all \(x,y\in U\).
special_cases_latex: \(\beta=1\) recovers the Lipschitz highest-derivative class.
immediate_consequences_latex: The class becomes weaker as the allowed exponent decreases, with constants and domain held fixed.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes the discontinuous endpoint \(\beta=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Smoothness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder-smooth objectives whose exponent or scale is unavailable to the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\ge1\) and a domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). An optimization problem is in an unknown-smoothness regime for an algorithm \(\mathcal{A}\) when there exist \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and \(L_{p,\beta}<\infty\) such that \[\|\nabla^p f(x)-\nabla^p f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{p,\beta}\|x-y\|_2^\beta\qquad(x,y\in D),\] but neither \(\beta\) nor a valid upper bound on \(L_{p,\beta}\) is supplied to \(\mathcal{A}\). Any claimed universal guarantee must therefore use observable model agreement or adaptive regularization rather than these unknown parameters as inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective has some Hölder smoothness, but its exponent and scale are not supplied to the algorithm, so adaptation must rely on observed model behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta\) and every certified upper bound on \(L_{p,\beta}\) are unavailable as inputs to \(\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: Algorithm operating without the smoothness parameters.
Existing but unknown Hölder exponent and constant.

review_flags: universal-regularization source defining the information model is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the unknown-smoothness leaf, but the precise information model and the assertion that universal guarantees must use observable agreement or adaptive regularization are substantive method-dependent claims without evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix \(p\in\mathbb N_0\), an open convex set \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and parameter sets \(\mathcal B\subseteq(0,1]\) and \(\mathcal L\subseteq(0,infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive deterministic regime in which the objective has some Hölder smoothness but its exponent and scale are unavailable to the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unknown-smoothness problem class is the union \[\mathcal F_{p,mathrm{unk}}(U):=\bigcup_{beta\in\mathcal B,\,L\in\mathcal L}\mathcal F_{p,beta}(L;U).\] An algorithm \(A\) operates in the unknown-smoothness regime when its initialization, query rule, acceptance tests, updates, and stopping rule do not take the realized pair \((\beta,L)\) as input. The pair may enter only the resulting guarantee: for every \(f\in\mathcal F_{p,beta}(L;U)\), \[C_A(varepsilon;f)\le B(varepsilon,p,beta,L,\text{declared data}).\] If the achieved dependence on \(\varepsilon\) matches the rate available when \((beta,L)\) is known, up to declared constants or logarithmic factors, the algorithm is called universal over the parameter family. Unknown smoothness concerns missing parameter information, not absence of a smoothness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unknown-smoothness class is a union of Hölder classes indexed by an exponent and constant. An algorithm belongs to this regime when it is not given the realized exponent or constant and does not use them in its rules. Its complexity guarantee may nevertheless depend on the actual parameters of the instance. Universality is the additional property of matching, up to stated losses, the tolerance rate attainable with known parameters.
assumptions_latex: Every admitted objective belongs to at least one declared Hölder class.
The derivative order \(p\), oracle interface, and admissible parameter sets are known.
The algorithm's source code and parameter initialization are independent of the realized \((\beta,L)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is smoothness-parameter-free while satisfying a parameter-dependent bound for every \(f\in\mathcal F_{p,mathrm{unk}}(U)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Parameter independence means that two instances producing identical oracle transcripts induce identical algorithmic decisions even if their valid Hölder labels differ.
special_cases_latex: Unknown \(L\) with known \(\beta=1\) is an unknown Lipschitz-scale regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: A backtracking estimate may adapt to observed model errors without treating the true \(L\) as an input.
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself guarantee a universal rate.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Model Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic scale-aware accuracy requirements for inexact function and Taylor-model values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), let \(T_{f,p}(x_k,s)\) be the exact order-\(p\) Taylor polynomial and let \(\widetilde T_{k,p}(s)\) and \(\widetilde f_k^+\) approximate \(T_{f,p}(x_k,s)\) and \(f(x_k+s)\), respectively. An approximate-model regime at trial step \(s_k\) requires computable bounds \[|\widetilde T_{k,p}(0)-T_{f,p}(x_k,0)|+|\widetilde T_{k,p}(s_k)-T_{f,p}(x_k,s_k)|\le\omega_k\Delta m_k\] and \[|\widetilde f_k^+-f(x_k+s_k)|+|\widetilde f_k-f(x_k)|\le\omega_k\Delta m_k,\] where \(\Delta m_k>0\) is predicted decrease and \(0\le\omega_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate function and model values are accurate relative to the predicted decrease, preventing deterministic errors from overwhelming the acceptance calculation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined model and function-value errors are each at most \(\omega_k\Delta m_k\).

notation.meaning: Positive predicted model decrease at iteration k.

review_flags: exact inexact-evaluation framework and constants vary across regularization methods
authoritative source required before fixing this relative-error convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-error regime is method-dependent and unsupported by a source fixing these particular sums and constants. In addition, \(\widetilde f_k\) appears in the second bound but is not introduced, while only \(\widetilde f_k^+\) is defined.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f"):U\to\mathbb R\) be \(p\)-times differentiable, let \(\widetilde f(x)\) and \(\widetilde D^jf(x)\) be deterministic approximations, and define \(\widetilde T_p(x,s)=\widetilde f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\widetilde D^jf(x)[s]^j/j!\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic, step-dependent inexact function and derivative models; stochastic confidence events are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible set of trial pairs \(\mathcal S\subseteq U\times\mathbb R^n\), the approximate Taylor models have aggregate order-\(r\) accuracy with constant \(\kappa_{mathrm{mod}}\) when \[|f(x+s)-\widetilde T_p(x,s)|\le\kappa_{mathrm{mod}}\|s\|^r\qquad\text{for every }(x,s)\in\mathcal S.\] A derivative-wise accuracy specification additionally fixes tolerances \(\omega_j(x,s)\ge0\) satisfying \[\|\widetilde D^jf(x)-D^jf(x)\|_{mathrm{op}}\le\omega_j(x,s),\qquad j=0,ldots,p,\] where \(D^0f=f\). The model is dynamically accurate when the algorithm chooses the \(\omega_j(x,s)\) during execution and verifies their declared bounds before using the model. Function-value errors at both \(x\) and \(x+s\) must be charged separately if they enter an actual-versus-predicted reduction test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate model replaces the exact function and derivatives in a Taylor polynomial by deterministic approximations. Aggregate accuracy bounds the discrepancy between the true objective at a trial point and the approximate model by a prescribed power of the step norm. A stronger derivative-wise specification bounds every approximate derivative in operator norm. Dynamic accuracy allows the tolerances to vary by iteration, provided the declared bounds are verified before the model is used.
assumptions_latex: All approximate derivatives have the same multilinear type as their exact counterparts.
The admissible trial-pair set \(\mathcal S\), norm, exponent \(r\), and constants are fixed or generated by a declared rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(x+s)-\widetilde T_p(x,s)|\le\kappa_{mathrm{mod}}\|s\|^r\) on \(\mathcal S\), with optional derivative-wise bounds \(\|\widetilde D^jf-D^jf\|_{mathrm{op}}\le\omega_j\).
special_cases_latex: Exact models have \(\omega_j=0\) for all \(j\).
Fixed absolute accuracy has iteration-independent \(\omega_j\); dynamic relative accuracy makes \(\omega_j\) depend on the current step or predicted decrease.
immediate_consequences_latex: Aggregate accuracy alone need not identify which derivative approximation caused the error.
boundary_notes: Biased or random estimators require probabilistic accuracy conditions.
The exact admissible exponent and tolerance schedule depend on the algorithm and require a dedicated source.

children.title: Complexity Proof Architecture
children.top_down_role: Organizes the reusable certificate and iteration-counting mechanisms behind trust-region and regularization results.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an iterative method generate \(x_k\), a model \(m_k\), a trial step \(s_k\), an acceptance indicator \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\), and a globalization parameter \(\sigma_k>0\) or radius \(\Delta_k>0\). Let \(\Psi(x)\) be the termination measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic architecture common to trust-region and regularization evaluation-complexity analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate-and-counting complexity architecture for tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is a collection of uniform constants and four asserted relations valid before termination: (i) a model certificate \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge\underline P_k(Psi(x_k),sigma_k,Delta_k)\); (ii) successful-step transfer \[a_k=1\Longrightarrow f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\eta\,[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)]\] for some \(\eta>0\); (iii) a parameter bound that yields \(\underline P_k\ge c_varepsilon>0\) whenever \(\Psi(x_k)>varepsilon\) and \(a_k=1\); and (iv) an iteration-accounting inequality \[|\mathcal U_K|le c_0+c_1|\mathcal S_K|,\] where \(\mathcal S_K=\{k<K:a_k=1\}\) and \(\mathcal U_K=\{k<K:a_k=0\}\). The architecture is complete only after a lower bound \(f_{mathrm{low}}\le f(x_k)\) and the evaluation charge per iteration are declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The architecture consists of a model-decrease certificate, a rule transferring predicted decrease to objective decrease on accepted iterations, a globalization-parameter bound giving uniform progress before termination, and an inequality controlling rejected iterations by accepted ones. A lower objective bound and per-iteration evaluation charges complete the accounting framework. This definition lists the formal interfaces only and asserts no complexity rate by itself.
assumptions_latex: All constants are independent of \(k\) and of the requested tolerance except where explicitly indexed by \(\varepsilon\).
The accepted and rejected iteration sets partition all iterations before termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture is the conjunction of the model certificate, successful-step transfer, uniform pretermination progress, and unsuccessful-to-successful counting relation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accounting relation may be written \(K=|\mathcal S_K|+|\mathcal U_K|le c_0+(1+c_1)|\mathcal S_K|\).
special_cases_latex: For trust-region methods, \(\Delta_k\) is the controlled parameter; for regularization methods, it is commonly \(\sigma_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Evaluation accounting can be attached once the maximum oracle charge of each iteration type is fixed.
boundary_notes: This record defines an analysis interface and does not supply a derivation or a rate.
No inspected source presented the entire architecture as one formal definition.

notation.meaning: Successful and unsuccessful iterations before K.
Certified lower bound on predicted model decrease.

children.title: Model-Decrease Certificates
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between auxiliary-model quality and outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Decrease Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable predicted-decrease bound that converts model quality into accepted objective progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a trial model, let \(s_k\) be a computed step, and let \(B_k>0\) be a computable criticality benchmark. A model-decrease certificate consists of constants \(\kappa_{\mathrm{md}}>0\) and the verifiable inequality \[\Delta m_k:=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{md}}B_k>0.\] If the model-agreement ratio \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k))/\Delta m_k\) satisfies \(\rho_k\ge\eta>0\), then the accepted step certifiably yields \[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\ge\eta\kappa_{\mathrm{md}}B_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient predicted decrease, combined with an accepted agreement ratio, certifies a proportional decrease in the true objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\ge\eta\kappa_{\mathrm{md}}B_k\).

notation.meaning: Predicted decrease of the trial model.
Computable benchmark tied to criticality or step size.
Ratio of actual to predicted decrease.

review_flags: generic certificate is algebraically valid but needs a regularization-complexity source fixing the benchmark

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic implication is correct and the certificate content kind matches the leaf, but the generic benchmark B_k is not tied to a defined regularization criticality or step measure. A regularization-complexity source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k(s)=f_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks\), where \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, and let the trust region be \(\|s\|le\Delta_k\) with \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order quadratic trust-region certificate based on a fixed fraction of the Cauchy decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k^{\mathrm C}\) minimize \(m_k(-tg_k)\) over \(t\ge0\) subject to \(\|tg_k\|le\Delta_k\), with \(s_k^{\mathrm C}=0\) when \(g_k=0\). For a fixed \(\thetain(0,1]\), a feasible trial step \(s_k\) has a fraction-of-Cauchy model-decrease certificate when \[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge\theta\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k^{\mathrm C})\bigr).\] The associated quantitative certificate is \[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge\frac{\theta}{2}\|g_k\|min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|g_k\|}{\|B_k\|}\right\},\] using the convention that the second argument is \(+infty\) when \(B_k=0\). The constant \(\theta\) must be independent of \(k\); feasibility and the displayed inequality are the complete certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic trust-region model, the Cauchy step minimizes the model along the negative-gradient ray within the trust region. A feasible trial step is certified when its predicted decrease is at least a fixed fraction \(\theta\) of the Cauchy decrease. This implies the stated lower bound in terms of gradient norm, trust-region radius, and model-Hessian norm. The fraction must be uniform across iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge\theta[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k^{\mathrm C})]\ge(\theta/2)\|g_k\|min\{\Delta_k,\|g_k\|/\|B_k\|\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first displayed inequality is the relative certificate; the second is its gradient-radius-curvature form.
special_cases_latex: An exact trust-region subproblem minimizer satisfies the relative certificate with \(\theta=1\).
The Cauchy step itself satisfies the quantitative bound with coefficient \(1/2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(g_k\ne0\), the certificate guarantees strictly positive predicted reduction.
boundary_notes: The certificate concerns predicted model decrease, not actual objective decrease.
Other norms require the corresponding dual-norm Cauchy construction and may change constants.

notation.meaning: Cauchy step for the quadratic trust-region model.

children.title: Acceptance-Parameter Control Calculus
children.top_down_role: Agreement tests and bounded globalization-parameter behavior.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an iterative minimization method generate trial steps \(s_k\), positive predicted reductions \(P_k>0\), actual reductions \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\), agreement ratios \(\rho_k=A_k/P_k\), and positive globalization parameters \(\sigma_k\). Fix thresholds \(-\infty<\eta_1<\eta_2<\infty\) and update factors \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional smooth nonconvex methods whose acceptance decision is based on an actual-to-predicted reduction ratio and whose globalization parameter is updated multiplicatively. The parameter convention is regularization-like: larger \(\sigma_k\) means a more conservative trial model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An acceptance-parameter control calculus is the partition \(\mathcal U=\{k:\rho_k<\eta_1\}\), \(\mathcal S=\{k:\rho_k\geq\eta_1\}\), and \(\mathcal V=\{k:\rho_k\geq\eta_2\}\subseteq\mathcal S\), together with the state rules \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&k\in\mathcal S,\\x_k,&k\in\mathcal U,\end{cases}\qquad \sigma_{k+1}\in\begin{cases}(0,\sigma_k],&k\in\mathcal V,\\[\sigma_k,\gamma_+\sigma_k],&k\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal V,\\[\gamma_+\sigma_k,\infty),&k\in\mathcal U.\end{cases}\] A bounded-control instance additionally specifies \(\bar\sigma<\infty\) such that \(0<\sigma_k\leq\bar\sigma\) for every iteration preceding termination. The calculus includes a forcing threshold \(\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\) when \(\sigma_k\geq\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\) implies \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); this implication prevents indefinitely many consecutive rejections once the parameter has entered the forcing regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calculus partitions iterations into unsuccessful, successful, and very successful indices using the ratio of actual to predicted reduction. Successful trials move the iterate, unsuccessful trials leave it unchanged, and the regularization-like control parameter is decreased or retained after very successful trials and increased after rejected trials. A bounded-control instance supplies a finite uniform upper bound and a forcing threshold above which every trial must be accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal S\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) exactly on \(\mathcal S\), and \(\sigma_k\geq\sigma_{\mathrm{acc}}\Rightarrow k\in\mathcal S\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a trust-region radius \(\Delta_k\), the inverse convention \(\sigma_k=\Delta_k^{-1}\) reverses the parameter-update inequalities while preserving the same acceptance partition.
special_cases_latex: With a single acceptance threshold, take \(\eta_2=\eta_1\), so that \(\mathcal V=\mathcal S\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If every unsuccessful update satisfies \(\sigma_{k+1}\geq\gamma_+\sigma_k\) and \(\sigma_k\leq\bar\sigma\), then any consecutive block of unsuccessful iterations beginning at parameter \(\sigma>0\) has length at most \(\left\lceil\log(\bar\sigma/\sigma)/\log\gamma_+\right\rceil\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover probabilistic acceptance tests, nonmonotone reference values, or parameters without a fixed monotonic relation to model conservatism.
No inspected source in the supplied source set established this exact regularization-parameter convention and forcing-threshold formulation.

notation.meaning: Predicted reduction, actual reduction, and their agreement ratio.

children.title: Model-Agreement Tests
children.top_down_role: Coverage of agreement measures used to classify trial iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Agreement Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-to-predicted reduction test for accepting a regularization trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), a model \(m_k\), and a trial step \(s_k\) with \(\Delta m_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\) and form \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{\Delta m_k}.\] For a fixed threshold \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\), accept the trial by setting \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\); otherwise reject it and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). The test outputs the agreement ratio, the acceptance decision, and the resulting next iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute actual reduction divided by predicted reduction, accept the step when this ratio reaches the threshold, and otherwise retain the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The actual-to-predicted reduction procedure is coherent and correctly classified as an algorithm, but no source supports this exact acceptance convention or its placement within the intended regularization framework.

children.title: Acceptance Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage of threshold choices governing successful, marginal, or rejected trials.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance Threshold Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-threshold classification of unsuccessful, successful, and highly successful trial iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose fixed thresholds \(0<\eta_1\le\eta_2<1\) and compute the agreement ratio \(\rho_k\). The iteration is unsuccessful when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), successful when \(\eta_1\le\rho_k<\eta_2\), and highly successful when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\). Only successful or highly successful trials update the iterate to \(x_k+s_k\). This partition is exhaustive and disjoint, and it permits separate globalization-parameter updates in the three regimes without changing the acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two ordered ratio thresholds partition trials into unsuccessful, successful, and highly successful regimes; the latter two accept the trial step.
assumptions_latex: The agreement ratio \(\rho_k\) is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), \(\eta_1\le\rho_k<\eta_2\), and \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\) define a disjoint exhaustive classification.

notation.meaning: Minimum ratio for highly successful classification.

review_flags: authoritative regularization-method source for the threshold convention required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval classification is mathematically exhaustive and disjoint and the condition content kind fits the leaf. However, the terminology and allowance of eta_1=eta_2, which makes the middle regime empty, require an authoritative regularization-method source with a precise locator.

children.title: Globalization Parameter Control
children.top_down_role: Coverage of adaptive regularization or neighborhood parameters used by complexity analyses.

knowledge_statements.title: Globalization Parameter Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform upper control of a multiplicatively updated regularization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\sigma_k>0\) be updated with constants \(\gamma_+>1\) and \(0<\gamma_-\leq 1\). On a rejected iteration set \(\sigma_{k+1}\leq\gamma_+\sigma_k\), and on an accepted iteration set \(\sigma_{k+1}\leq\sigma_k\). If every trial with \(\sigma_k\geq\bar\sigma\) is accepted, then
\[\sigma_k\leq \sigma_{\max}:=\max\{\sigma_0,\gamma_+\bar\sigma\}\quad\text{for every }k.\]
Thus the globalization mechanism cannot increase the regularization parameter without bound once sufficiently large parameters guarantee model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sufficiently large regularization forces acceptance, multiplicative rejection updates keep every regularization parameter below a uniform explicit bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k\sigma_k\leq\max\{\sigma_0,\gamma_+\bar\sigma\}\).

notation.meaning: globalization or regularization parameter at iteration k
threshold above which acceptance is guaranteed

review_flags: Exact update convention and authoritative complexity reference remain to be matched.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundedness statement is mathematically coherent and fits Globalization Parameter Control, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the threshold-acceptance and update conventions. Those conventions vary across regularization methods, so an authoritative source is required.

children.title: Bounded-Control Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage of parameter ranges supporting uniform iteration accounting.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Control Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient regime for bounded acceptance-control parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A globalization sequence \((\sigma_k)_{k\geq 0}\) is in a bounded-control regime if there exist finite constants \(0<\sigma_{\min}\leq\sigma_{\max}<\infty\) such that
\[\sigma_{\min}\leq\sigma_k\leq\sigma_{\max}\quad\text{for every }k.\]
A sufficient condition is that rejected trials satisfy \(\sigma_{k+1}\leq\gamma_+\sigma_k\) for some \(\gamma_+>1\), accepted trials satisfy \(\sigma_{k+1}\leq\sigma_k\), every trial with \(\sigma_k\geq\bar\sigma\) is accepted, and the updates enforce \(\sigma_k\geq\sigma_{\min}>0\). Under these conditions one may take
\[\sigma_{\max}=\max\{\sigma_0,\gamma_+\bar\sigma\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Control is bounded when the parameter remains between positive finite constants. A positive floor, threshold acceptance, nonincreasing accepted updates, and capped multiplicative rejected updates provide a sufficient regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_k\in[\sigma_{\min},\max\{\sigma_0,\gamma_+\bar\sigma\}]\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: globalization or regularization parameter at iteration k
uniform positive lower bound and finite upper bound
threshold at or above which acceptance is guaranteed
upper multiplicative growth factor for a rejected update
