children.title: Successful-Iteration Accounting
children.top_down_role: Conversion of certified progress into successful-iteration counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Successful-Iteration Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Telescoping decrease converts certified accepted-step progress into a count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x_k)\geq f_{\inf}\), and let \(\mathcal S_\varepsilon\) contain the successful iterations occurring before termination at accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\). If every \(k\in\mathcal S_\varepsilon\) satisfies
\[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\kappa\varepsilon^\alpha\]
for constants \(\kappa>0\) and \(\alpha>0\), while unsuccessful iterations leave the iterate unchanged, then
\[|\mathcal S_\varepsilon|\leq\left\lfloor\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{\kappa\varepsilon^\alpha}\right\rfloor.\]
The bound counts accepted iterations requiring certified objective progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform decrease on every successful pretermination step bounds their number by the initial objective gap divided by the certified decrease.
assumptions_latex: Each successful pretermination iteration decreases \(f\) by at least \(\kappa\varepsilon^\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal S_\varepsilon|\leq\lfloor(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/(\kappa\varepsilon^\alpha)\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: successful iterations before the accuracy test is met
lower bound on attained objective values

review_flags: Standard telescoping result, but no supplied locator supports this complexity statement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping complexity bound is precise, mathematically standard, and appropriate for Successful-Iteration Accounting. No source or locator is supplied, however, so the nontrivial complexity statement cannot remain candidate-review knowledge without evidence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below by \(f_{\mathrm{low}}\). Let \(\chi(x)\geq0\) be a criticality measure, fix \(\epsilon>0\), and let \(T_\epsilon=\inf\{k\geq0:\chi(x_k)\leq\epsilon\}\). Let \(\mathcal S=\{k:x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\}\) be the accepted-iteration set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic monotone smooth nonconvex algorithms for which accepted iterations have a uniform objective-decrease certificate before the requested criticality tolerance is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successful-iteration accounting certificate at tolerance \(\epsilon\) is a number \(\delta(\epsilon)>0\) satisfying \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\delta(\epsilon)\qquad\text{for every }k\in\mathcal S\text{ with }k<T_\epsilon.\] Its associated accounting functional is \[N_{\mathcal S}(\epsilon;f_0,f_{\mathrm{low}},\delta)=\left\lfloor\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\mathrm{low}}}{\delta(\epsilon)}\right\rfloor+1.\] The certificate asserts that the number of accepted iterations strictly before termination obeys \[|\mathcal S\cap\{0,\ldots,T_\epsilon-1\}|\leq N_{\mathcal S}(\epsilon;f_0,f_{\mathrm{low}},\delta).\] For a family \(\delta(\epsilon)=c\epsilon^p\) with \(c>0\), the accounting order is \(p\), and the successful-iteration count is \(O(\epsilon^{-p})\) with constants independent of \(\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A successful-iteration accounting certificate is a positive lower bound on the objective decrease achieved by every accepted iteration before the target tolerance is reached. The associated accounting functional divides the available objective-value gap by that certified decrease. It bounds the number of successful iterations, and a certificate proportional to the p-th power of the tolerance produces a successful-iteration order of p.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{succ}}(\epsilon):=|\mathcal S\cap\{0,\ldots,T_\epsilon-1\}|\leq\left\lfloor(f(x_0)-f_{\mathrm{low}})/\delta(\epsilon)\right\rfloor+1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The definition can use a level-set lower bound \(f_{\mathrm{low}}\leq\inf\{f(x_k):k<T_\epsilon\}\) instead of a global lower bound on \(f\).
special_cases_latex: If \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq c\epsilon^{(p+1)/p}\), then \(N_{\mathrm{succ}}(\epsilon)=O(\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p})\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any sharper lower bound on \(\delta(\epsilon)\) immediately sharpens the successful-iteration count without changing unsuccessful-iteration accounting.
boundary_notes: The definition does not count rejected trials or oracle calls made within a successful iteration.
Nonmonotone methods require replacing the objective gap by an appropriate decreasing reference or potential function.
No inspected source supplied the exact abstract accounting functional stated here.

children.title: Unsuccessful-Iteration Accounting
children.top_down_role: Control of rejected iterations and total evaluation counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsuccessful-Iteration Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative parameter updates control rejection overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\sigma_k\leq\sigma_{\max}\). Each unsuccessful iteration multiplies \(\sigma_k\) by at least \(\gamma_+>1\), while each successful iteration can reduce it by no more than a factor \(\gamma_-\in(0,1]\). For any prefix containing \(U\) unsuccessful and \(S\) successful iterations,
\[U\leq \frac{\log(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_0)+S\log(1/\gamma_-)}{\log\gamma_+}.\]
Consequently, after applying integer rounding, the total iteration or evaluation count is at most an affine function of the successful-iteration count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded multiplicatively updated parameter makes the number of rejected trials at most affine in the number of accepted trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\leq[\log(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_0)+S\log(1/\gamma_-)]/\log\gamma_+\).

notation.meaning: numbers of unsuccessful and successful iterations in a prefix

review_flags: Update inequalities vary across regularization frameworks; an exact source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic accounting formula follows from the displayed multiplicative inequalities and fits Unsuccessful-Iteration Accounting. Because regularization frameworks use materially different successful and unsuccessful update intervals, a source specifying these exact inequalities and the associated evaluation accounting is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(T\in\mathbb N\), let \(\mathcal S_T\) and \(\mathcal U_T\) partition \(\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\), and let \(\sigma_k>0\) be a regularization-like control parameter. Suppose \(\sigma_k\leq\bar\sigma\), an unsuccessful iteration satisfies \(\sigma_{k+1}\geq\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\sigma_k\) with \(\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}>1\), and a successful iteration satisfies \(\sigma_{k+1}\geq\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\sigma_k\) with \(0<\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic multiplicative parameter updates with a positive initial parameter and a finite uniform parameter bound. The definition counts outer iterations; evaluation counts require a separate per-iteration oracle-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unsuccessful-iteration accounting constant is \[c_{\mathrm{us}}:=\frac{|\log\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}|}{\log\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}},\qquad b_{\mathrm{us}}:=\frac{\log(\bar\sigma/\sigma_0)}{\log\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}}.\] An iteration sequence is unsuccessfully accountable when every prefix ending at \(T\) satisfies \[|\mathcal U_T|\leq c_{\mathrm{us}}|\mathcal S_T|+b_{\mathrm{us}}.\] The corresponding total-iteration functional is \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}(N_{\mathrm{succ}}):=(1+c_{\mathrm{us}})N_{\mathrm{succ}}+b_{\mathrm{us}}.\] If iteration \(k\) uses at most \(q_{\mathcal S}\) counted oracle calls when successful and at most \(q_{\mathcal U}\) when unsuccessful, its evaluation-accounting functional is \[N_{\mathrm{eval}}:=q_{\mathcal S}|\mathcal S_T|+q_{\mathcal U}|\mathcal U_T|.\] Thus unsuccessful accounting converts a successful-iteration bound into a total-iteration or evaluation bound while preserving its tolerance exponent whenever all accounting constants are independent of the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsuccessful-iteration accounting bounds rejected trials by an affine function of accepted trials. Its constants are determined by the multiplicative increase after rejection, the possible decrease after acceptance, and the uniform parameter range. Adding this rejection count to a successful-iteration bound gives a total-iteration bound; weighting each class by its oracle cost gives an evaluation bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal U_T|\leq c_{\mathrm{us}}|\mathcal S_T|+b_{\mathrm{us}}\) and \(T\leq(1+c_{\mathrm{us}})|\mathcal S_T|+b_{\mathrm{us}}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a trust-region radius \(\Delta_k\), the same definition applies to \(\sigma_k=\Delta_k^{-1}\) when accepted and rejected radius updates admit uniform multiplicative bounds.
special_cases_latex: If successful iterations never decrease \(\sigma_k\), then \(\gamma_{\mathrm{dec}}=1\), \(c_{\mathrm{us}}=0\), and the rejection count is bounded by the fixed startup term \(b_{\mathrm{us}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(|\mathcal S_T|=O(\epsilon^{-p})\) and the update constants do not depend on \(\epsilon\), then \(T=O(\epsilon^{-p})\).
boundary_notes: The affine count can fail without a uniform parameter bound or a guaranteed multiplicative change on rejection.
Inner subproblem iterations and repeated accuracy refinements are excluded unless included in \(q_{\mathcal S}\) and \(q_{\mathcal U}\).

children.title: Complexity Bound Sharpness Theory
children.top_down_role: Compares constructive guarantees with information barriers and realized worst cases.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Worst-Case Evaluation Complexity and Optimality of Second-Order Methods for Nonconvex Smooth Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: upper bounds, lower bounds, and optimality of second-order method classes

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of a Worst-Case Complexity Bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak F\) be a class of problem instances, \(\mathfrak A\) a class of admissible algorithms under a fixed oracle and cost model, and \(T(A,f,\epsilon)\) the counted cost for algorithm \(A\) on instance \(f\) to attain a specified \(\epsilon\)-criticality target. Let \(r(\epsilon)>0\) diverge as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic deterministic worst-case complexity in a fixed problem class, oracle model, target definition, and unit-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An upper bound of order \(r\) for an algorithm \(A\in\mathfrak A\) is sharp on \(\mathfrak F\) when there exist constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) and \(\epsilon_0>0\) such that \[\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}T(A,f,\epsilon)\leq C r(\epsilon)\qquad(0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0),\] and either of the following matching conditions holds. Algorithmic sharpness requires a family \(f_\epsilon\in\mathfrak F\) with \[T(A,f_\epsilon,\epsilon)\geq c r(\epsilon).\] Oracle-class sharpness requires \[\inf_{B\in\mathfrak A}\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}T(B,f,\epsilon)\geq c r(\epsilon).\] The first condition realizes the worst-case order for the particular method; the second identifies the order as an information barrier for the entire algorithm class. A bound is exponent-sharp when these relations hold up to logarithmic or tolerance-independent factors rather than matching constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complexity upper bound is sharp only relative to fixed problems, algorithms, information, target, and cost. It is algorithmically sharp if instances force the given method to spend the same asymptotic order as its upper bound. It is oracle-class sharp if no admissible method can improve that order. Exponent sharpness permits logarithmic or constant-factor discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}T(A,f,\epsilon)=\Theta(r(\epsilon))\) for algorithmic sharpness, while \(\inf_{B\in\mathfrak A}\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}T(B,f,\epsilon)=\Theta(r(\epsilon))\) for oracle-class sharpness.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a power law \(r(\epsilon)=\epsilon^{-p}\), exponent sharpness means that the constructive and obstructive complexity exponents both equal \(p\).
special_cases_latex: A realized worst-case trajectory establishes algorithmic sharpness but does not by itself establish an oracle lower bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two bounds cannot be declared matching unless their admissible algorithms, target criterion, smoothness class, dimension convention, and counted operations agree.
boundary_notes: The definition distinguishes method-specific bad examples from minimax information lower bounds.
Dimension-dependent and randomized bounds require additional quantifiers not included in this deterministic formulation.
No inspected source supplied this exact two-level sharpness definition.

notation.meaning: Counted cost to meet the prescribed tolerance.
Fixed problem and admissible algorithm classes.

review_flags: An authoritative source is needed for the exact distinction between algorithmic and oracle-class sharpness.

children.title: Constructive Upper-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Method-dependent guarantees indexed by oracle and target order.

knowledge_statements.title: Constructive Upper-Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation upper bounds for adaptive regularization using derivatives through order \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\leq q\leq p\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below, and suppose its \(p\)-th derivative is Lipschitz continuous on the relevant level set. A suitably implemented adaptive regularization method of order \(p\), using derivative information through order \(p\), produces a point satisfying a normalized \(q\)-th-order approximate criticality condition with tolerance \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\) after at most
\[O\!\left(\varepsilon^{-(p+1)/(p-q+1)}\right)\]
successful iterations and, under bounded rejection overhead, the same-order number of objective and derivative evaluations. Constants may depend on smoothness, initial objective gap, and algorithmic parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-p adaptive regularization attains qth-order approximate criticality in order epsilon to the negative (p+1)/(p-q+1) evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the generated level set.
\(\nabla^p f\) is Lipschitz continuous on that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_\varepsilon=O(\varepsilon^{-(p+1)/(p-q+1)})\) evaluations.

notation.meaning: evaluations required to meet tolerance epsilon

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q\in\mathbb N\) index an oracle revealing derivatives through order \(q\), let \(j\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\) index a criticality target, and let \(\mathfrak F_{q,\nu}(L,\Delta f)\) be a specified class of smooth nonconvex objectives with derivative regularity exponent \(\nu\), regularity constant \(L\), and initial objective gap at most \(\Delta f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-dependent deterministic worst-case guarantees indexed by oracle order, target order, smoothness regime, and counted cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constructive upper-bound family is a collection \[\mathscr U=\{(A_{q,j},\,\mathcal O_q,\,\chi_j,\,C_{q,j},\,r_{q,j}):q\in Q,\ j\in J_q\}\] such that each explicitly specified algorithm \(A_{q,j}\), using oracle \(\mathcal O_q\), satisfies \[\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F_{q,\nu}(L,\Delta f)}T_{\mathcal O_q}(A_{q,j},f,\epsilon)\leq C_{q,j}(L,\Delta f,\text{algorithm parameters})\,r_{q,j}(\epsilon)\] for every \(0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0\), and terminates at an iterate \(x\) with \(\chi_j(x)\leq\epsilon\). Constructive means that the record identifies the method, its admissible parameter rules, its oracle calls, and its stopping criterion; a bare existence assertion is not a member of the family. Uniformity means that \(C_{q,j}\) and \(\epsilon_0\) do not depend on the particular \(f\) or on \(\epsilon\) within the declared class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constructive upper-bound family is an indexed collection of actual algorithms and their worst-case guarantees. Every member fixes the derivative oracle, target order, problem regularity, stopping test, cost, and tolerance rate. Its constant must be uniform over the declared objective class and independent of the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathcal O_q}(A_{q,j},f,\epsilon)\leq C_{q,j}r_{q,j}(\epsilon)\) uniformly for \(f\in\mathfrak F_{q,\nu}(L,\Delta f)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family may be represented as a table only when each row preserves all indices and quantifiers in the displayed uniform bound.
special_cases_latex: For first-order stationarity, \(j=1\) and one may take \(\chi_1(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Lower-Bound Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case barriers for deterministic algorithms using derivatives through order \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For each derivative order \(q\), let \(\mathcal O_q(f,x)=(f(x),\nabla f(x),\ldots,\nabla^q f(x))\), let \(\mathfrak A_q\) be a declared class of deterministic algorithms whose next query is a function of prior oracle answers, and let \(\mathfrak F_q\) be a fixed smooth nonconvex problem class. Let \(\chi\) be the target criticality measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic black-box derivative-oracle complexity. Dimension may depend on the query budget and must be quantified as part of the lower-bound family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An oracle lower-bound family of rate \(r_q(\epsilon)\) is a collection of constants \(c_q>0\), tolerances \(\epsilon_q>0\), and adversarial instances such that \[\inf_{A\in\mathfrak A_q}\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F_q}T_{\mathcal O_q}(A,f,\epsilon)\geq c_q r_q(\epsilon)\qquad(0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_q).\] Equivalently, for every \(A\in\mathfrak A_q\) and every sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), there exists an instance \(f_{A,\epsilon}\in\mathfrak F_q\), in an admissible dimension \(n_{A,\epsilon}\), such that after every \(t<c_qr_q(\epsilon)\) oracle queries the algorithm's output \(x_t\) satisfies \(\chi(x_t)>\epsilon\). The family is order-indexed when the same statement is supplied separately for several \(q\), with the information revealed by \(\mathcal O_q\), the smoothness class, and the dimension rule recorded for each index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle lower-bound family says that every admissible derivative-limited algorithm has a hard smooth nonconvex instance requiring at least the stated number of oracle queries before reaching the target. The algorithm is universally quantified before the adversarial instance. Every derivative order has its own oracle, function class, dimension rule, and rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{A\in\mathfrak A_q}\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F_q}T_{\mathcal O_q}(A,f,\epsilon)=\Omega(r_q(\epsilon))\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The minimax inequality is equivalent to the adversarial quantifier order \(\forall A\,\forall\epsilon\,\exists f_{A,\epsilon}\) with the stated pretermination failure condition.
special_cases_latex: A first-order lower bound uses \(q=1\), \(\mathcal O_1(f,x)=(f(x),\nabla f(x))\), and commonly \(\chi(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).

children.title: Sharpness Constructions

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matched lower-bound constructions that realize the asymptotic exponent of an upper complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an objective class \(\mathcal F\), an oracle model \(\mathcal O\), a target measure \(\chi\), and a cost convention. For a specified method \(A\), a method-specific sharpness construction for exponent \(r>0\) is a family \(\{(f_\varepsilon,x_{0,\varepsilon})\}_{\varepsilon>0}\subseteq\mathcal F\) and a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(\varepsilon\), such that
\[T_A(f_\varepsilon,x_{0,\varepsilon};\varepsilon)\geq c\varepsilon^{-r}\]
before \(A\) produces a point \(x\) satisfying \(\chi(x)\leq\varepsilon\). If the lower bound instead holds for every admissible method using \(\mathcal O\), it is an oracle-class sharpness construction. When the corresponding method-specific or oracle-class upper bound is \(O(\varepsilon^{-r})\) under the same objective class, oracle, target, and cost convention, the matched complexity is \(\Theta(\varepsilon^{-r})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sharpness construction supplies hard instances giving a matching lower bound for either one specified method or every method in a specified oracle class. A theta conclusion is valid only when the matching upper bound concerns the same method or oracle-class complexity under identical conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\), \(\mathcal O\), \(\chi\), and the cost convention are fixed.
Any matched upper bound uses the same objective class, oracle model, target measure, cost unit, and method-level or oracle-class quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matched lower and upper bound yields \(T_\varepsilon=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-r})\) for the same method-specific or oracle-class complexity function.

notation.meaning: objective class used by the construction
cost incurred by method A from x_0 on f before reaching tolerance epsilon

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix an algorithm \(A\), a function class \(\mathfrak F\), a criticality measure \(\chi\), and an upper-complexity rate \(r(\epsilon)\). For an instance \(f\), write \(x_k(A,f)\) for the generated iterates and \(T(A,f,\epsilon)=\inf\{k:\chi(x_k(A,f))\leq\epsilon\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic method-specific sharpness constructions for smooth nonconvex objectives. The construction may be a tolerance-indexed family rather than one fixed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sharpness construction realizing rate \(r\) for \(A\) is a family \(\{(n_\epsilon,f_\epsilon,x_{0,\epsilon})\}_{0<\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0}\) such that \(f_\epsilon:\mathbb R^{n_\epsilon}\to\mathbb R\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F\) with all defining class constants uniformly bounded in \(\epsilon\), the algorithm is well defined from \(x_{0,\epsilon}\), and there exists \(c>0\), independent of \(\epsilon\), for which \[\chi(x_k(A,f_\epsilon))>\epsilon\qquad\text{for every }0\leq k<c r(\epsilon).\] Equivalently, \[T(A,f_\epsilon,\epsilon)\geq c r(\epsilon).\] A trajectory-interpolation construction additionally prescribes compatible values of \(f_\epsilon\) and its required derivatives at the iterates and produces a globally defined objective in \(\mathfrak F\) attaining those data. Uniform class membership is essential: allowing smoothness constants or the initial objective gap to diverge with \(\epsilon\) does not realize the claimed normalized worst-case rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sharpness construction is a uniform family of smooth objectives and starting points on which a fixed algorithm fails the target for at least the claimed asymptotic number of iterations. The objectives must retain the same regularity and gap bounds as the upper-bound class. A trajectory-interpolation construction realizes prescribed oracle data along the algorithm's path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(A,f_\epsilon,\epsilon)=\Omega(r(\epsilon))\) with constants and problem-class parameters uniform in \(\epsilon\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The pretermination inequality \(\chi(x_k)>\epsilon\) for all \(k<cr(\epsilon)\) is equivalent to the hitting-time lower bound.
special_cases_latex: If one fixed objective and starting point realize the inequality along a sequence \(\epsilon_\ell\downarrow0\), they define a sequential sharpness construction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with a uniform \(O(r(\epsilon))\) upper bound for the same method and class, the construction establishes \(\Theta(r(\epsilon))\) method-specific complexity.
boundary_notes: Method-specific sharpness does not imply a minimax oracle lower bound.
The admissible dimension dependence must be reported when \(n_\epsilon\) grows as \(\epsilon\) decreases.

children.title: Complexity Comparison Validity Boundaries

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent a complexity claim by a signature \(\Sigma=(\mathfrak F,\mathfrak A,\mathcal O,\chi,\mathcal C,\mathcal Q)\), where \(\mathfrak F\) is the problem class, \(\mathfrak A\) the algorithm class, \(\mathcal O\) the information oracle, \(\chi\) the target, \(\mathcal C\) the counted cost, and \(\mathcal Q\) the quantifier convention, including dimension and probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparisons of deterministic or randomized upper and lower complexity statements. Direct order comparisons require identical signatures or an explicit reduction between them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two complexity claims with signatures \(\Sigma_1\) and \(\Sigma_2\) are directly comparable when their problem classes, admissible algorithms, information returned per query, criticality targets, cost units, and quantifier conventions coincide up to tolerance-independent equivalence. They are reducibly comparable when there exist maps between instances, algorithms, targets, and costs such that \[\chi_2(R_xx)\leq a\,\chi_1(x),\qquad T_2(R_AA,R_ff,a\epsilon)\leq b\,T_1(A,f,\epsilon)+d,\] with constants \(a,b>0\) and \(d\geq0\) independent of \(\epsilon\). The validity boundary of a comparison is the set of signature components for which equality or such a reduction has been established. Outside that boundary, an inequality between displayed tolerance exponents is not, by itself, a mathematical ordering of the two complexity results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid complexity comparison fixes the objective class, admissible algorithms, oracle information, target, cost unit, and quantifiers. Claims with identical signatures can be compared directly. Claims with different signatures can be compared only through an explicit reduction whose distortion is independent of tolerance. Bare exponents from incompatible signatures are not ordered results.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_1\sim\Sigma_2\) only under componentwise equivalence, or \(\Sigma_1\preceq\Sigma_2\) only when a tolerance-uniform reduction controls both target and cost.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Direct comparability is reducible comparability with identity maps and tolerance-independent changes of units.
special_cases_latex: Function-evaluation and derivative-evaluation bounds are directly comparable only when the oracle model assigns an agreed cost to each returned derivative.
Expected and high-probability bounds have different quantifier components and require a probabilistic conversion before comparison.
immediate_consequences_latex: A lower bound for first-order oracles cannot certify sharpness of a second-order method unless a reduction accounts for the additional Hessian information.

Different stationarity measures require explicit norm or measure equivalence constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity comparisons must align fixed- and growing-dimension quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A lower-bound family whose member for horizon \(N\) lies in \(\mathbb R^{n_N}\) with \(n_N\geq N+1\) establishes
\[\forall N\;\exists n_N\;\exists f_N:\quad T(f_N)>N,\]
but it does not establish
\[\exists n\;\forall N\;\exists f_N:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\quad T(f_N)>N.\]
Therefore such a growing-dimension oracle lower bound cannot, without an additional embedding or fixed-dimensional construction, be compared as a fixed-dimension sharpness result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard instance whose dimension grows with the iteration horizon does not by itself prove the same lower bound in any fixed dimension.
assumptions_latex: The adversarial construction may choose dimension after the horizon \(N\) is specified.
No dimension-preserving embedding theorem is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall N\,\exists n_N\,\exists f_N)\) does not imply \((\exists n\,\forall N\,\exists f_N)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Guarantee Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-compatible comparison of randomized complexity guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a randomized algorithm with stopping time \(T_\varepsilon\), an expected guarantee is \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E[T_\varepsilon(f)]\leq N(\varepsilon)\); a high-probability guarantee is \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P(T_\varepsilon(f)>N(\varepsilon,\delta))\leq\delta\); and an almost-sure guarantee requires \(\mathbb P(T_\varepsilon(f)<\infty)=1\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\). Upper and lower bounds are directly comparable only when they use the same randomness source, adversary model, success event, and probability quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected, high-probability, and almost-sure bounds are distinct; comparisons require matching randomness, adversary, event, and quantifier conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(T_\varepsilon\) is measurable with respect to the algorithm's randomness.
All comparisons use the same objective class \(\mathcal F\) and accuracy event.

children.title: Oracle Compatibility

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for transferring complexity bounds between oracle models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O_A\) and \(\mathcal O_B\) be oracle models. A bound measured in \(\mathcal O_A\)-calls transfers to \(\mathcal O_B\) with factor \(c\) only if every admissible \(\mathcal O_A\)-response can be simulated from at most \(c\) calls to \(\mathcal O_B\), uniformly over the objective class, without revealing extra information or changing the success criterion. If simulations exist in both directions with constants independent of dimension and tolerance, the two oracle complexities are equivalent up to constant factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle bounds transfer only through uniform information-preserving simulations; two-way constant-cost simulation gives constant-factor complexity equivalence.
assumptions_latex: Both oracle models act on the same objective class and use the same target event.
Simulation cost is uniform over instances, dimensions, and tolerances.
The simulation preserves the admissible information history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_B\leq cT_A\) under one-way simulation, with constant-factor equivalence under two-way simulation.

children.title: Cross-Oracle Comparison Failures
children.top_down_role: Coverage of misleading comparisons between incompatible computational information models.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Oracle Comparison Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Different oracle targets can classify the same point incompatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(f(x)=x^4/4-x^2/2\). At \(x=0\),
\[f'(0)=0,\qquad f''(0)=-1.\]
Thus \(x=0\) satisfies every first-order stationarity test \(|f'(x)|\leq\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\geq0\), but fails the second-order test \(f''(x)\geq-\varepsilon_H\) whenever \(0\leq\varepsilon_H<1\). Hence a first-order-oracle bound for first-order stationarity cannot be ordered against a second-order-oracle bound for second-order stationarity without reconciling both oracle information and target criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict saddle is perfectly first-order stationary but not second-order stationary, invalidating comparisons that silently change both oracle and target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(x=0\), first-order success holds while second-order success fails for \(\varepsilon_H<1\).
review_flags: Concrete calculation is self-contained, but the cross-oracle comparison principle lacks a supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial calculation is correct, the counterexample kind fits the terminal container, and the example cleanly separates first- and second-order target criteria. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be smooth and bounded below. A trust-region method uses local models \(m_k\), radii \(\Delta_k>0\), feasible trial steps \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), and agreement ratios comparing actual and predicted reduction. Let \(\chi(x)\) be a specified criticality measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional smooth nonconvex trust-region algorithms. Complexity is counted in explicitly declared outer iterations or oracle evaluations, not in arithmetic operations used by the subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region complexity specification is a tuple \[\mathfrak T=(\{m_k\},\{\|\cdot\|_k\},\{\Delta_k\},\mathcal D,\mathcal A,\chi,\mathcal C)\] in which \(\mathcal D\) is a uniform model-decrease certificate, \(\mathcal A\) is an agreement-based acceptance and radius-update rule, and \(\mathcal C\) is a cost convention. For tolerance \(\epsilon>0\), its complexity is the worst-case hitting cost \[N_{\mathfrak T}(\epsilon)=\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}\inf\{\mathcal C(0{:}k):\chi(x_k)\leq\epsilon\}.\] A valid bound \(N_{\mathfrak T}(\epsilon)\leq R(\epsilon)\) must use a model-decrease certificate that is uniform before termination, an acceptance rule that converts predicted decrease into objective decrease, and a radius-control statement that bounds rejected trials. The tuple records whether \(R\) counts successful iterations, all outer iterations, objective evaluations, derivative evaluations, or another declared oracle unit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region complexity is the worst-case counted cost for a model-and-radius method to reach a declared criticality target. Its specification includes the model, radius norm, sufficient-decrease certificate, acceptance and radius rules, stopping measure, and cost convention. A complete bound accounts for both accepted progress and rejected radius adjustments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathfrak T}(\epsilon)=\sup_{f\in\mathfrak F}\inf\{\mathcal C(0{:}k):\chi(x_k)\leq\epsilon\}\), with every component of \(\mathfrak T\) fixed independently of \(\epsilon\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When each outer iteration incurs one new objective evaluation and uniformly many derivative evaluations, outer-iteration and evaluation bounds are equivalent up to fixed factors.
special_cases_latex: For first-order criticality, one may take \(\chi(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
For second-order criticality, a common target records both \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\) and the negative part of \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A successful-iteration bound alone is not a total evaluation bound unless unsuccessful iterations and per-iteration oracle costs are also controlled.
boundary_notes: The supplied classical trust-region sources define the method mechanics but do not state this exact abstract worst-case complexity tuple.
Infinite-dimensional, stochastic, and derivative-free trust-region complexities require additional regimes.

children.title: Trust-Region Complexity Framework

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Trust-Region State and Transition System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable and bounded below. At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k\) model \(f\) near \(x_k\), let \(\|\cdot\|_k\) be a norm, and let \(\Delta_k>0\). Fix \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\) and \(0<\gamma_1\leq\gamma_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical deterministic unconstrained trust-region framework retaining the state variables and transition rules used in convergence and complexity arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trust region is \[\mathcal B_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-x_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}.\] A feasible trial step satisfies \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\) and has positive predicted reduction \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\). Define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)}.\] The state transition is \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k\geq\eta_1,\\x_k,&\rho_k<\eta_1,\end{cases}\] and the radius transition satisfies \[\Delta_{k+1}\in\begin{cases}[\Delta_k,\infty),&\rho_k\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta_k,\Delta_k],&\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta_k,\gamma_2\Delta_k],&\rho_k<\eta_1.\end{cases}\] A complexity-ready instance supplements this transition system with a quantitative model-decrease certificate, a target criticality measure, and a declared evaluation-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The framework forms a local model inside a norm ball, computes a model-reducing feasible trial step, compares actual and predicted reduction, accepts sufficiently accurate trials, and updates the radius according to the agreement class. Complexity analysis adds a quantitative decrease certificate, a stopping measure, and a cost convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\) exactly triggers acceptance, while \(\rho_k<\eta_1\) triggers rejection and contraction by a factor in \([\gamma_1,\gamma_2]\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing the model in step coordinates as \(q_k(s)=m_k(x_k+s)\) gives the equivalent trust-region constraint \(\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: For a quadratic model, \(m_k(x_k+s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), with symmetric \(H_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Successful iterations form \(\mathcal S=\{k:\rho_k\geq\eta_1\}\), very successful iterations form \(\mathcal V=\{k:\rho_k\geq\eta_2\}\), and \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal S\).
boundary_notes: The radius-update intervals intentionally allow multiple implementations.
The definition excludes nonmonotone reference values and inexact agreement ratios.

notation.meaning: Ratio of achieved objective reduction to predicted model reduction.

children.title: Quadratic Model-Radius Coupling
children.top_down_role: The model and neighborhood interface used by complexity arguments.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(H_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(\|\cdot\|_k\) be a norm, and let \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained trust-region methods with possibly indefinite quadratic models and iteration-dependent norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic model-radius pair at \(x_k\) is \[q_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+ rac12s^TH_ks,\qquad \mathcal T_k=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\}.\] The associated trust-region subproblem is \[\min_{s\in\mathcal T_k}q_k(s).\] A trial step is model-decreasing when \(q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)>0\). The pair is uniformly complexity-compatible with a reference norm \(\|\cdot\|\) when constants \(0<\underline
u\leq\overline
u<\infty\), independent of \(k\), satisfy \[\underline
u\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq\overline
u\|s\|\qquad	ext{for every }s\in\mathbb R^n.\] Under this compatibility, the radius controls the physical step by \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k/\underline
u\), while model-decrease certificates expressed in either norm differ only by uniform constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupling consists of a quadratic local model and a radius-constrained neighborhood in which that model is trusted. The Hessian approximation may be indefinite. A complexity-compatible pair requires uniform equivalence between the iteration norm and a fixed reference norm, so the radius and all norm-based decrease certificates remain uniformly comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\in\mathcal T_k\Rightarrow\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), and uniform norm equivalence gives \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k/\underline\nu\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With an invertible scaling matrix \(S_k\), the norm \(\|s\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}s\|_2\) converts the constraint to \(\|w\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) under \(s=S_kw\).
special_cases_latex: With \(H_k=\nabla^2 f(x_k)\), \(q_k\) is the second-order Taylor model.
With \(H_k=0\), the model is linear but the same radius coupling remains defined.
immediate_consequences_latex: The compact trust region ensures existence of a global subproblem minimizer in finite dimensions.
boundary_notes: Uniform norm equivalence is an added complexity-compatibility condition; the cited basic framework itself permits iteration-dependent norms more generally.
The definition does not require exact solution of the trust-region subproblem.

children.title: Quadratic Model Geometry
children.top_down_role: Coverage of local quadratic representations used in trust-region complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Model Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and optimality geometry of a quadratic trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_0\in\mathbb R\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and \(\Delta>0\). Define
\[m(s)=f_0+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs\quad\text{for }s\in\mathbb R^n\text{ with }\|s\|_2\leq\Delta.\]
Let \(B=Q\Lambda Q^{\mathsf T}\), where \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal and \(\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\). In spectral coordinates \(y=Q^{\mathsf T}s\) and \(h=Q^{\mathsf T}g\),
\[m(s)-f_0=\sum_{i=1}^n\left(h_i y_i+\tfrac12\lambda_i y_i^2\right),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n y_i^2\leq\Delta^2.\]
A vector \(s_*\in\mathbb R^n\) is a global minimizer of this trust-region subproblem if and only if there exists \(\lambda_*\geq0\) such that
\[(B+\lambda_*I)s_*=-g,\qquad B+\lambda_*I\succeq0,\qquad \|s_*\|_2\leq\Delta,\qquad \lambda_*(\Delta-\|s_*\|_2)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal eigendecomposition separates the quadratic model into scalar curvature directions. A feasible step is a global trust-region minimizer exactly when it satisfies the shifted linear system, positive-semidefinite curvature condition, and complementary radius condition for a nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral representation and the displayed multiplier conditions characterize the global minimizers of \(\min_{\|s\|_2\leq\Delta}m(s)\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal eigendecomposition of the symmetric model Hessian
step and gradient expressed in spectral coordinates

children.title: Trust-Radius Control
children.top_down_role: Coverage of neighborhood-size adaptation across accepted or rejected trials.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Radius Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard ratio-based radius update for an unconstrained trust-region iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given thresholds \(0\leq \eta_1<\eta_2<1\), factors \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\), a maximum radius \(\Delta_{\max}>0\), ratio \(\rho_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), and trial step \(s_k\), choose \(\Delta_{k+1}\) by
\[
\Delta_{k+1}\in
\begin{cases}
(0,\gamma_-\Delta_k],&\rho_k<\eta_1,\\
[\gamma_-\Delta_k,\Delta_k],&\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2,\\
[\Delta_k,\min\{\gamma_+\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}\}],&\rho_k\geq\eta_2\ \text{and}\ \|s_k\|=\Delta_k,\\
\{\Delta_k\},&\rho_k\geq\eta_2\ \text{and}\ \|s_k\|<\Delta_k.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus poor agreement contracts the trusted region, while strong agreement permits expansion only when the current boundary is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract the radius after poor model agreement, retain or moderately reduce it after intermediate agreement, and permit bounded expansion after strong agreement with a boundary step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\leq\Delta_{\max}\), with contraction or expansion controlled by \(\rho_k\) and boundary activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Radius Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling conditions used to turn a quadratic trust-region model into a decrease estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let
\[
m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks,
\qquad \|s\|\leq\Delta_k.
\]
A trial step \(s_k\) is model-radius coupled with constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{md}}>0\) when \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) and
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\geq \kappa_{\mathrm{md}}\|g_k\|\min\!\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|g_k\|}{\max\{\|B_k\|,1\}}\right\}.
\]
The condition explicitly links predicted reduction to both local first-order criticality and the radius, preventing an admissible but negligibly decreasing step from serving as the trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid trial step stays inside the trust region and achieves predicted decrease proportional to the gradient norm times the smaller curvature or radius scale.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at \(x_k\), with \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\) whenever \(g_k\neq0\), with decrease quantitatively coupled to \(\Delta_k\).

notation.meaning: quadratic model at the current iterate

children.title: Model Agreement-Acceptance Calculus
children.top_down_role: Acceptance structures connecting predicted and realized decrease.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(s_k\) satisfy \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\). Fix thresholds \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\) and contraction factors \(0<\gamma_1\leq\gamma_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical monotone deterministic trust-region acceptance with exact objective values and a positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the predicted reduction, achieved reduction, and agreement ratio by \[P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k),\qquad A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k),\qquad \rho_k=\frac{A_k}{P_k}.\] The trial is unsuccessful when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), successful when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and very successful when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\). Acceptance and radius control are \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k\geq\eta_1,\\x_k,&\rho_k<\eta_1,\end{cases}\] \[\Delta_{k+1}\in\begin{cases}[\Delta_k,\infty),&\rho_k\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta_k,\Delta_k],&\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta_k,\gamma_2\Delta_k],&\rho_k<\eta_1.\end{cases}\] Thus the calculus links realized decrease to the model certificate: every accepted iteration satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})=\rho_kP_k\geq\eta_1P_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The agreement ratio divides actual objective reduction by predicted model reduction. A trial is accepted when this ratio reaches the acceptance threshold and is very successful at the higher threshold. Rejected trials leave the iterate fixed and contract the radius; very successful trials do not contract it. Every accepted trial realizes at least the acceptance-threshold fraction of its predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\in\mathcal S\Rightarrow f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta_1[m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)]>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The model is often normalized by \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), but the ratio depends only on model differences and does not require that normalization.
special_cases_latex: When \(\rho_k=1\), the realized and predicted reductions agree exactly.
When \(\rho_k<0\), the trial increases the objective and is rejected under \(\eta_1>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The successful and very-successful sets satisfy \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal S\).
A lower bound on \(P_k\) immediately gives a lower bound scaled by \(\eta_1\) on accepted objective decrease.
boundary_notes: The ratio is undefined when the predicted reduction is zero or negative.
Inexact objective values and nonmonotone acceptance require modified ratios.

children.title: Model-Agreement Ratios
children.top_down_role: Coverage of predicted-versus-realized decrease comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Agreement Ratios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-to-predicted reduction ratio for a trust-region trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a current point \(x_k\), model \(m_k\), and trial step \(s_k\), define the actual reduction and predicted reduction by
\[
\operatorname{ared}_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k),\qquad
\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k).
\]
Whenever \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), the model-agreement ratio is
\[
\rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
1-\rho_k=\frac{[f(x_k+s_k)-m_k(s_k)]-[f(x_k)-m_k(0)]}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.
\]
Thus \(\rho_k=1\) denotes exact agreement in reduction, while negative \(\rho_k\) denotes an objective increase despite positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The agreement ratio divides actual objective reduction by positive model-predicted reduction; one means exact agreement, and a negative value means the trial increased the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\in\mathbb R\) is well-defined and measures relative agreement between actual and predicted reduction.

children.title: Trial-Step Acceptance
children.top_down_role: Coverage of successful-iteration classifications used in trust-region analyses.

knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient-agreement acceptance rule for a trust-region trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\). For a trial step satisfying \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), declare the iteration successful and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k
\]
when
\[
\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}\geq\eta.
\]
Acceptance certifies the quantitative objective decrease
\[
f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq\eta\,[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)]>0.
\]
The rule concerns acceptance of the point; any simultaneous radius enlargement requires a separate radius-control criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a trial point when its actual reduction is at least a fixed positive fraction of predicted reduction; acceptance then guarantees strict objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho_k\geq\eta\), then \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) and \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\).

children.title: Trial-Step Rejection
children.top_down_role: Coverage of unsuccessful trials plus their role in complexity accounting.

knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Step Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard rejection rule when actual reduction is too small relative to prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Reject the trial point and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k
\]
when
\[
\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}<\eta.
\]
Rejection includes objective-increasing trials, for which \(\rho_k<0\), and decreasing trials whose reduction is insufficient relative to the model prediction. In a standard trust-region scheme, rejection is paired with a contracted radius \(\Delta_{k+1}\leq\gamma_-\Delta_k\), where \(0<\gamma_-<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject a trial whose actual reduction is below the required fraction of predicted reduction, retain the current iterate, and ordinarily contract the radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho_k<\eta\), then \(x_{k+1}=x_k\); standard control additionally gives \(\Delta_{k+1}<\Delta_k\).

children.title: Agreement Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Coverage of regimes where local models fail to predict objective behavior adequately.

knowledge_statements.title: Agreement Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp algebraic boundaries for defining the agreement ratio and guaranteeing acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\). If \(p_k\leq0\), the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio is undefined or cannot certify descent. For \(p_k>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), acceptance satisfies the exact equivalence
\[
\rho_k\geq\eta
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl|[f(x_k+s_k)-f(x_k)]-[m_k(s_k)-m_k(0)]\bigr|\leq(1-\eta)p_k
\]
whenever the signed reduction error is nonnegative; without that sign restriction, the sufficient condition with the absolute value remains valid. Hence no acceptance guarantee follows from an error estimate exceeding \((1-\eta)p_k\), and vanishing predicted reduction makes relative agreement ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ratio loses meaning at nonpositive predicted reduction; acceptance is guaranteed only when model-reduction error is at most the unused fraction of positive prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive prediction and error no larger than \((1-\eta)p_k\) suffice for \(\rho_k\geq\eta\); these guarantees fail beyond the stated boundaries.

children.title: Scaling-Norm Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Metric choices compatible with uniform complexity control.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(S_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and write physical steps as \(s=S_kw\). Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a fixed reference norm, and define \(\|s\|_k=\|S_k^{-1}s\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional iteration-dependent trust-region scaling with constants uniform over all iterations included in a complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \(\{S_k\}\) defines a uniform scaling-norm equivalence regime when there exist constants \(0<\underline s\leq\overline s<\infty\), independent of \(k\), such that \[\underline s\|w\|\leq\|S_kw\|\leq\overline s\|w\|\qquad\text{for all }w\in\mathbb R^n\text{ and all }k.\] Equivalently, \[\overline s^{-1}\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq\underline s^{-1}\|s\|\qquad\text{for all }s\in\mathbb R^n.\] The scaled trust region \(\|w\|\leq\Delta_k\) is therefore the physical region \(\|S_k^{-1}s\|\leq\Delta_k\). For a quadratic physical model \(q_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), the scaled model has gradient and Hessian \[g_k^{\mathrm s}=S_k^Tg_k,\qquad H_k^{\mathrm s}=S_k^TH_kS_k,\] and satisfies \(q_k(S_kw)=q_k^{\mathrm s}(w)\). Uniform equivalence prevents the constants in radius, gradient, and decrease comparisons from degenerating with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaling regime uses nonsingular coordinate maps to define iteration-dependent trust-region norms. It is uniform when the scaling matrices and their inverses are bounded by iteration-independent constants. Then scaled and physical trust regions, gradients, Hessians, and model decreases are equivalent up to fixed constants suitable for complexity bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|S_k^{-1}s\|\leq\Delta_k\) is equivalent to \(s=S_kw\) with \(\|w\|\leq\Delta_k\), and \(\overline s^{-1}\|s\|\leq\|s\|_k\leq\underline s^{-1}\|s\|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the Euclidean norm, uniform equivalence is equivalent to \(\sup_k\|S_k\|_2<\infty\) and \(\sup_k\|S_k^{-1}\|_2<\infty\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed diagonal scaling with positive diagonal entries automatically gives uniform equivalence.
With \(S_k=I\), the scaled and physical norms coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: A scaled feasible step obeys \(\|s_k\|\leq\overline s\Delta_k\).
Criticality measures expressed with dual scaled norms remain uniformly comparable to those in the reference dual norm.
boundary_notes: Nonsingular but increasingly ill-conditioned \(S_k\) does not define a uniform complexity regime.
The source supports the scaling identities; uniform spectral bounds are the additional condition used here to express complexity compatibility.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower and upper scaling bounds.

review_flags: Uniform boundedness of the scaling and inverse is an explicit complexity-regime condition beyond the basic coordinate identities in the cited section.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scaling and Norm-Equivalence Regime

children.title: Variable Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage of coordinate or metric scaling used in trust-region models.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly well-conditioned variable metrics suitable for iteration-independent complexity constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and define the iteration-dependent scaled norm by
\[
\|s\|_{D_k}=\|D_ks\|_2.
\]
The scaling regime is uniformly admissible when constants \(0<d_-\leq d_+<\infty\), independent of \(k\), satisfy
\[
d_-\|s\|_2\leq\|s\|_{D_k}\leq d_+\|s\|_2
\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Equivalently, \(d_-\leq\sigma_{\min}(D_k)\leq\sigma_{\max}(D_k)\leq d_+\). A trust region \(\|s\|_{D_k}\leq\Delta_k\) therefore contains and is contained in Euclidean balls with radii \(\Delta_k/d_+\) and \(\Delta_k/d_-\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable scaling is uniformly admissible when all scaling matrices have singular values bounded above and away from zero independently of the iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled and Euclidean trust regions are uniformly comparable with constants \(d_-\) and \(d_+\).

notation.meaning: uniform lower and upper scaling bounds
scaled norm induced by the scaling matrix

children.title: Norm-Equivalence Control
children.top_down_role: Coverage of uniform comparisons between model, step, plus criticality norms.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Equivalence Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact comparison of radius balls and dual norms under uniform norm equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\|\cdot\|_a\) and \(\|\cdot\|_b\) be norms on \(\mathbb R^n\), and suppose constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) satisfy
\[
c\|s\|_a\leq\|s\|_b\leq C\|s\|_a
\qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
For every radius \(\Delta>0\), their balls satisfy
\[
\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\|s\|_a\leq\Delta/C\}
\subseteq
\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\|s\|_b\leq\Delta\}
\subseteq
\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\|s\|_a\leq\Delta/c\}.
\]
If \(\|\cdot\|_{a,*}\) and \(\|\cdot\|_{b,*}\) denote the corresponding dual norms, then every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{C}\|v\|_{a,*}\leq\|v\|_{b,*}\leq\frac{1}{c}\|v\|_{a,*}.
\]
Thus radius and dual-norm factors in a decrease certificate can be converted explicitly whenever \(c\) and \(C\) are uniform over the iterations considered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform equivalence of two norms gives explicit inclusions between their radius balls and reciprocal comparison bounds for their dual norms, so radius and dual-norm factors can be transferred with controlled constants.
assumptions_latex: The constants \(c\) and \(C\) are independent of the iteration index whenever the norms vary by iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\Delta>0\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), the stated ball inclusions hold and \(C^{-1}\|v\|_{a,*}\leq\|v\|_{b,*}\leq c^{-1}\|v\|_{a,*}\).

notation.meaning: dual norm corresponding to the a-norm
dual norm corresponding to the b-norm
positive radius in the b-norm ball

children.title: Dimension-Dependent Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Coverage of norm comparisons whose constants vary with problem dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional equivalence constants for standard vector norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(1\leq p\leq q\leq\infty\), the standard vector norms satisfy
\[
\|x\|_q\leq\|x\|_p\leq n^{1/p-1/q}\|x\|_q,
\]
where \(1/\infty=0\). In particular,
\[
\|x\|_\infty\leq\|x\|_2\leq\sqrt n\|x\|_\infty,
\qquad
\|x\|_2\leq\|x\|_1\leq\sqrt n\|x\|_2.
\]
Consequently, transferring a trust-region radius or decrease certificate between these norms may introduce dimension-dependent factors. A bound called dimension-free in one norm remains dimension-free after transfer only if the required equivalence constants are uniformly bounded as \(n\) varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard finite-dimensional norms are equivalent, but their sharp comparison factors can grow with dimension and therefore enter transferred complexity constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_q\leq\|x\|_p\leq n^{1/p-1/q}\|x\|_q\), so norm transfer can be dimension dependent.

notation.meaning: standard p-norm on finite-dimensional Euclidean space

children.title: Metric Uniformity Failures
children.top_down_role: Coverage of scaling regimes that prevent uniform complexity control.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Uniformity Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of iteration- or dimension-uniform constants under degenerating variable metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Uniform metric transfer fails if the equivalence constants are not bounded independently of the relevant index. For example, on \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(D_k=\operatorname{diag}(k,k^{-1})\) and \(\|s\|_{D_k}=\|D_ks\|_2\). Then
\[
k^{-1}\|s\|_2\leq\|s\|_{D_k}\leq k\|s\|_2,
\]
and both constants deteriorate as \(k\to\infty\). The scaled unit ball has Euclidean semiaxes \(k^{-1}\) and \(k\), so no positive constants \(c,C\), independent of \(k\), satisfy \(c\|s\|_2\leq\|s\|_{D_k}\leq C\|s\|_2\). Therefore complexity constants derived by uniform norm transfer need not remain iteration independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerating scaling matrices destroy uniform norm equivalence; their trust regions become arbitrarily anisotropic, invalidating iteration-independent transfers of complexity constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No iteration-independent \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) uniformly compares \(\|\cdot\|_{D_k}\) with \(\|\cdot\|_2\).

notation.meaning: norm induced by the variable scaling

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\) on \(\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\). Let \(s_k^{\mathrm C}\) be a Cauchy step, and when \(H_k\) has negative curvature let \(s_k^{\mathrm E}\) be an eigenpoint step. Fix a fraction \(\kappa_{\mathrm d}\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic trust-region models. The certificate concerns predicted model decrease; objective decrease follows only after a separate agreement-based acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A first-order trust-region decrease certificate requires \[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm d}\,[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm C})].\] A joint gradient-curvature certificate requires \[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm d}\max\{q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm C}),\ q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm E})\}.\] More generally, for a nonnegative criticality measure \(\Psi_k(\Delta_k)\), a general criticality-measure certificate has the form \[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm d}\Psi_k(\Delta_k).\] The family is uniform when \(\kappa_{\mathrm d}\) and every norm-equivalence or curvature-quality constant entering \(\Psi_k\) are positive and independent of \(k\). A step satisfying a joint certificate cannot ignore whichever of the gradient or negative-curvature reference steps gives the larger model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region decrease certificate requires the computed step to obtain a fixed fraction of a reference model decrease. The first-order family uses the Cauchy reference. The curvature-sensitive family also uses an eigenpoint and requires a fraction of the better reduction. A general certificate lower-bounds predicted decrease by a criticality measure depending on the radius. Uniform constants make the certificate usable in complexity analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm d}\max\{\Delta q_k^{\mathrm C},\Delta q_k^{\mathrm E}\}\) in the joint certificate regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The maximum form equals \(q_k(0)-\min\{q_k(s_k^{\mathrm C}),q_k(s_k^{\mathrm E})\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H_k\succeq0\), the curvature reference may be omitted and the family reduces to a Cauchy decrease certificate.
An exact global solution of the trust-region subproblem satisfies the certificate with \(\kappa_{\mathrm d}=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If an accepted step has \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), then its objective decrease is at least \(\eta_1\kappa_{\mathrm d}\Psi_k(\Delta_k)\).
boundary_notes: The certificate does not prescribe how the step is computed.
For nonquadratic models, eigenpoint definitions and curvature decrease require corresponding model-regularity conditions.

children.title: Cauchy Decrease Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: First-order model-decrease certificates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k(s)=q_k(0)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), where \(H_k\) is symmetric, and let the trust region be \(\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\). Assume \(g_k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order predicted-decrease certificates for finite-dimensional quadratic trust-region models, including indefinite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Cauchy step is \[s_k^{\mathrm C}=-t_k^{\mathrm C}g_k,\qquad t_k^{\mathrm C}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\geq0,\ \|tg_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k}q_k(-tg_k).\] A trial step \(s_k\) satisfies a fraction-of-Cauchy decrease certificate with constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm C}\in(0,1]\) when \[\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k,\qquad q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm C}[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm C})].\] In the Euclidean norm, with \(\beta_k\geq\|H_k\|_2\), the Cauchy reference decrease admits the standard scale \[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm C})\geq\frac12\|g_k\|_2\min\left\{\frac{\|g_k\|_2}{\beta_k},\Delta_k\right\}.\] Consequently the certificate supplies a quantitative predicted-decrease lower bound whenever the gradient is nonzero, regardless of whether \(H_k\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cauchy step minimizes the quadratic model along the feasible negative-gradient ray. A computed trial step has a fraction-of-Cauchy certificate when it is feasible and achieves at least a fixed fraction of the Cauchy step's model reduction. In the Euclidean norm this gives the standard gradient times minimum-of-gradient-over-curvature-and-radius decrease scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm C}}2\|g_k\|_2\min\{\|g_k\|_2/\beta_k,\Delta_k\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(g_k^TH_kg_k\leq0\), the Cauchy step lies on the trust-region boundary.
If \(g_k^TH_kg_k>0\), its ray length is the smaller of the unconstrained line minimizer and the boundary length.
special_cases_latex: The exact Cauchy step itself satisfies the certificate with \(\kappa_{\mathrm C}=1\).
Any exact global trust-region minimizer achieves at least the Cauchy decrease.
immediate_consequences_latex: With an acceptance ratio \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), the realized objective decrease is at least the displayed lower bound multiplied by \(\eta_1\).
boundary_notes: When \(g_k=0\), the Cauchy decrease is zero and does not certify progress from negative curvature.
For non-Euclidean norms, norm-ratio factors enter the quantitative lower bound.

notation.meaning: Cauchy step along the feasible negative-gradient ray.
Upper bound on quadratic model curvature.

children.title: Cauchy-Point Decrease
children.top_down_role: Coverage of first-order decrease obtained from the canonical steepest model direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy-Point Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted-decrease certificate for exact minimization along the negative-gradient ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs,
\]
where \(B\) is symmetric, \(g\neq0\), and \(\Delta>0\). Define the Cauchy point by \(s_C=-t_Cg\), where
\[
t_C\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\leq t\leq\Delta/\|g\|}m(-tg).
\]
Then its predicted reduction satisfies
\[
m(0)-m(s_C)\geq\tfrac12\|g\|\min\!\left\{\Delta,\frac{\|g\|}{\|B\|}\right\},
\]
with \(\|g\|/\|B\|=+\infty\) when \(B=0\). Thus the computable pair \((g,B)\), radius \(\Delta\), and ray minimizer certify a positive first-order model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact minimization of a quadratic model along the negative-gradient ray achieves at least half the gradient norm times the smaller radius or curvature scale.

children.title: Approximate-Cauchy Decrease
children.top_down_role: Coverage of relaxed first-order decrease requirements for inexact subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Cauchy Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fraction-of-Cauchy decrease certificate for an inexact trust-region trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the quadratic model
\[
m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs,
\]
let \(s_C\) be its Cauchy point in the ball \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\). A feasible step \(s\) satisfies an approximate-Cauchy certificate with fraction \(\kappa_C\in(0,1]\) if
\[
m(0)-m(s)\geq\kappa_C[m(0)-m(s_C)].
\]
Consequently,
\[
m(0)-m(s)\geq\frac{\kappa_C}{2}\|g\|\min\!\left\{\Delta,\frac{\|g\|}{\|B\|}\right\},
\]
with the zero-curvature convention \(\|g\|/\|B\|=+\infty\). Hence exact solution of the trust-region subproblem is unnecessary for the standard decrease scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible step attaining a fixed fraction of Cauchy-point reduction inherits the Cauchy decrease bound with the same fractional degradation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy Certificate Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies loss when a trial step attains only a fraction of exact Cauchy decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(s_C\) minimize \(m(-tg)\) over \(0\le t\|g\|\le\Delta\). Then \(m(0)-m(s_C)\ge \tfrac12\|g\|\min\{\Delta,\|g\|/\|H\|\}\), with \(\|g\|/\|H\|=+\infty\) when \(H=0\). Consequently, any feasible step \(s\) satisfying \(m(0)-m(s)\ge\theta[m(0)-m(s_C)]\), for \(0<\theta\le1\), satisfies \[m(0)-m(s)\ge \frac{\theta}{2}\|g\|\min\!\left\{\Delta,\frac{\|g\|}{\|H\|}\right\}.\] Thus approximate Cauchy solution degrades the certificate only by the multiplicative factor \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step achieving a fraction θ of exact Cauchy decrease retains the standard Cauchy lower bound multiplied by θ.

notation.meaning: Exact minimizer along the negative-gradient ray.
Retained fraction of exact Cauchy decrease.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k(s)=q_k(0)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\) on \(\|s\|_k\leq\Delta_k\), and suppose symmetric \(H_k\) has a negative eigenvalue \(\tau_k<0\). Fix \(\kappa_{\mathrm{nc}},\kappa_{\mathrm E}\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature-sensitive certificates for finite-dimensional indefinite quadratic trust-region models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An admissible negative-curvature direction is a vector \(u_k\) satisfying \[g_k^Tu_k\leq0,\qquad\|u_k\|_k=\Delta_k,\qquad u_k^TH_ku_k\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{nc}}	au_k(
u_k^{\mathrm E})^2\Delta_k^2,\] where \(
u_k^{\mathrm E}=\|u_k\|_2/\|u_k\|_k\). The eigenpoint step is \[s_k^{\mathrm E}=t_k^{\mathrm E}u_k,\qquad t_k^{\mathrm E}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0<t\leq1}q_k(tu_k).\] For a quadratic model these sign and curvature conditions give \(t_k^{\mathrm E}=1\). A trial step \(s_k\) has an eigenpoint curvature-decrease certificate when \[\|s_k\|_k\leq\Delta_k,\qquad q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm E}[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k^{\mathrm E})].\] Its quantitative curvature scale is \[q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq- rac12\kappa_{\mathrm E}\kappa_{\mathrm{nc}}	au_k(
u_k^{\mathrm E})^2\Delta_k^2>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eigenpoint certificate selects a boundary-scaled direction that has nonpositive directional slope and captures a fixed fraction of a negative eigenvalue. The eigenpoint minimizes the quadratic model along this direction. A certified trial step achieves a fixed fraction of the eigenpoint reduction, yielding decrease proportional to the magnitude of negative curvature times the squared radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k(0)-q_k(s_k)\geq\tfrac12\kappa_{\mathrm E}\kappa_{\mathrm{nc}}|\tau_k|(\nu_k^{\mathrm E})^2\Delta_k^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the Euclidean norm with a unit eigenvector \(v_k\) for \(\tau_k\), one may choose \(u_k=\pm\Delta_kv_k\), with the sign selected so that \(g_k^Tu_k\leq0\).
special_cases_latex: For an exact most-negative eigenvector in the Euclidean norm, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{nc}}=1\) and \(\nu_k^{\mathrm E}=1\).
If \(H_k\succeq0\), no negative-curvature eigenpoint certificate is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: Combining the eigenpoint and Cauchy certificates prevents the model solver from ignoring either a large gradient or significant negative curvature.
After acceptance with \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), the same curvature-scale lower bound holds for objective decrease with an additional factor \(\eta_1\).
boundary_notes: The definition requires a strictly negative curvature value; zero curvature gives no positive eigenpoint decrease bound.
Approximate eigenvectors must retain a uniform positive curvature-capture constant for complexity use.

notation.meaning: A negative eigenvalue or certified negative-curvature value of \(H_k\).
Eigenpoint step minimizing the model along \(u_k\).

children.title: Eigenpoint Decrease
children.top_down_role: Coverage of curvature-sensitive decrease based on extreme spectral information.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenpoint Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a leftmost eigenvector with nonpositive eigenvalue to certify quadratic-model decrease at the trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), suppose \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\le0\), and let \(u\) be a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\). Choose its sign so that \(g^{\mathsf T}u\le0\), and set \(s_E=\Delta u\). Then \(\|s_E\|=\Delta\) and \[m(0)-m(s_E)=-\Delta g^{\mathsf T}u-\frac12\Delta^2\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge\frac12\Delta^2\bigl(-\lambda_{\min}(H)\bigr).\] When \(\lambda_{\min}(H)<0\), the Rayleigh quotient and sign condition constitute a directly checkable curvature-decrease certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the smallest Hessian eigenvalue is nonpositive, a signed leftmost-eigenvector step on the trust-region boundary yields decrease at least half its negative value times the squared radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(0)-m(s_E)\ge\tfrac12\Delta^2(-\lambda_{\min}(H))\).

notation.meaning: Unit leftmost eigenvector with sign chosen against the gradient.
Smallest eigenvalue of the symmetric model Hessian.

children.title: Negative-Curvature Decrease
children.top_down_role: Coverage of model reduction obtained from directions of negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends eigenpoint decrease to any direction carrying certified negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be a unit vector satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\le-\gamma\) for some \(\gamma>0\). Replace \(d\) by \(-d\), if necessary, so that \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\), and take \(s=\Delta d\). For the quadratic model \(m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), \[m(0)-m(s)=-\Delta g^{\mathsf T}d-\frac12\Delta^2d^{\mathsf T}Hd\ge\frac12\gamma\Delta^2.\] Hence any verifiable Rayleigh-quotient bound below \(-\gamma\) supplies a feasible decrease guarantee without requiring an exact eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any unit direction with curvature at most −γ, signed against the gradient, guarantees quadratic-model decrease of at least γΔ²/2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(0)-m(\Delta d)\ge\tfrac12\gamma\Delta^2\) after choosing \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\).

children.title: Approximate Curvature Detection
children.top_down_role: Coverage of inexact spectral information sufficient for curvature-sensitive guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Curvature Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translates an additive approximate-eigenvalue guarantee into detection and near-semidefiniteness certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a curvature routine returns a unit vector \(u\) and \(\widehat\lambda=u^{\mathsf T}Hu\) satisfying \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\le\widehat\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(H)+\eta\), where \(\eta\ge0\). For a tolerance \(\varepsilon_H>0\), if \(\widehat\lambda\le-\varepsilon_H\), then \(u\) certifies negative curvature and, after sign selection, the boundary step gives at least \(\tfrac12\varepsilon_H\Delta^2\) model decrease. If \(\widehat\lambda>-\varepsilon_H\), then \(\lambda_{\min}(H)>-(\varepsilon_H+\eta)\). Thus the detector either produces a decrease direction or certifies approximate positive semidefiniteness with the additive error \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive eigenvalue approximation either detects usable negative curvature or certifies that the Hessian is positive semidefinite up to εH+η.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\lambda\le-\varepsilon_H\) yields curvature decrease, while \(\widehat\lambda>-\varepsilon_H\) implies \(H\succeq-(\varepsilon_H+\eta)I\).
