knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let a baseline trust-region framework be specified by a model-validity condition \(V_k\), a decrease condition \(D_k\), an acceptance statistic \(\rho_k\), a radius update, a criticality target \(\chi(x)
\leq\epsilon\), and a counted oracle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract classification of deterministic or stochastic trust-region methods according to features that alter the worst-case complexity interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A trust-region method is a complexity-material variant of the baseline if it replaces at least one baseline interface by a mathematically distinct object that enters the quantified evaluation bound: a conditional or random model-validity event \(V_k\), accuracy-controlled inexact evaluations, a nonmonotone acceptance reference, an altered success probability, or a different counted oracle. Formally, the variant must declare a tuple \[\mathfrak T=(V_k,D_k,\rho_k,U_k,\chi,\mathcal O,\mathbb P)\] and a bound \(N_{\mathfrak T}(
\epsilon,
\delta)\) whose quantifiers use that tuple. A mere change in the numerical subproblem solver is not a distinct complexity variant when it preserves the same uniform decrease certificate, validity assumptions, acceptance rule, and oracle count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complexity variant changes an assumption or mechanism that appears in the worst-case guarantee, such as conditional models, dynamic accuracy, nonmonotone acceptance, probability of model accuracy, or oracle accounting. Merely swapping interchangeable inner solvers does not create a new complexity framework.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Classification as a complexity variant requires an explicit altered interface and an associated evaluation-bound statement using that interface.
special_cases_latex: Probabilistically accurate models add a probability law and confidence or expectation quantifier.
Dynamic-accuracy methods add evaluation error tolerances linked to predicted decrease.
Nonmonotone methods replace \(f(x_k)\) in the acceptance numerator by a declared reference value.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two implementations with the same tuple \(\mathfrak T\) belong to the same complexity variant even if their linear algebra differs.
Bounds from different variants are comparable only after aligning their probability and oracle conventions.
boundary_notes: This is a project-level organizing definition and requires a source or explicit convention for promotion.
The definition does not assert that every listed variant achieves the same accuracy exponent.

notation.meaning: Tuple of mechanisms and quantifiers defining the complexity framework.

review_flags: Needs a survey or framework source supporting the stated criterion for complexity-material variants.
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity-Material Trust-Region Variant

children.title: Conditional-Model Trust Regions
children.top_down_role: Complexity interfaces based on conditionally valid local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Model Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-accuracy predicate sufficient to transfer predicted trust-region decrease to objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k\) model \(f(x_k+s)\) on \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\). The model is conditionally fully linear when, on a declared validity condition \(\mathcal C_k\), constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\) independent of \(k\) satisfy \[|f(x_k+s)-m_k(s)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k(s)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\] for every \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\). A conditional-model trust-region complexity argument may charge ordinary successful-step decrease only on iterations satisfying \(\mathcal C_k\); iterations outside it require a separate bound, restoration mechanism, or probability estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional model has uniform function and gradient accuracy only when a stated validity event holds; invalid iterations must be accounted for separately.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m_k\) are differentiable on the trust region
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_k\Longrightarrow\sup_{\|s\|\le\Delta_k}|f(x_k+s)-m_k(s)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2\text{ and }\sup_{\|s\|\le\Delta_k}\|\nabla f(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k(s)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fully-linear inequalities form a coherent conditional model-accuracy predicate, and condition fits the leaf. A source is needed to establish this named conditional-model variant and the required accounting of invalid iterations; the validity condition is otherwise application-dependent.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust Region with Conditionally Valid Local Models
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m_k\) be a model defined on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). Let \(V_k\) be a checkable model-validity condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic conditional-model framework, including derivative-free models that are rebuilt until a local validity condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A conditional-model trust-region iteration is one in which the trial step and acceptance test are used only after the condition \(V_k\) certifies prescribed local model accuracy. A first-order conditionally valid model has constants \(\kappa_f,
\kappa_g\geq0\), independent of \(k\), such that whenever \(V_k\) holds, \[|f(x_k+s)-m_k(x_k+s)|
\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,
\qquad\|\nabla f(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k(x_k+s)\|_2
\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\] for every \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta_k\). If \(V_k\) fails, the framework invokes a model-improvement operation rather than interpreting an unsuccessful ratio as evidence that the radius alone is too large. A second-order version adds a uniformly scaled Hessian-accuracy condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional-model trust region permits the model to be used for optimization only when a checkable condition guarantees uniform local accuracy on the current ball. If the condition fails, the model or its defining geometry is repaired before ordinary acceptance logic is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On every iteration declared model-valid, the model obeys the displayed uniform value and gradient accuracy inequalities throughout the trust region.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
The displayed conditions are commonly called full linearity of \(m_k\) on \(B(x_k,
\Delta_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For interpolation models, \(V_k\) may require a sufficiently well-poised interpolation set.
For an exact first-order Taylor model with Lipschitz gradient, the validity bounds hold uniformly for sufficiently small radii.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failed model-validity test is logically distinct from rejection of a valid trial step.
Uniform gradient accuracy makes model criticality comparable with objective criticality at scale \(\Delta_k\).
boundary_notes: Accuracy only at \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) is weaker than uniform conditional validity over the trust region.
The exact constants and second-order extension depend on the selected conditional-model framework.

notation.meaning: Checkable event or predicate under which the model is locally valid.

source_refs.locator: Section 9.1, conditional model validity condition (9.1.2), p. 308; Section 9.4, Conditional Models and Derivative-Free Optimization, pp. 322–333

children.title: Dynamic-Accuracy Trust Regions
children.top_down_role: Adaptive function, derivative, and model precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Accuracy Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region iteration that tightens oracle accuracy relative to the predicted model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), and \(\omega\in(0,1)
\), construct an inexact model \(m_k\), compute \(s_k\) with \(\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k\), and set \(\delta m_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Request function approximations \(\bar f_k^0,\bar f_k^s\) with certified errors at most \(\omega\delta m_k\). If the requested certification fails, increase oracle precision and recompute. Otherwise form \[\bar\rho_k=\frac{\bar f_k^0-\bar f_k^s}{\delta m_k},\] accept or reject \(s_k\) using fixed ratio thresholds, update \(\Delta_k\), and stop when the prescribed inexact criticality certificate meets its tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method makes oracle errors proportional to predicted reduction, recomputing at higher precision when necessary before applying the usual acceptance ratio.
assumptions_latex: the oracle can return certified error bounds at requested precisions
fixed acceptance and radius-update thresholds are supplied
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\bar f_k^0-f(x_k)|\le\omega\delta m_k\text{ and }|\bar f_k^s-f(x_k+s_k)|\le\omega\delta m_k\) before the acceptance decision.

notation.meaning: acceptance ratio formed from certified inexact values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the container, but the stated error budget, recomputation rule, acceptance policy, and stopping certificate depend on a particular dynamic-accuracy framework. No source verifies these choices, and the scope mentions derivative and model precision while the algorithm specifies only function-value accuracy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). An inexact evaluation oracle returns \(\bar f(x,
\epsilon)\) satisfying \(|\bar f(x,
\epsilon)-f(x)|
\leq\epsilon\) for a requested accuracy \(\epsilon\geq0\). Let \(d_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional trust-region methods with adaptively requested deterministic function accuracy; derivative errors require separate controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dynamic-accuracy trust-region iteration selects accuracies \(\epsilon_k,
\epsilon_k^+\geq0\) for the evaluations at \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) so that \[\max\{\epsilon_k,
\epsilon_k^+\}
\leq\eta_0d_k,
\qquad0<\eta_0<\tfrac12\eta_1,\] where \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\) is the successful-step threshold. It then forms the inexact ratio \[\bar\rho_k=
\frac{\bar f(x_k,
\epsilon_k)-\bar f(x_k+s_k,
\epsilon_k^+)}{d_k}.\] The defining rule ties evaluation precision to the current predicted decrease and may repeatedly reduce the requested errors until the inequality holds. Function and derivative accuracies are distinct controls unless the oracle supplies a verified relation between them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic-accuracy trust-region method requests only enough function accuracy to make the observed-to-predicted reduction ratio reliable. Both function errors are bounded by a fixed fraction of the current predicted decrease and can be tightened adaptively before the acceptance decision.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
The oracle condition is \(\bar f(x,
0)=f(x)\) and \(|\bar f(x,
\epsilon)-\bar f(x,
0)|
\leq\epsilon\).
special_cases_latex:
Exact function values correspond to \(\epsilon_k=
\epsilon_k^+=0\).
When predicted decrease becomes small, the rule forces increasingly accurate evaluations.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\bar\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), then the exact reduction ratio remains positive because \(2\eta_0<\eta_1\).
Loose evaluations are permitted when the predicted decrease is large.
boundary_notes: Pointwise accuracy at two evaluated points does not imply uniform model validity in a neighborhood.
No gradient-accuracy conclusion follows from the function-error inequality alone.

notation.meaning: Accuracy fraction relative to predicted decrease.

source_refs.locator: Section 10.6.1, inexact evaluation condition (10.6.1) and dynamic accuracy rule (10.6.2), pp. 399–401; Section 10.6.2, p. 406

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-memory nonmonotone acceptance for smooth unconstrained trust-region methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks\), and define \(R_k=\max_{0\le j\le \min\{k,M-1\}}f(x_{k-j})\) for a fixed \(M\ge1\). For a trial step \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|s_k\|\le\Delta_k\) and \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), set \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{nm}}=(R_k-f(x_k+s_k))/(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k))\). Accept whenever \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{nm}}\ge\eta\), where \(\eta\in(0,1)\). Although an accepted step may increase \(f\), it satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})\le R_k-\eta\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\bigr)\), providing decrease relative to the bounded-memory reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance may increase the current objective, but it enforces sufficient decrease from the maximum of a fixed number of recent objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable and bounded below on the generated level region.
The trial step gives strictly positive predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_{k+1})\le R_k-\eta\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: maximum objective value in the bounded reference window

source_refs.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-memory acceptance rule and stated decrease inequality are mathematically coherent and the principle kind fits the leaf, but the cited basic trust-region section does not support the nonmonotone reference rule or its role in evaluation-complexity analysis. A direct nonmonotone trust-region source with a specific algorithm or theorem locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\) be a quadratic model on \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\}\). Fix an integer memory length \(M\geq0\) and an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization with a windowed maximum reference value; other nonmonotone reference sequences are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C_k=\max\{f(x_{k-j}):0\leq j\leq\min(k,M)\}\). For a trial step \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) and \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), define \[\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}=\frac{C_k-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] A windowed nonmonotone trust-region iteration accepts the trial point when \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}\geq\eta\), setting \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\); otherwise it sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). The trust-region radius is updated from \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}\), commonly by contraction after rejection and possible expansion after sufficiently successful boundary steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A windowed nonmonotone trust-region method replaces the current objective value in the usual actual-reduction numerator by \(C_k\), the largest objective value among the most recent \(M+1\) iterates. A trial step with positive predicted reduction is accepted precisely when the ratio \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}=(C_k-f(x_k+s_k))/(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k))\) reaches the prescribed threshold \(\eta\). Thus an accepted step may increase \(f\) relative to \(f(x_k)\), but only within the allowance determined by the finite-memory reference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining acceptance relation is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{NM}}\geq\eta\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(M=0\), \(C_k=f(x_k)\), so the definition reduces to the monotone trust-region ratio.
special_cases_latex: An accepted step can satisfy \(f(x_k+s_k)>f(x_k)\) provided \(f(x_k+s_k)\leq C_k-\eta[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accepted step satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})\leq C_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover weighted-average reference values, watchdog procedures, or filter acceptance.
No convergence or evaluation-complexity claim is included.
review_flags: No inspected authoritative source in the supplied corpus was found that supports this exact windowed-reference definition and update scope.

children.title: Probabilistically Accurate Trust-Region Models
children.top_down_role: Expected and high-probability complexity under random model accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistically Accurate Trust-Region Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order expected and tail evaluation complexity with conditionally accurate random models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) contain the algorithmic history before constructing the random model \(M_k\). Suppose \(M_k\) is fully linear on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) with conditional probability at least \(p>1/2\), meaning that, on the accuracy event, \(|f(y)-M_k(y)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2\) and \(\|
abla f(y)-
abla M_k(y)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\) throughout that ball. Under standard trust-region acceptance, radius-update, sufficient-decrease, and drift conditions, the stopping time \(T_\varepsilon=\inf\{k:\|
abla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[T_\varepsilon]\le C\varepsilon^{-2}\); compatible concentration assumptions yield \(\mathbb P(T_\varepsilon>C_1\varepsilon^{-2}+t)\le e^{-C_2t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally reliable fully linear random models retain first-order trust-region complexity in expectation and, with concentration assumptions, with exponentially decaying delay probability.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has Lipschitz-continuous gradient and is bounded below on the relevant region.
\(\mathbb P(M_k\text{ is fully linear}\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\ge p>1/2\).
Algorithmic constants satisfy the drift and sufficient-decrease requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[T_\varepsilon]=O(\varepsilon^{-2})\), with an exponential upper tail under additional concentration hypotheses.

notation.meaning: random trust-region model at iteration k
sigma-field generated by the prior algorithmic history
first iteration reaching gradient norm at most epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but the threshold p>1/2, drift hypotheses, expected bound, and exponential tail formula depend on the precise stochastic trust-region framework. No citation is supplied, and the unspecified “compatible concentration assumptions” are insufficient to identify a theorem supporting the stated tail bound.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let the random model \(M_k\), center \(X_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\) be defined on a probability space, and let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) denote the information available before \(M_k\) is generated.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random second-order models for finite-dimensional smooth trust-region methods; the definition is conditional on the algorithmic history and uses uniform accuracy over the current ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g,\kappa_H>0\) and \(p\in(0,1]\), define the event \(I_k\) that, for every \(s\) with \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\), \[|f(X_k+s)-M_k(s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^3,\quad \|
abla f(X_k+s)-
abla M_k(s)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k^2,\] \[\|
abla^2f(X_k+s)-
abla^2M_k(s)\|\leq\kappa_H\Delta_k.\] The model sequence is \(p\)-probabilistically fully quadratic when \[\mathbb P(I_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\quad	ext{almost surely for every }k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random trust-region model is probabilistically fully quadratic when, conditional on all prior algorithmic information, it has probability at least \(p\) of uniformly approximating the objective, gradient, and Hessian on the current radius-\(\Delta_k\) ball with errors of orders \(\Delta_k^3\), \(\Delta_k^2\), and \(\Delta_k\), respectively. The probability requirement is imposed at every iteration and does not require independence between successive models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining probability condition is \(\mathbb P(I_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely for all \(k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(p=1\), the model is fully quadratic almost surely at every iteration.
Omitting the Hessian inequality and replacing the function and gradient orders by \(\Delta_k^2\) and \(\Delta_k\) gives the nearby fully linear model notion.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dependence of \(M_k\) on earlier random iterates is permitted because accuracy is measured conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\).
boundary_notes: This definition alone supplies neither an expected-complexity theorem nor a high-probability stopping bound.
The threshold on \(p\) needed by a particular convergence theorem is not part of the model-accuracy definition.

notation.meaning: event that the current model satisfies all three uniform accuracy inequalities
sigma-algebra generated by the algorithmic history before model construction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cubic regularization of a quadratic Taylor model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable at \(x\), set \(g=\nabla f(x)\) and \(H=\nabla^2f(x)\), and choose \(M>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean unconstrained optimization using an exact gradient and Hessian; this is the classical isotropic cubic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cubic-regularized second-order model at \(x\) is \[m_{x,M}(s)=f(x)+g^Ts+\frac12s^THs+\frac{M}{6}\|s\|^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n.\] A cubic-regularization step is any \(s_M(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R^n}m_{x,M}(s)\), and the associated update is \(T_M(x)=x+s_M(x)\). A global minimizer satisfies \[g+Hs_M(x)+\frac{M}{2}\|s_M(x)\|s_M(x)=0,\qquad H+\frac{M}{2}\|s_M(x)\|I\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cubic regularization augments the quadratic Taylor model of \(f\) at \(x\) by the coercive term \((M/6)\|s\|^3\). A step is a global minimizer of this model over all of \(\mathbb R^n\), and the next point is \(x+s\). Its global optimality system consists of stationarity for the cubic model together with positive semidefiniteness of the shifted Hessian \(H+(M/2)\|s\|I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining object is \(T_M(x)=x+s_M(x)\) with \(s_M(x)\in\arg\min_s m_{x,M}(s)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\sigma=M/2\), the same model is written \(f(x)+g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3\).
special_cases_latex: If \(s_M(x)=0\), then the optimality conditions imply \(g=0\) and \(H\succeq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(M>0\), \(m_{x,M}(s)\to+\infty\) as \(\|s\|\to\infty\), so the model has at least one global minimizer.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require \(H\succeq0\).
Adaptive parameter updates and inexact subproblem solutions are separate variants.

notation.meaning: positive cubic coefficient in the normalization \(M\|s\|^3/6\)
point obtained from a global cubic-model minimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic regularization of a quadratic Taylor model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Phase Cubic-Regularization Convergence Under Degree-Two Gradient Domination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A thresholded global-to-local objective-gap rate for the referenced cubic-regularized iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R} have minimizer x^* and satisfy f(x)-f(x^*)\le\tau_f\|\nabla f(x)\|^2 for every x\in\mathbb{R}^d, where \tau_f>0. Suppose method (4.1.16) generates \{x_k\}_{k\ge0} and, for constants L,L_0>0, f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{L_0}{3\sqrt2(L+L_0)^{3/2}}\|\nabla f(x_{k+1})\|^{3/2} for every k\ge0. Define \widetilde\omega=\frac{L_0^4}{324(L+L_0)^6\tau_f^3}. If f(x_0)-f(x^*)\ge\widetilde\omega, then for each k with f(x_k)-f(x^*)\ge\widetilde\omega,\quad f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le(f(x_0)-f(x^*))e^{-k\sigma}, where \sigma=\frac{\widetilde\omega^{1/4}}{\widetilde\omega^{1/4}+(f(x_0)-f(x^*))^{1/4}}. If k_0 is the smallest index with f(x_{k_0})-f(x^*)<\widetilde\omega and such an index exists, then for every k\ge k_0,\quad f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)\le\widetilde\omega\left(\frac{f(x_k)-f(x^*)}{\widetilde\omega}\right)^{4/3}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under global degree-two gradient domination and the stated one-step decrease bound, the referenced cubic method has an exponential objective-gap estimate while the gap remains above a threshold. If the gap first falls below that threshold, subsequent iterates satisfy a local four-thirds-power recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&f(x_0)-f(x^*)\ge\widetilde\omega\Rightarrow \forall k\text{ with }f(x_k)-f(x^*)\ge\widetilde\omega,\quad f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le(f(x_0)-f(x^*))e^{-k\sigma},\\ &\sigma=\frac{\widetilde\omega^{1/4}}{\widetilde\omega^{1/4}+(f(x_0)-f(x^*))^{1/4}},\\ &k_0=\min\{k:f(x_k)-f(x^*)<\widetilde\omega\}\text{ exists}\Rightarrow\forall k\ge k_0,\quad f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)\le\widetilde\omega\left(\frac{f(x_k)-f(x^*)}{\widetilde\omega}\right)^{4/3}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Regime Cubic-Regularization Rate Under Degree-One Gradient Domination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap convergence of the referenced cubic-regularized method for degree-one gradient-dominated objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the cubic-regularized method denoted (4.1.16) be applied to a degree-one gradient-dominated function f with minimizer x^*, and define \widehat\omega=\frac{18}{L_0^2}\tau_f^3(L+L_0)^3. If f(x_0)-f(x^*)\ge\widehat\omega, then for every k\ge0,\quad \log\!\left(\frac{f(x_k)-f(x^*)}{\widehat\omega}\right)\le\left(\frac23\right)^k\log\!\left(\frac{f(x_0)-f(x^*)}{\widehat\omega}\right). If f(x_0)-f(x^*)\le\gamma^2\widehat\omega for some \gamma>1, then for every k\ge0,\quad f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le\widehat\omega\,\frac{\gamma^2(2+\frac32\gamma)^2}{(2+(k+\frac32)\gamma)^2}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the referenced cubic-regularized method on a degree-one gradient-dominated objective, an initial gap above the threshold obeys a geometric contraction of its logarithmic normalized gap. An initial gap within gamma squared times the threshold obeys an explicit inverse-square bound at every iteration.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is gradient dominated of degree }p=1\text{ with constant }\tau_f
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}f(x_0)-f(x^*)\ge\widehat\omega\Rightarrow\forall k\ge0,\ \log\!\frac{f(x_k)-f(x^*)}{\widehat\omega}\le(\frac23)^k\log\!\frac{f(x_0)-f(x^*)}{\widehat\omega},\\ \gamma>1,\ f(x_0)-f(x^*)\le\gamma^2\widehat\omega\Rightarrow\forall k\ge0,\ f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le\widehat\omega\frac{\gamma^2(2+\frac32\gamma)^2}{(2+(k+\frac32)\gamma)^2}.\end{cases}

children.title: Cubic Model Globalization Architectures
children.top_down_role: Model geometries and parameter-control families underlying cubic regularization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable and let \(x_k\), \(g_k\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(M_k>0\) be the current point, derivative data, curvature model, and cubic coefficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained methods whose globalization is obtained by minimizing a coercive cubic model; acceptance-controlled ARC is treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cubic-model globalization architecture is a sequence of models \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks+\frac{M_k}{6}\|s\|^3\] together with steps \(s_k\in\arg\min_s m_k(s)\) and updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). In the fixed-overestimator architecture, if \(\nabla^2f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\), one prescribes \(M_k\geq L\); then the cubic model is an upper model along the trial step. In a searched architecture, \(M_k\) is increased until the majorization test \[f(x_k+s_k)\leq m_k(s_k)\] holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The architecture consists of a coercive cubic model, a rule selecting a global model minimizer, and a rule controlling the cubic coefficient. A fixed architecture uses a coefficient at least as large as the Hessian Lipschitz constant. A searched architecture increases the coefficient until the computed model value upper-bounds the new objective value. Both globalize Newton-type steps without imposing a bounded trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A generated step obeys \(s_k\in\arg\min m_k\), while the parameter-control rule enforces either \(M_k\geq L\) or the direct test \(f(x_k+s_k)\leq m_k(s_k)\).
special_cases_latex: The constant choice \(M_k=L\) gives a fixed cubic Newton architecture when \(L\) is known.
immediate_consequences_latex: For accepted majorizing steps, \(f(x_{k+1})\leq m_k(s_k)\leq m_k(0)=f(x_k)\).
boundary_notes: Ratio-based acceptance and multi-interval ARC updates are not included.
The statement uses exact Hessians and exact global model minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Isotropic Cubic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean cubic model used in cubic-regularization methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), a gradient vector \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), a symmetric matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(\sigma>0\), the isotropic cubic model is \[m(s)=f(x)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\frac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n.\] Its regularizer is rotationally invariant: for every orthogonal matrix \(Q\), \(\|Qs\|_2^3=\|s\|_2^3\). Consequently the regularization strength depends only on Euclidean step length, while anisotropy enters solely through the linear and quadratic terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isotropic cubic model adds a positive multiple of the cubed Euclidean step norm to a quadratic local model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(s)=f(x)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3\).

notation.meaning: trial displacement from the current point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and rotational-invariance statement are mathematically correct and fit the isotropic-cubic-model leaf, but the record has no citation. An authoritative cubic-regularization source with a specific section, definition, theorem, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(M>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean cubic subproblems with a direction-independent regularization coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An isotropic cubic model is \[q_M(s)=c+g^Ts+\frac12s^THs+\frac{M}{6}\|s\|_2^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n.\] It is isotropic because for every orthogonal matrix \(Q\), \(\|Qs\|_2^3=\|s\|_2^3\); under the coordinate change \(s=Qz\), the regularizer remains \(M\|z\|_2^3/6\). A global minimizer \(s_*\) is characterized by \[g+Hs_*+\frac{M}{2}\|s_*\|_2s_*=0,\qquad H+\frac{M}{2}\|s_*\|_2I\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An isotropic cubic model is a quadratic function plus a scalar multiple of the cube of the Euclidean norm. The cubic penalty is invariant under every orthogonal change of coordinates and therefore applies the same regularization geometry in all directions. A global minimizer satisfies cubic stationarity and positive semidefiniteness of the Hessian shifted by the scalar \((M/2)\|s_*\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining regularizer is \((M/6)\|s\|_2^3\), invariant under \(s\mapsto Qs\) for every orthogonal \(Q\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(\lambda=(M/2)\|s_*\|_2\), the optimality system becomes \((H+\lambda I)s_*=-g\), \(H+\lambda I\succeq0\), and \(\lambda=(M/2)\|s_*\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=0\) and \(g\ne0\), the minimizer is antiparallel to \(g\) and has norm \(\sqrt{2\|g\|_2/M}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The model is coercive for every symmetric \(H\), including indefinite matrices.
boundary_notes: Direction-dependent norms or tensor regularizers are anisotropic models and are excluded.

notation.meaning: scalar spectral shift induced by the minimizer norm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong duality and primal recovery from an interior dual maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's local notation for the isotropic cubic subproblem value function v, dual function ψ, curvature matrix H, minimum eigenvalue H_min, and auxiliary quantities G² and τ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that \(G^2=0\) and that the dual problem admits a maximizer \(\lambda^*>-H_{\min}\). Then
\[
\min_{h\in\mathbb R^n}v(h)=\max_{\lambda\in\operatorname{dom}\psi\cap\mathbb R_+}\psi(\lambda).
\]
Moreover,
\[
h_*=-(H+\lambda^*I_n)^{-1}g
\]
is a global minimizer of the primal problem, and
\[
\tau(\lambda^*)=\frac{4\lambda^*|\lambda^*|}{M^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If G squared is zero and the dual has a maximizer strictly above the singular boundary minus H_min, then strong duality holds. The shifted linear-system solution is a global primal minimizer, and τ has the stated value at the dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{h\in\mathbb R^n}v(h)=\max_{\lambda\in\operatorname{dom}\psi\cap\mathbb R_+}\psi(\lambda),\qquad -(H+\lambda^*I_n)^{-1}g\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathbb R^n}v(h),\qquad \tau(\lambda^*)=\frac{4\lambda^*|\lambda^*|}{M^2}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the canonical Euclidean cubic model, its unconstrained minimization problem, and the notation for a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $g\in\mathbb R^n$, a symmetric matrix $H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $M>0$, define
\[
v(h)=\langle g,h\rangle+\frac12\langle Hh,h\rangle+\frac{M}{6}\|h\|^3,\qquad h\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
The associated auxiliary problem is
\[
\min_{h\in\mathbb R^n}v(h),
\]
and a global minimizer is denoted by $h_*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector g, a symmetric matrix H, and a positive parameter M, the isotropic cubic model is the linear-quadratic function augmented by M/6 times the cube of the Euclidean norm. Its auxiliary problem minimizes this model over all of R^n, and h* denotes a global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity condition for the exact isotropic cubic-model minimizer in the standing norm geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable, \(M>0\), \(x\in\mathbb E\), and \(T=T_M(x)\). With \(r_M(x)=\|T_M(x)-x\|\),
\[
\nabla f(x)+\nabla^2f(x)(T-x)+\frac12Mr_M(x)B(T-x)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cubic Newton step satisfies stationarity of the cubic-regularized quadratic model: the gradient, Hessian step, and radial cubic term sum to zero.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the minimized second-order Taylor model augmented by a cubic term in the ambient norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be twice differentiable on a vector space equipped with norm \(\|\cdot\|\). For \(M>0\) and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), define
\[
\bar f_M(x)=\min_y\left[f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac12\bigl(\nabla^2f(x)(y-x),y-x\bigr)+\frac{M}{6}\|y-x\|^3\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The value bar f sub M at x is the minimum of the second-order Taylor model at x augmented by M times the cube of the step norm divided by six.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian and dual function for the extracted constrained formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Lagrangian and dual function of the displayed constrained problem only. It does not assert equivalence with the cubic-regularized quadratic subproblem, multiplier nonnegativity, a dual optimization problem, or strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $g\in\mathbb R^n$, let $H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, and let $M>0$. Define
\[
\widetilde v(h,\tau)=\langle g,h\rangle+\tfrac12\langle Hh,h\rangle+\tfrac{M}{12}|\tau|^3,
\qquad
f(h,\tau)=\tfrac12\|h\|^2-\tfrac12\tau.
\]
For the displayed problem
\[
\min_{h\in\mathbb R^n,\,\tau\in\mathbb R}\{\widetilde v(h,\tau):f(h,\tau)\le0\},
\]
define
\[
\mathcal L(h,\tau,\lambda)=\widetilde v(h,\tau)+\lambda f(h,\tau),
\qquad (h,\tau,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
\psi(\lambda)=\inf_{h\in\mathbb R^n,\,\tau\in\mathbb R}\mathcal L(h,\tau,\lambda).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the displayed constrained formulation, the Lagrangian is its objective plus lambda times its inequality function, and the dual function is the infimum of that Lagrangian over h and tau. The extract defines lambda over the entire real line and makes no equivalence or duality-gap claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(h,\tau,\lambda)=\widetilde v(h,\tau)+\lambda f(h,\tau),\qquad \psi(\lambda)=\inf_{h\in\mathbb R^n,\,\tau\in\mathbb R}\mathcal L(h,\tau,\lambda)

\]

children.title: Anisotropic Cubic Model Family
children.top_down_role: Anisotropic cubic regularization and metric selection.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(H=H^T\), \(\sigma>0\), and let \(W=W^T\succ0\) define \(\|s\|_W=(s^TWs)^{1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional cubic models whose regularization geometry is induced by a fixed positive-definite metric at the current iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The metric-induced anisotropic cubic model is \[q_{\sigma,W}(s)=c+g^Ts+\frac12s^THs+\frac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_W^3.\] A uniformly nondegenerate anisotropic family \(\{W_k\}\) satisfies constants \(0<\underline w\leq\overline w<\infty\) such that \[\underline w I\preceq W_k\preceq\overline w I\quad\text{for every }k.\] For \(s\ne0\), stationarity of the model is \[g+Hs+\sigma\|s\|_W Ws=0.\] The family is genuinely anisotropic when some \(W_k\) is not a scalar multiple of \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An anisotropic cubic model replaces the Euclidean cubic penalty by the cube of a metric norm \(\|s\|_W\). The positive-definite matrix \(W\) changes the penalty with direction. Uniform spectral lower and upper bounds keep the metric norm equivalent to the Euclidean norm throughout the iteration sequence. Stationarity contains the direction-dependent factor \(Ws\), unlike the scalar radial term in an isotropic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining cubic term is \((\sigma/3)(s^TWs)^{3/2}\) with \(W\succ0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under \(z=W^{1/2}s\), the cubic term becomes \((\sigma/3)\|z\|_2^3\), while the linear and quadratic terms transform to \((W^{-1/2}g)^Tz\) and \(z^TW^{-1/2}HW^{-1/2}z/2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(W=\alpha I\) with \(\alpha>0\), the model is isotropic after replacing \(\sigma\) by \(\sigma\alpha^{3/2}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Uniform metric bounds imply \(\underline w^{3/2}\|s\|_2^3\leq\|s\|_W^3\leq\overline w^{3/2}\|s\|_2^3\).
boundary_notes: Indefinite or singular \(W\) is excluded because it does not define a norm.
No specific metric-selection or complexity theorem is asserted.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Cubic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cubic regularization in a prescribed symmetric positive-definite scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and define \(\|s\|_D=(s^{\mathsf T}Ds)^{1/2}\). A scaled cubic model at \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is \[m_D(s)=f(x)+g^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\frac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_D^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n,\] where \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sigma>0\). With the coordinate change \(z=D^{1/2}s\), the regularizer becomes \(\sigma\|z\|_2^3/3\), while the linear and quadratic coefficients become \(D^{-1/2}g\) and \(D^{-1/2}BD^{-1/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled cubic model measures step length in a fixed positive-definite metric and becomes isotropic after the associated coordinate transformation.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Cubic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent metric form of anisotropic cubic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each iteration \(k\), let \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and define \(\|s\|_{M_k}=(s^{\mathsf T}M_ks)^{1/2}\). A variable-metric cubic model is \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks+\frac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_{M_k}^3,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n,\] with \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sigma_k>0\). Unlike a fixed scaled model, \(M_k\) may depend on the iteration history, but it must be fixed while the current subproblem is solved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric cubic model changes the positive-definite norm defining cubic regularization from one iteration to the next.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks+\tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_{M_k}^3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Conditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform metric equivalence needed to transfer Euclidean cubic-complexity estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence of symmetric metrics \((M_k)\) is uniformly conditioned relative to the Euclidean norm when constants \(0<\underline\mu\le\overline\mu<\infty\), independent of \(k\), satisfy \[\underline\mu I\preceq M_k\preceq\overline\mu I\qquad\text{for every }k.\] Equivalently, \(\sqrt{\underline\mu}\|s\|_2\le\|s\|_{M_k}\le\sqrt{\overline\mu}\|s\|_2\) for every \(s\in\mathbb R^n\) and every \(k\). Hence \(\|s\|_{M_k}^3\) and \(\|s\|_2^3\) are uniformly equivalent, with constants \(\underline\mu^{3/2}\) and \(\overline\mu^{3/2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform eigenvalue bounds make every variable metric—and its cubic regularizer—uniformly equivalent to the Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline\mu^{3/2}\|s\|_2^3\le\|s\|_{M_k}^3\le\overline\mu^{3/2}\|s\|_2^3\) for all \(k\) and \(s\).

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform norm equivalence when metric eigenvalues vanish or diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M_k=\operatorname{diag}(k^{-2},1,\ldots,1)\) and \(s=e_1\), one has \(\|s\|_{M_k}^3=k^{-3}\) while \(\|s\|_2^3=1\); thus no positive uniform lower-equivalence constant exists. For \(M_k=\operatorname{diag}(k^2,1,\ldots,1)\), no finite uniform upper-equivalence constant exists. Therefore, if \(\lambda_{\min}(M_k)\downarrow0\) or \(\lambda_{\max}(M_k)\uparrow\infty\), Euclidean step-size and decrease estimates cannot be transferred through fixed metric-equivalence constants; any standard complexity proof using such constants requires additional control or a different geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing or unbounded metric eigenvalues destroy uniform comparison with Euclidean cubic regularization, breaking complexity arguments that rely on fixed norm-equivalence constants.
assumptions_latex: Complexity transfer is attempted through iteration-independent norm-equivalence constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_k\lambda_{\min}(M_k)=0\) or \(\sup_k\lambda_{\max}(M_k)=\infty\) precludes uniform two-sided Euclidean norm equivalence.

children.title: Fixed-Parameter Cubic Regularization
children.top_down_role: Methods using a prescribed regularization scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Parameter Cubic Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or approximate cubic regularization with a prescribed scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a fixed \(\sigma>0\), at iteration \(k\) form \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+
abla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}s+ rac12s^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f(x_k)s+ rac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3.\] Compute a global minimizer, or a step satisfying specified first- and second-order subproblem conditions, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). Stop when the chosen stationarity test holds, for example \(\|
abla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\). If \(
abla^2 f\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L\) and \(\sigma\ge L/2\), Taylor's bound gives \(f(x_k+s)\le m_k(s)\) for every \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-parameter method repeatedly minimizes a cubic Taylor model using one prescribed regularization coefficient, without acceptance-driven parameter updates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), where \(s_k\) approximately minimizes \(m_k\); if \(\sigma\ge L/2\), then \(f(x_k+s)\le m_k(s)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind for the fixed-parameter method leaf, and the majorization threshold sigma at least L/2 is correct under the conventional Hessian-Lipschitz bound with cubic Taylor remainder L||s||^3/6. No source is supplied, however, and the alternative approximate-step conditions are not specified sufficiently to associate the algorithm with an authoritative variant.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz Hessian on a set containing the generated iterates, and choose a prescribed constant \(M>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-Hessian, exact-subproblem cubic regularization with one coefficient used at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fixed-parameter cubic-regularization iteration is \[s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\frac12s^T\nabla^2f(x_k)s+\frac{M}{6}\|s\|^3\right\},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k,\] where the same \(M\) is used for all \(k\). The majorizing fixed-parameter regime additionally requires \(M\geq L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-parameter cubic method chooses one positive cubic coefficient \(M\) before the iteration and repeatedly moves to a global minimizer of the corresponding cubic Taylor model. When the Hessian is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(M\geq L\), the model majorizes the objective at its trial point, so no acceptance ratio or parameter search is needed in the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient sequence is constant, \(M_k\equiv M\), and every update satisfies \(x_{k+1}=T_M(x_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(\sigma=M/2\), the fixed regularizer is \((\sigma/3)\|s\|^3\) at every iteration.
special_cases_latex: The choice \(M=L\) is the canonical fixed coefficient when an exact Hessian Lipschitz constant is known.
immediate_consequences_latex: In the majorizing regime, \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)\).
boundary_notes: Iteration-dependent backtracking or ratio-based updates are not fixed-parameter methods.
The definition does not address inexact derivative data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice differentiability and M>0 do not by themselves justify the extract's assertion that the minimizer is unique. The mapping is therefore retained as an argmin set; uniqueness requires additional conditions not stated in the item. The stationarity formula also uses the extract's norm-associated operator B.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be twice differentiable, let \(M>0\), and let \(f_2(x;y)\) denote the second-order Taylor approximation of \(f\) at \(x\). Define
\[
T_M(x):=\operatorname*{Arg\,min}_{y\in\mathbb E}
\left\{f_2(x;y)+\frac{M}{6}\lVert y-x\rVert^3\right\}.
\]
For any \(T\in T_M(x)\) at which the norm-cubic term has the derivative represented in the extract by \(B\), the first-order stationarity condition is
\[
\nabla f(x)+\nabla^2f(x)(T-x)+\frac{M}{2}\lVert T-x\rVert B(T-x)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice differentiable function and fixed positive M, the cubic regularization mapping is the set of minimizers of the second-order Taylor model plus M/6 times the cubed step norm. Any minimizer satisfies the displayed stationarity condition under the extract's norm geometry. The stated assumptions alone do not ensure uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: f_2(x;y)\text{ is the second-order Taylor approximation of }f\text{ at }x
B\text{ represents the derivative geometry of the norm-cubic term as in the extract}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_M(x):=\operatorname*{Arg\,min}_{y\in\mathbb E}\left\{f_2(x;y)+\frac{M}{6}\lVert y-x\rVert^3\right\},\quad T\in T_M(x)\Longrightarrow \nabla f(x)+\nabla^2f(x)(T-x)+\frac{M}{2}\lVert T-x\rVert B(T-x)=0

children.title: Adaptive Regularization with Cubics
children.top_down_role: Acceptance-controlled cubic regularization with adaptive scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Regularization with Cubics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-ratio cubic regularization with multiplicative parameter adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\sigma_0>0\), thresholds \(0<\eta_1\le\eta_2<1\), and factors \(\gamma_1>1\), \(\gamma_2>1\). At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks+\tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_2^3\), obtaining positive predicted reduction. Set \(\rho_k=(f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k))/(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k))\). If \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Decrease \(\sigma_k\) after very successful iterations, keep or moderately adjust it after successful iterations, and set \(\sigma_{k+1}\ge\gamma_1\sigma_k\) after rejection. Stop at the prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ARC accepts steps by actual-to-predicted reduction and adapts cubic regularization downward after strong agreement and upward after rejection.
assumptions_latex: Each computed step has positive predicted reduction.
Parameter updates preserve a fixed positive lower bound on \(\sigma_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) exactly when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), with \(\sigma_k\) adapted according to agreement quality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and high-level acceptance architecture fit the ARC leaf. The parameter-update intervals and permitted adjustments vary across ARC formulations, and no authoritative algorithm locator is supplied to support this particular version.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(\sigma_k>0\). Fix \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\) and update factors \(0<\gamma_1<1<\gamma_2\leq\gamma_3\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic ARC with a quadratic base model, cubic regularization, ratio-based acceptance, and interval-valued parameter updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks+\frac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|^3,\qquad T_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\frac12s^TB_ks.\] Compute a step \(s_k\) giving sufficient reduction of \(m_k\), and set \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{T_k(0)-T_k(s_k)}.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. Choose \(\sigma_{k+1}\in[\gamma_1\sigma_k,\sigma_k]\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\), \(\sigma_{k+1}\in[\sigma_k,\gamma_2\sigma_k]\) if \(\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2\), and \(\sigma_{k+1}\in[\gamma_2\sigma_k,\gamma_3\sigma_k]\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ARC constructs a cubic model with a positive coefficient \(\sigma_k\), compares actual objective decrease with the decrease predicted by the unregularized quadratic part, accepts sufficiently successful trials, and adapts \(\sigma_k\) according to the ratio. Very successful iterations may decrease regularization, ordinary successful iterations keep or moderately increase it, and unsuccessful iterations increase it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining mechanism couples the acceptance rule \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\) with a success-dependent update of \(\sigma_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k\) for all \(k\), the mechanism reduces to fixed-parameter cubic regularization with an acceptance test.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every rejected trial leaves the iterate unchanged and increases \(\sigma_k\) by at least the factor \(\gamma_2\).
boundary_notes: Different ARC sources permit slightly different update intervals and sufficient-decrease conditions.
This definition does not specify an inner stopping certificate.
review_flags: No inspected source supplied an exact locator for this complete ratio and interval-update convention.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(\sigma>0\), and define \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global certificates for an isotropic Euclidean cubic subproblem; approximate certificates form a separate child topic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact solver-certificate pair is \((s,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_+\) satisfying \[(H+\lambda I)s=-g,\qquad H+\lambda I\succeq0,\qquad \lambda=\sigma\|s\|.\] A solver is certificate-producing when it returns such a pair. The vector component \(s\) is then a global minimizer of \(q\), including cases in which \(H\) is indefinite or \(H+\lambda I\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact certificate consists of a step and a nonnegative scalar shift. The shifted linear system enforces stationarity, positive semidefiniteness certifies the correct curvature branch, and the scalar equation couples the shift to the step norm. Together these conditions characterize global solutions of the cubic subproblem rather than merely stationary points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate relation is \((H+\lambda I)s=-g\), \(H+\lambda I\succeq0\), and \(\lambda=\sigma\|s\|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \(\lambda\) yields \(g+Hs+\sigma\|s\|s=0\) and \(H+\sigma\|s\|I\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: When \(H+\lambda I\succ0\), the certified step is uniquely \(s=-(H+\lambda I)^{-1}g\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any certified shift satisfies \(\lambda\geq\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(H)\}\).
boundary_notes: Stationarity without the shifted positive-semidefinite condition does not certify global optimality.
The certificate permits nonunique steps in singular hard cases.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral secular-equation solver for cubic subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3\), where \(H=Q\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)Q^T\), \(d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_n\), and \(u=Q^Tg\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact high-accuracy solvers based on an eigendecomposition and a scalar secular equation, including the singular hard case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the nonsingular branch, a spectral-secular solver finds \(\lambda>\max\{0,-d_1\}\) satisfying \[\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{u_i^2}{(d_i+\lambda)^2}\right)^{1/2}=\frac{\lambda}{\sigma},\] and returns \[s=-Q\operatorname{diag}\big((d_i+\lambda)^{-1}\big)u.\] The admissible root must also satisfy \(H+\lambda I\succeq0\). On the singular hard-case branch \(\lambda=-d_1\geq0\), one uses the pseudoinverse solution plus a vector in \(\ker(H+\lambda I)\), chosen so that \(\|s\|=\lambda/\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral-secular solver diagonalizes the Hessian and reduces the nonlinear optimality system to one scalar equation for the spectral shift \(\lambda\). Once an admissible root is found, each spectral component of the step is obtained by dividing the corresponding gradient component by \(d_i+\lambda\). If the admissible shift lies at the smallest-eigenvalue boundary, a nullspace component supplies the required norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver returns \((s,\lambda)\) satisfying the exact cubic certificate through the secular equation and the shifted spectral representation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The secular equation is \(\|(H+\lambda I)^{-1}g\|=\lambda/\sigma\) on the positive-definite branch.
special_cases_latex: If \(u_i\ne0\) for some \(i\) with \(d_i=d_1\), the admissible solution cannot use the singular boundary \(\lambda=-d_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: After an eigendecomposition, evaluation of the scalar secular function requires only the eigenvalues and transformed gradient components.
boundary_notes: The inverse formula is invalid at a singular shift and must be replaced by a pseudoinverse-plus-nullspace construction.
This definition does not prescribe a particular scalar root-finding tolerance.

notation.meaning: gradient expressed in the eigenbasis of \(H\)

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Cubic Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal-eigenbasis representation of the isotropic cubic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_s q(s)\), where \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3\), \(B=B^{\mathsf T}=Q\Lambda Q^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\sigma>0\). With \(z=Q^{\mathsf T}s\) and \(h=Q^{\mathsf T}g\), the problem is exactly \[\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\;h^{\mathsf T}z+\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i z_i^2+\frac{\sigma}{3}\|z\|_2^3.\] At a global minimizer there exists \(\lambda=\sigma\|z\|_2\ge0\) such that \((\lambda_i+\lambda)z_i=-h_i\) for every \(i\), and \(\lambda_i+\lambda\ge0\). Thus the multidimensional problem reduces to a scalar shift plus diagonal solves, including separate treatment of singular hard cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonalizing the Hessian reduces the isotropic cubic subproblem to diagonal shifted equations coupled by one scalar norm-consistency condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B+\lambda I)s=-g\), \(B+\lambda I\succeq0\), and \(\lambda=\sigma\|s\|_2\) characterize a global solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Secular Cubic Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar root-finding for the regular cubic-subproblem case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)Q^{\mathsf T}\), \(h=Q^{\mathsf T}g\), and \(\sigma>0\), seek a shift \(\lambda>\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(B)\}\). Define \(z_i(\lambda)=-h_i/(\lambda_i+\lambda)\) and the secular residual \[\phi(\lambda)=\|z(\lambda)\|_2-\frac{\lambda}{\sigma}.\] Use safeguarded bisection or Newton interpolation on a bracket containing a zero of \(\phi\). When \(|\phi(\lambda)|\) meets the prescribed tolerance, return \(s=Qz(\lambda)\). If no regular root exists because the limiting shifted matrix is singular, invoke a hard-case correction in the eigenspace of \(\lambda_{\min}(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A secular solver finds the scalar shift equating shifted-system step length with the cubic consistency value, then reconstructs the step spectrally.
assumptions_latex: \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) and its spectral decomposition is available.
The regular case admits a root above the singular shift boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s=Qz(\lambda)\) satisfies \((B+\lambda I)s=-g\) and \(\lambda=\sigma\|s\|_2\) up to the root tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-point equation and lower bound for the cubic step length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the norm of a global cubic-subproblem minimizer under an invertible shifted-curvature representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h_*\) be a global minimizer of \(v\), and assume that there exists \(\lambda^*>-H_{\min}\) such that
\[
h_*=-(H+\lambda^*I_n)^{-1}g.
\]
Define \(r=\|h_*\|\). Then
\[
r=\frac{2}{M}\lambda^*,
\qquad
r=\left\|\left(H+\frac{Mr}{2}I_n\right)^{-1}g\right\|,
\]
and
\[
r\geq\frac{2}{M}\bigl(-\lambda_{\min}(H)\bigr)_+.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a global cubic step has an invertible shifted-system representation, its norm equals twice the multiplier divided by M, satisfies the displayed scalar fixed-point equation, and is no smaller than the negative-curvature threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r=\frac{2\lambda^*}{M}=\left\|\left(H+\frac{Mr}{2}I_n\right)^{-1}g\right\|,\qquad r\geq\frac{2}{M}\bigl(-\lambda_{\min}(H)\bigr)_+.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual first-order condition and primal recovery for a cubic subproblem

Let
\[
\lambda^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\operatorname{dom}\psi\cap\mathbb R_+}\psi(\lambda),
\]
and assume that \(\lambda^*>-H_{\min}\). Then
\[
\left\|(H+\lambda^*I_n)^{-1}g\right\|=\frac{2}{M}\lambda^*.

Moreover,
\[
h_*=-(H+\lambda^*I_n)^{-1}g
\]
is a global minimizer of \(v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Shifted-System Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cubic-subproblem solution through repeated symmetric shifted linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the cubic model \(q(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|_2^3\), initialize a bracket for \(\lambda\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(B)\}\). At each scalar iteration, solve or approximately solve \[(B+\lambda I)s(\lambda)=-g,\] compute \(r(\lambda)=\sigma\|s(\lambda)\|_2-\lambda\), and update the bracket or a safeguarded Newton step according to the sign and derivative information. Return \(s(\lambda)\) when both the shifted-system residual and \(|r(\lambda)|\) satisfy prescribed tolerances. If \(B+\lambda I\) is singular, detect the null space and apply the appropriate hard-case correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sigma>0\). knowledge_statements.title: Lanczos Cubic Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a Euclidean cubic model onto a Lanczos basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\), with \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), \(g\ne0\), and \(\sigma>0\). After \(j\) Lanczos steps initialized by \(q_1=g/\lVert g\rVert\), let \(Q_j=[q_1,\ldots,q_j]\) have orthonormal columns and \(T_j=Q_j^{\mathsf T}HQ_j\). Every \(s\in\operatorname{range}(Q_j)\) has the unique form \(s=Q_jy\), and orthonormality gives
\[m(Q_jy)=\lVert g\rVert e_1^{\mathsf T}y+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}T_jy+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert y\rVert^3.\]
Thus minimizing the full cubic model over the Lanczos subspace is exactly equivalent to solving this \(j\)-dimensional cubic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos projection replaces the full Hessian by a symmetric tridiagonal matrix while preserving the linear term and Euclidean cubic regularizer exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_j\) is generated by exact-arithmetic Lanczos iteration from \(g/\lVert g\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{s\in\operatorname{range}(Q_j)}m(s)=\min_{y\in\mathbb R^j}m(Q_jy)\) with the displayed tridiagonal reduced model.

children.title: Krylov Cubic Subspaces

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov Cubic Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested Hessian-gradient spaces used for matrix-free cubic-model minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a symmetric matrix \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), a vector \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and an integer \(j\ge1\), the order-\(j\) Krylov cubic subspace is
\[\mathcal K_j(H,g)=\operatorname{span}\{g,Hg,\ldots,H^{j-1}g\}.\]
A Krylov cubic iterate is any minimizer or approximate minimizer of \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\) over \(\mathcal K_j(H,g)\). These spaces are nested, \(\mathcal K_j(H,g)\subseteq\mathcal K_{j+1}(H,g)\), and can be generated using Hessian-vector products without forming \(H\). If the Krylov sequence becomes linearly dependent, the subspaces stabilize at an \(H\)-invariant space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Krylov cubic method minimizes the cubic model over nested spaces generated by repeated Hessian actions on the model gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_j(H,g)\subseteq\mathcal K_{j+1}(H,g)\), with stabilization when the generating sequence becomes linearly dependent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Krylov-subspace definition specialized to a cubic model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly describes the nested Krylov spaces and their stabilization, and definition is the appropriate content kind. knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Cubic Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or certified solution of the projected cubic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an orthonormal basis \(Q_j\), reduced matrix \(T_j=Q_j^{\mathsf T}HQ_j\), reduced gradient \(h_j=Q_j^{\mathsf T}g\), and \(\sigma>0\), solve
\[\min_{y\in\mathbb R^j}\;\widehat m_j(y)=h_j^{\mathsf T}y+\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}T_jy+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert y\rVert^3.\]
Compute \((y_j,\lambda_j)\) satisfying \((T_j+\lambda_jI)y_j=-h_j\), \(T_j+\lambda_jI\succeq0\), and \(\lambda_j=\sigma\lVert y_j\rVert\), using a spectral-secular solve or its singular hard-case completion. Return \(s_j=Q_jy_j\); for an inexact solve, stop only when prescribed reduced stationarity, curvature, and model-decrease tolerances are met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the projected cubic optimality system in reduced coordinates, then lift the solution through the orthonormal Krylov basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is \(s_j=Q_jy_j\), where \(y_j\) solves or certifiably approximates the reduced cubic model.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reduced cubic optimality conditions are the full cubic conditions applied to the projected model

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Cubic-Solution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware inner-solve conditions commonly sufficient for cubic-regularization complexity analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\), an approximate cubic-solution certificate with constants \(\kappa_g,\kappa_H\ge0\) consists of a step \(s\) satisfying
\[m(s)\le m(0),\qquad \lVert g+Hs+\sigma\lVert s\rVert s\rVert\le\kappa_g\lVert s\rVert^2,\qquad H+\sigma\lVert s\rVert I\succeq-\kappa_H\lVert s\rVert I.\]
The first inequality certifies nonpositive predicted change; the second gives scale-compatible approximate stationarity; and the third bounds failure of the shifted positive-semidefiniteness condition. An outer complexity theorem may replace these inequalities by stronger conditions, but must specify constants uniformly over iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified inexact cubic step has nonpositive model change, quadratic-scale stationarity residual, and linearly scaled shifted-curvature error.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(g,s\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities provide verifiable model-decrease, stationarity, and shifted-curvature certificates for the inner solve.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual, curvature, and decrease certificate for an inexact cubic step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3\), where \(H=H^T\) and \(\sigma>0\). Fix tolerances \(\kappa_r,\kappa_c\geq0\) and \(\kappa_d>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic inexact Euclidean cubic subproblem solutions described by scale-aware residual, curvature, and model-decrease tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonzero step \(s\) is \((\kappa_r,\kappa_c,\kappa_d)\)-certified when \[\|g+Hs+\sigma\|s\|s\|\leq\kappa_r\|s\|^2,\] \[\lambda_{\min}(H+\sigma\|s\|I)\geq-\kappa_c\|s\|,\] and \[q(0)-q(s)\geq\kappa_d\sigma\|s\|^3.\] The first inequality measures approximate cubic stationarity, the second permits only controlled violation of the shifted curvature condition, and the third prevents acceptance of a nearly stationary step with negligible model reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate cubic-solution certificate combines three independently checkable properties: the model-gradient residual is at most quadratic in the step norm, the shifted Hessian is positive semidefinite up to a step-scaled tolerance, and model decrease is at least a positive multiple of the natural cubic scale \(\sigma\|s\|^3\). special_cases_latex: Setting \(\kappa_r=\kappa_c=0\) recovers the exact first- and second-order certificate, while the decrease condition remains explicit.
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual tolerance is invariant under comparing quantities at the natural stationarity scale \(\|s\|^2\).

The zero step requires a separate termination convention and is excluded here.

children.title: Cubic Subproblem Degeneracy Classes

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3\), let \(d_1=\lambda_{\min}(H)\), and let \(E_1=\ker(H-d_1I)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact isotropic cubic subproblems classified by whether the optimal shifted Hessian is nonsingular or singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certified global solution \((s_*,\lambda_*)\) is regular when \(H+\lambda_*I\succ0\). It is boundary-degenerate when \(H+\lambda_*I\succeq0\) is singular. The hard case is the boundary-degenerate class satisfying \[\lambda_*=-d_1\geq0,\qquad g\perp E_1.\] In that class, writing \(A=H-d_1I\), solutions have the form \[s_*=-A^\dagger g+z,\\ z\in E_1,	frac{}{}\qquad \|s_*\|=\frac{-d_1}{\sigma}.\] Such a solution exists when \(\|A^\dagger g\|\leq(-d_1)/\sigma\); the nullspace component supplies the remaining squared norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic subproblem is regular when its optimal spectral shift makes the shifted Hessian positive definite. It is boundary-degenerate when the optimal shift lies at the smallest-eigenvalue boundary. The hard case additionally requires the gradient to be orthogonal to the smallest-eigenvalue eigenspace. The step then consists of a pseudoinverse particular solution plus a smallest-eigenvalue component whose length enforces the cubic norm equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hard-case defining relations are \(\lambda_*=-\lambda_{\min}(H)\), \(g\perp E_1\), and \(s_*=-A^\dagger g+z\) with \(z\in E_1\) and \(\|s_*\|=\lambda_*/\sigma\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The hard case is exactly the singular-shift branch of the certificate \((H+\lambda I)s=-g\), \(H+\lambda I\succeq0\), and \(\lambda=\sigma\|s\|\).
special_cases_latex: If \(g=0\) and \(d_1<0\), every vector \(s\in E_1\) with \(\|s\|=-d_1/\sigma\) is a global minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonuniqueness occurs when the admissible set of nullspace components contains more than one vector.
boundary_notes: A singular shifted matrix is not by itself sufficient for the hard case; compatibility \(g\perp E_1\) is required.
When \(d_1\geq0\) and \(g=0\), the zero solution is a different degenerate stationary case.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Cubic Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singularity of the shifted curvature matrix at a cubic global solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\), with \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sigma>0\). A global solution \(s_*\) has degenerate cubic curvature when, for \(\lambda_*:=\sigma\lVert s_*\rVert\),
\[(H+\lambda_*I)s_*=-g,\qquad H+\lambda_*I\succeq0,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(H)+\lambda_*=0.\]
Equivalently, the shifted matrix required by the cubic global-optimality system is positive semidefinite but singular. When \(s_*\ne0\), the model Hessian adds the rank-one term \(\sigma s_*s_*^{\mathsf T}/\lVert s_*\rVert\); hence degeneracy of \(H+\lambda_*I\) need not imply singularity of the complete model Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate cubic curvature occurs when the optimal shifted Hessian is positive semidefinite but singular.
assumptions_latex: \(s_*\) is a global minimizer of the cubic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\sigma\lVert s_*\rVert I\succeq0\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(H)+\sigma\lVert s_*\rVert=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: singularity is the boundary case of the shifted positive-semidefiniteness optimality condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbed secular equation in the degenerate boundary case
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The displayed source equation uses λ as its scalar argument; here it is evaluated at the stated optimal dual point λ_δ^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that \(G^2=0\), the unperturbed dual maximizer occurs at \(\lambda^*=-H_{\min}\), \(k\in I^*\), and \(\delta>0\). For
\[
v_\delta(h)=v(h)+\delta h^{(k)},
\]
the optimal dual point \(\lambda_\delta^*\) satisfies
\[
\frac{\delta^2}{(H_{\min}+\lambda_\delta^*)^2}+\sum_{i\notin I^*}\frac{(g^{(i)})^2}{(H_i+\lambda_\delta^*)^2}=\frac{4(\lambda_\delta^*)^2}{M^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the unperturbed degenerate cubic subproblem has its dual optimum at the singular boundary, a positive linear perturbation along a minimum-curvature eigendirection yields an optimal dual point satisfying the displayed secular equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\delta^2}{(H_{\min}+\lambda_\delta^*)^2}+\sum_{i\notin I^*}\frac{(g^{(i)})^2}{(H_i+\lambda_\delta^*)^2}=\frac{4(\lambda_\delta^*)^2}{M^2}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing-perturbation recovery of a degenerate cubic minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the source's local spectral notation I*, H_i, H_min, and e_i. The limit is taken through positive perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(k\in I^*\). For \(\delta>0\), define
\[
v_\delta(h)=v(h)+\delta h^{(k)},
\]
and let
\[
h_*(\delta)=-(H+\lambda_\delta^*I_n)^{-1}(g+\delta e_k)
\]
be a global minimizer of \(v_\delta\) for its corresponding optimal dual point \(\lambda_\delta^*\). Then the limit as \(\delta\downarrow0\) exists and equals
\[
h_*=\sum_{i\notin I^*}\left(-\frac{g^{(i)}}{H_i-H_{\min}}\right)e_i+h_*^{(k)}e_k,
\qquad
h_*^{(k)}=-\left[\frac{4H_{\min}^2}{M^2}-\sum_{i\notin I^*}\frac{(g^{(i)})^2}{(H_i-H_{\min})^2}\right]^{1/2}.
\]
Moreover, \(h_*\) is a global minimizer of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global minimizers of the positively perturbed cubic subproblems converge as the perturbation vanishes. The limit has the stated spectral-coordinate formula and is a global minimizer of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}h_*(\delta)=\sum_{i\notin I^*}\left(-\frac{g^{(i)}}{H_i-H_{\min}}\right)e_i-\left[\frac{4H_{\min}^2}{M^2}-\sum_{i\notin I^*}\frac{(g^{(i)})^2}{(H_i-H_{\min})^2}\right]^{1/2}e_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathbb R^n}v(h).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Cubic Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-case parametrization of all global minimizers sharing a singular multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m(s)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\lVert s\rVert^3\), and suppose \(\lambda_*=-\lambda_{\min}(H)>0\), \(g\in\operatorname{range}(H+\lambda_*I)\), and \(p:=-(H+\lambda_*I)^\dagger g\) satisfies \(\lVert p\rVert\le\lambda_*/\sigma\). Then every vector
\[s_*=p+z,\qquad z\in\ker(H+\lambda_*I),\qquad \lVert z\rVert^2=(\lambda_*/\sigma)^2-\lVert p\rVert^2\]
is a global minimizer. Conversely, every global minimizer associated with this singular multiplier has this form. The solution is nonunique precisely when the right-hand radius is positive, because the nullspace sphere then contains at least two points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the hard case, all minimizers are a pseudoinverse solution plus a nullspace vector of prescribed norm; positive nullspace radius causes nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed nullspace sphere is exactly the set of global minimizers associated with \(\lambda_*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of uniqueness at a boundary dual optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An explicit two-dimensional isotropic cubic subproblem showing that boundary attainment of the dual optimum can coexist with multiple global primal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist cubic subproblems with multiple global minimizers and a dual optimum attained at the boundary. In particular, for
\[
n=2,\qquad g=(-1,0)^\top,\qquad H=\operatorname{diag}(0,-1),\qquad M=1,
