knowledge_statements.statement_title: Higher-derivative complexity family for first-order criticality
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R,\quad p\ge2,\quad \epsilon\in(0,1),\quad \phi_{f,1}^{1}(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth optimization using derivatives through order (p) while requiring only first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A higher-derivative bound for a first-order target is a worst-case evaluation estimate for a degree-(p) method, with \(p\ge2\), whose stopping set is
\[\mathcal X_{1}(\epsilon)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\epsilon\}.\]
For a problem class \(\mathcal F_{p,\beta}\), define
\[N_{p,1}(\epsilon)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{p,\beta}}\inf\{k\ge0:x_k\in\mathcal X_1(\epsilon)\}.\]
A bound belongs to this family when \(N_{p,1}(\epsilon)\le C_{p,\beta}\epsilon^{-a_{p,1,\beta}}+C'_{p,\beta}\), where evaluations may include \(f\) and derivatives through order \(p\), while the target itself uses only the gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This complexity family concerns methods that may evaluate high derivatives and construct high-degree models but terminate as soon as the gradient norm is at most ε. Its worst-case count is the maximum over the stated smoothness class of the first evaluation index attaining that gradient condition. Constants may depend on the derivative order and smoothness class, but not on ε.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{p,1}(\epsilon)\le C_{p,\beta}\epsilon^{-a_{p,1,\beta}}+C'_{p,\beta},\qquad p\ge2,\quad\mathcal X_1(\epsilon)=\{x:\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\epsilon\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using radius \(\delta=1\), the stopping condition is \(\phi_{f,1}^{1}(x)\le\epsilon\).
special_cases_latex: For \(p=2\), the family covers regularized quadratic or cubic-regularization models targeting a small gradient.
For \(p=3\), third derivatives may inform the step although stationarity remains first order.
immediate_consequences_latex: The target order is fixed at one, so negative curvature is not itself part of the termination requirement.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert a particular optimal exponent.
The cost of forming or contracting derivative tensors is outside an evaluation-only count unless explicitly included.

notation.meaning: worst-case evaluation count for reaching the first-order target using degree-p information

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Derivative Bounds for Second-Order Targets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong second-order complexity with separate gradient and curvature tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\geq2\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below, and assume that its derivatives through order \(p\) are Lipschitz continuous on the relevant level set. A degree-\(p\) strong adaptive regularization method reaches \(x\) satisfying
\[
\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\epsilon_1,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\geq-\epsilon_2
\]
within
\[
O\!\left(\max\left\{\epsilon_1^{-\frac{p+1}{p}},\epsilon_2^{-\frac{p+1}{p-1}}\right\}\right)
\]
evaluations of the objective and its derivatives through order \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree-p regularization attains gradient and curvature tolerances with the maximum of the first-order and second-order evaluation exponents.
assumptions_latex: Derivatives \(\nabla^j f\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), are Lipschitz continuous on the relevant level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The evaluation count is \(O(\max\{\epsilon_1^{-(p+1)/p},\epsilon_2^{-(p+1)/(p-1)}\})\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R,\quad p\ge2,\quad \epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in(0,1),\quad \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\text{ denotes the least Hessian eigenvalue}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained optimization with curvature-aware termination and models using derivatives through order (p).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A higher-derivative bound for a second-order target is a worst-case evaluation estimate for reaching
\[\mathcal X_2(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)=\{x:\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\epsilon_1,\ \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\ge-\epsilon_2\}.\]

\[N_{p,2}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{p,\beta}}\inf\{k\ge0:x_k\in\mathcal X_2(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\}.\]
A two-tolerance bound is any uniform estimate \(N_{p,2}\le B_{p,2}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\) with tolerance-independent problem-class constants. A single-tolerance convention fixes a declared relation between \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family measures the evaluations needed by a method using derivatives through order p to reach a point with both a small gradient and almost no negative Hessian curvature. knowledge_statements.title: Third-Order Target Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong third-order bound at the transition \(q=3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\geq3\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below, and suppose its derivatives through order \(p\) are Lipschitz continuous. For tolerances \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3\in(0,1)\), a strong order-three adaptive regularization method finds \(x\) and admissible radii satisfying
\[
\phi_{f,j}^{\delta_j}(x)\leq\epsilon_j\frac{\delta_j^j}{j!},
\qquad j=1,2,3,
\]
within
\[
O\!\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq3}\epsilon_j^{-\frac{3(p+1)}{p}}\right)
\]
evaluations. This is the first strong-criticality order governed by the \(q>2\) exponent rather than the sharper separate low-order exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For strong third-order criticality, the known general bound changes to the q-greater-than-two regime, giving exponent 3(p+1)/p for each tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Derivatives through order \(p\) are Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong third-order criticality is obtained in \(O(\max_{1\leq j\leq3}\epsilon_j^{-3(p+1)/p})\) evaluations.

\[\phi_{f,3}^{\delta}(x)=f(x)-\min_{\|d\|\le\delta}T_{f,3}(x,d).\]

\[\phi_{f,3}^{\delta_k}(x_k)\le\epsilon\chi_3(\delta_k),\qquad \chi_3(\delta)=\delta+\frac{\delta^2}{2}+\frac{\delta^3}{6},\]

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A third-order target bound counts evaluations until the maximum decrease predicted by the cubic Taylor polynomial on a declared radius is at most ε times a radius normalization. The method must have access to derivatives through at least order three, though it may use a still higher-degree model. This target is distinct from merely requiring a small gradient and an almost positive-semidefinite Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: General Criticality-Order Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong arbitrary-order evaluation bounds for Lipschitz-smooth regularized models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\leq q\leq p\), let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be bounded below, and assume derivatives through order \(p\) are Lipschitz continuous. For strong tolerances \(\epsilon_j\), a degree-\(p\) adaptive regularization method reaches
\[
\phi_{f,j}^{\delta_j}(x)\leq\epsilon_j\frac{\delta_j^j}{j!},
\qquad j=1,\ldots,q.
\]
For \(q\in\{1,2\}\), the evaluation bound is
\[
O\!\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\epsilon_j^{-\frac{p+1}{p-j+1}}\right).
\]
For \(q>2\), the general smooth non-composite bound is
\[
O\!\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\epsilon_j^{-\frac{q(p+1)}{p}}\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong arbitrary-order regularization has separate sharp exponents for orders one and two, while orders above two obey the general q(p+1)/p exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(1\leq q\leq p\) and \(f\) is bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed piecewise bounds control evaluations of \(f\) and all derivatives through order \(p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Arbitrary-Order Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order evaluation complexity for deterministic regularized Taylor methods using derivatives through order \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\geq 1\), and consider deterministic algorithms whose iterations use values of \(f\) and its derivatives through order \(p\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below and \(\nabla^p f\) is Lipschitz continuous. Regularized \(p\)-th order Taylor methods attain an iterate \(x\) satisfying \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\epsilon\) after at most \(O(\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p})\) evaluations of these quantities. In the corresponding deterministic \(p\)-th order oracle model, worst-case function families require \(\Omega(\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p})\) evaluations, so the exponent \((p+1)/p\) is sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For first-order stationarity, regularized order-p Taylor methods have worst-case evaluation complexity proportional to epsilon raised to minus (p+1)/p, and this exponent is oracle-optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the relevant level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_p(\epsilon)=\Theta(\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p})\) in the stated deterministic oracle model.

Oracle-model details and dimension dependence need source verification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of an arbitrary-order evaluation bound
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[\mathfrak A_{p,q}\text{ is an algorithm class},\quad \mathcal F_{p,\beta}\text{ is a smooth objective class},\quad \epsilon\downarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-based worst-case sharpness for a fixed oracle model, problem class, model degree, and target criticality order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An arbitrary-order rate \(R_{p,q}(\epsilon)\) is sharp for \((\mathfrak A_{p,q},\mathcal F_{p,\beta})\) when matching upper and lower evaluation bounds hold up to positive constants: there exist \(c,C>0\) and \(\epsilon_0>0\) such that
\[\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{p,q}}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{p,\beta}}N(\mathcal A,f,\epsilon)\le C R_{p,q}(\epsilon)\]
and
\[\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{p,q}}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{p,\beta}}N(\mathcal A,f,\epsilon)\ge c R_{p,q}(\epsilon)\]
for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0\). Equivalently, the minimax evaluation complexity is \(\Theta(R_{p,q}(\epsilon))\) under the same oracle, target, and smoothness conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrary-order complexity bound is sharp when its ε dependence is matched by a worst-case lower bound over the same objective class and algorithmic oracle model. Thus no algorithm in the declared class can improve the asymptotic rate by more than a constant factor, and some algorithm achieves that rate. Changing the oracle or target changes the sharpness claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{p,q}}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_{p,\beta}}N(\mathcal A,f,\epsilon)=\Theta\!\left(R_{p,q}(\epsilon)\right)\quad(\epsilon\downarrow0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a power rate \(R_{p,q}(\epsilon)=\epsilon^{-a_{p,q}}\), sharpness means matching upper and lower tolerance exponents \(a_{p,q}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Realization of a regularized higher-order model subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[m_{x,\sigma}(s)=T_{f,p}(x,s)+\frac{\sigma}{r}\|s\|^r,\qquad p\ge2,\quad r>p,\quad \sigma>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional computation of acceptable steps for nonconvex regularized Taylor models; exact and certified inexact realizations are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A higher-order subproblem realization is a procedure \(\mathcal S\) that maps the finite model data \((\nabla f(x),\ldots,\nabla^p f(x),\sigma)\) and requested inner tolerances to a step \(s=\mathcal S(x,\sigma)\) carrying a verifiable model certificate. An exact realization returns
\[s\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb R^n}m_{x,\sigma}(u).\]
An inexact realization returns a step satisfying a declared conjunction such as
\[m_{x,\sigma}(s)<m_{x,\sigma}(0),\qquad \|\nabla_s m_{x,\sigma}(s)\|\le\eta_g\|s\|^{r-1},\]
possibly supplemented by higher-order model-criticality conditions. The realization includes both the computational route and the certificate checked by the outer regularization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher-order subproblem realization is a concrete mapping from Taylor-derivative data and a regularization parameter to a model step, together with conditions that the outer algorithm can verify. It may globally minimize the regularized polynomial, or it may return an inexact step with strict model decrease and a scaled small model gradient, optionally with stronger criticality certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S:(\nabla f(x),\ldots,\nabla^p f(x),\sigma,\eta)\mapsto s\quad\text{with a declared certificate }\mathcal C(m_{x,\sigma},s,\eta)=\mathrm{true}.\]
special_cases_latex: Global model minimization is the idealized exact realization.
Convexification and nested lower-order optimization are distinct computational realizations when they deliver the required certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Outer evaluation guarantees can be stated independently of inner arithmetic only when the certificate, rather than a particular solver, is assumed.
boundary_notes: Strict model decrease and small model gradient need not certify global optimality for a nonconvex polynomial.
This definition does not assign an inner iteration or bit-complexity bound.
review_flags: The precise certificate sufficient for the intended outer arbitrary-order method requires a dedicated source.
knowledge_statements.title: Realization of a regularized higher-order model subproblem

children.title: Conceptual Global Model Minimization

knowledge_statements.title: Conceptual Global Model Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized exact solution of each regularized Taylor subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), order \(p\geq1\), and \(\sigma_k>0\), form \(m_k(s)=T_p(x_k,s)+\frac{\sigma_k}{p+1}\|s\|^{p+1}\), where \(T_p(x_k,s)=f(x_k)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{1}{j!}\nabla^j f(x_k)[s]^j\). Select any global minimizer \(s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb{R}^n}m_k(s)\). Evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\), accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when the prescribed actual-to-predicted reduction test succeeds, and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\); update \(\sigma_k\) by the acceptance rule and stop at the required criticality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration globally minimizes the regularized Taylor model, tests the resulting trial point by actual versus predicted decrease, and updates the regularization parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\) is a globally optimal model step and is passed to the outer acceptance mechanism.

notation.meaning: order-p Taylor polynomial of the objective at x
regularized Taylor model at iteration k

review_flags: A higher-order regularization reference with the precise idealized subproblem rule is needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conceptual global minimization of a regularized Taylor model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[m_{x,\sigma}(s)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{1}{j!}\nabla^j f(x)[s]^j+\frac{\sigma}{r}\|s\|^r,\qquad r>p,\quad\sigma>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized exact treatment of each unconstrained regularized polynomial subproblem in evaluation-complexity analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Conceptual global model minimization selects, at every outer iterate \(x\), a step from the complete global minimizer set
\[S^*(x,\sigma)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R^n}m_{x,\sigma}(s).\]
The conceptual step rule is any selection \(s(x,\sigma)\in S^*(x,\sigma)\). The regularization term is chosen so that \(m_{x,\sigma}(s)\to+\infty\) as \(\|s\|\to\infty\), making the minimizer set nonempty for continuous finite-dimensional models. The word conceptual indicates that the global solve is an analytical assumption used to define an outer iteration or evaluation count, not a claim that the polynomial minimization is computationally efficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conceptual global model minimization means choosing an actual global minimizer of the regularized Taylor model at every outer iteration. Coercive regularization ensures that such a minimizer exists in finite dimensions. The definition deliberately idealizes the inner computation and therefore supports evaluation-complexity reasoning without asserting an efficient implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k\in S^*(x_k,\sigma_k)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R^n}m_{x_k,\sigma_k}(s)\quad\text{for every outer iteration }k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[m_{x,\sigma}(s_k)=\inf_{s\in\mathbb R^n}m_{x,\sigma}(s).\]
special_cases_latex: For \(p=2\) and \(r=3\), this is global minimization of a cubicly regularized quadratic model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The selected step has model value no larger than \(m_{x,\sigma}(0)=f(x)\).
boundary_notes: First- or second-order stationarity of the model is not equivalent to global minimization when the model is nonconvex.
No polynomial-time or finite inner-iteration guarantee is included.

notation.meaning: set of global minimizers of the regularized model

review_flags: The supplied source hints do not provide a precise locator for arbitrary-order regularized-model global minimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Higher-Order Solution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable inner conditions replacing exact global model minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m_k(s)=T_p(x_k,s)+ rac{\sigma_k}{p+1}\|s\|^{p+1}\), a step \(s_k
eq0\) has an approximate first-order model certificate with parameter \(	heta\geq0\) when \(m_k(s_k)<m_k(0)\) and \(\|
abla_s m_k(s_k)\|\leq	heta\|s_k\|^p\). If second-order outer guarantees are required, additionally demand \(\lambda_{\min}(
abla_s^2m_k(s_k))\geq-	heta\|s_k\|^{p-1}\). These inequalities are computable from the model and certify decrease together with scale-consistent approximate first- or second-order stationarity of the inner subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-decreasing step is acceptable when its model gradient, and optionally its negative curvature, is small relative to the natural powers of the step length.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is twice differentiable at \(s_k\) when the second-order condition is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual inequalities certify scale-consistent approximate stationarity of the regularized model.

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

review_flags: A source is needed to match these inner conditions to a specific outer evaluation-complexity theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and scale-dependent residuals fit the leaf. However, no cited theorem establishes which outer evaluation-complexity result is preserved by these exact first- and second-order inner conditions, including the permitted range of theta and any required model-decrease constants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled approximate solution certificate for a higher-order model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[m(s)=T_{f,p}(x,s)+\frac{\sigma}{r}\|s\|^r,\qquad p\ge2,\quad r>p,\quad \sigma>0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact inner solution of a differentiable regularized Taylor subproblem, certified by decrease and scale-aware model criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given tolerances \(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_q\ge0\) and a radius \(\delta_s>0\), an approximate order-(q) solution certificate for the model is a step \(s\) satisfying strict or prescribed model decrease together with
\[m(s)\le m(0)-\Delta_m,\qquad \phi_{m,q}^{\delta_s}(s):=m(s)-\min_{\|d\|\le\delta_s}T_{m,q}(s,d)\le\eta_q\chi_q(\delta_s),\]
where \(\Delta_m\ge0\) is declared by the outer method. A common first-order scaled certificate is
\[m(s)<m(0),\qquad \|\nabla m(s)\|\le\theta\|s\|^{r-1}.\]
The scaling prevents a fixed absolute inner tolerance from overwhelming the model decrease as \(s\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate higher-order solution certificate is a checkable set of inequalities attached to an inexact model step. It combines sufficient model decrease with a bound on the remaining Taylor decrease of the model around that step. At first order this is often a model-gradient residual proportional to a power of the step norm. The exact tolerances and certificate order must be declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s\text{ is certified}\iff m(s)\le m(0)-\Delta_m\quad\text{and}\quad\phi_{m,q}^{\delta_s}(s)\le\eta_q\chi_q(\delta_s).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q=1\), \(\phi_{m,1}^{\delta_s}(s)=\delta_s\|\nabla m(s)\|\).
special_cases_latex: Setting all tolerances to zero yields an exact Taylor-criticality certificate, but not necessarily a global-minimizer certificate.
Taking \(q=1\) produces a scaled first-order residual test.
immediate_consequences_latex: A certificate can serve as a solver-independent interface between the inner and outer algorithms.
boundary_notes: The definition does not claim that every displayed certificate is sufficient for every outer complexity theorem.
Local model criticality does not in general establish global optimality.

notation.meaning: order-q Taylor-decrease residual of the model at the candidate step

review_flags: The intended outer theorem must be sourced before fixing the exact sufficient certificate and scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled approximate solution certificate for a higher-order model

knowledge_statements.title: Convexified Tensor Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification on a prescribed convex region using a weak-convexity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(q:C	o\mathbb{R}\) be a twice-differentiable tensor-polynomial model satisfying \(
abla^2q(s)\succeq-ho I\) for every \(s\in C\), where \(ho\geq0\). For any center \(s_0\in C\), define \(\widehat q(s)=q(s)+ rac{ho}{2}\|s-s_0\|^2\). Then \(
abla^2\widehat q(s)=
abla^2q(s)+ho I\succeq0\) on \(C\), so \(\widehat q\) is convex there. Minimizing \(\widehat q\) over \(C\) is therefore a convex auxiliary subproblem, although its minimizer need not minimize the original nonconvex model \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A twice-differentiable tensor polynomial with curvature bounded below by minus rho becomes convex on the region after adding a quadratic term of curvature rho.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is twice differentiable with \(\nabla^2q(s)\succeq-\rho I\) on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat q=q+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\cdot-s_0\|^2\) is convex on \(C\).
review_flags: An authoritative source specialized to convexification of tensor or higher-order polynomial subproblems is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexification of a tensor Taylor subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[P_x(s)=\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{1}{j!}\nabla^j f(x)[s]^j,\qquad s\in\mathbb R^n,\quad p\ge2.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional auxiliary-model construction in which an added regularizer makes a higher-order polynomial objective convex on its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convexified tensor subproblem is an optimization problem
\[\min_{s\in D}\ \widehat m_x(s),\qquad \widehat m_x(s)=P_x(s)+R_x(s),\]
where \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex, \(R_x:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a declared convexifying regularizer, and
\[\widehat m_x(\tau u+(1-\tau)v)\le\tau\widehat m_x(u)+(1-\tau)\widehat m_x(v)\]
for all \(u,v\in D\) and \(\tau\in[0,1]\). If twice differentiable, this condition is equivalently \(\nabla^2\widehat m_x(s)\succeq0\) throughout \(D\). The construction is a realization of the original tensor model only when the resulting step also satisfies the outer method’s required decrease and accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convexified tensor subproblem adds a specified regularizer to a Taylor polynomial built from multilinear derivative tensors so that the complete auxiliary objective is convex on a convex domain. Convexity may be stated by Jensen’s inequality or, for a twice differentiable model, by a positive-semidefinite Hessian everywhere. Acceptance by an outer method remains a separate certificate requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat m_x=P_x+R_x\text{ is a convexified tensor model on }D\iff D\text{ is convex and }\widehat m_x\text{ is convex on }D.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\widehat m_x\in C^2(D)\) on an open convex domain, convexity is equivalent to \(\nabla^2\widehat m_x(s)\succeq0\) for every \(s\in D\).
special_cases_latex: For quadratic \(P_x\), adding a sufficiently large quadratic term shifts the Hessian to positive semidefiniteness.
A convex domain restriction may be represented by adding its convex indicator to \(R_x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every local minimizer of the convexified auxiliary model is global on \(D\).
boundary_notes: A high even-power norm regularizer does not automatically convexify an arbitrary polynomial globally; convexity must be established for the chosen coefficient and domain.
Convexifying an auxiliary model may change its minimizers relative to the original nonconvex model.

notation.meaning: unregularized Taylor polynomial excluding its constant term
convexifying regularizer or extended-valued convex term

review_flags: A source specific to convexified higher-order tensor subproblems is needed to identify the intended regularizer family.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexification of a tensor Taylor subproblem

children.title: Nested Lower-Order Solves
children.top_down_role: Realization of higher-order models through lower-order inner optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Lower-Order Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic realization of a higher-order step through certified lower-order inner iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a differentiable higher-order model \(m:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(z_0=0\). At inner iteration \(i\), construct a lower-order regularized model \(\ell_i(d)=m(z_i)+\nabla m(z_i)^\top d+\frac12d^\top B_i d+\frac{\tau_i}{r}\|d\|^r\), where \(B_i\) is available lower-order curvature information, \(\tau_i>0\), and \(r>2\). Approximately minimize \(\ell_i\), accept a trial displacement \(d_i\) using decrease in \(m\), and set \(z_{i+1}=z_i+d_i\). Terminate when \(m(z_i)<m(0)\) and \(\|\nabla m(z_i)\|\leq\theta\|z_i\|^p\); return \(s=z_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner regularization method repeatedly solves lower-order models until the resulting higher-order step has model decrease and a scale-consistent residual certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is continuously differentiable and bounded below on the inner level set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(s\) satisfies \(m(s)<m(0)\) and \(\|\nabla m(s)\|\leq\theta\|s\|^p\).

notation.meaning: inner iterate representing a candidate outer step

review_flags: This generic nested scheme requires a source specifying convergence and total inner-work guarantees.
The lower-order solver and acceptance rule are intentionally abstract.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the nested-solve leaf, but the lower-order solver, acceptance test, curvature model, and parameter update are not specified sufficiently to define a particular algorithm. The assumptions do not establish finite termination at the displayed certificate or any inner-work guarantee. A concrete nested method and convergence theorem are required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested lower-order realization of a higher-order model step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is a regularized degree-}p\text{ model},\qquad 1\le\ell<p.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner iterative realization of a higher-order regularized model using subproblems whose local models require derivatives only through order (ℓ<p).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nested lower-order solve for \(m\) is an inner sequence \(z_0=0,z_1,\ldots,z_J=s\) generated by an order-(\ell) solver \(\mathcal B_\ell\):
\[z_{j+1}=\mathcal B_\ell\bigl(z_j;m,\eta_j\bigr),\qquad \ell<p,\]
where each inner subproblem uses derivatives of \(m\) with respect to its variable only through order \(\ell\). Termination occurs at the first \(J\) for which the outer-model certificate \(\mathcal C(m,z_J,\eta)=\mathrm{true}\). The nested construction realizes the higher-order step precisely when \(s=z_J\) satisfies that certificate; merely running a lower-order method on \(m\) is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested lower-order solve treats the higher-order regularized polynomial as an inner optimization objective and applies an iterative solver whose local subproblems use fewer derivative orders. The final inner iterate becomes the outer step only after it meets the higher-order model certificate required by the outer algorithm. The inner iteration count is distinct from the outer objective-evaluation count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s=z_J,\qquad z_{j+1}=\mathcal B_\ell(z_j;m,\eta_j),\quad \ell<p,\qquad \mathcal C(m,z_J,\eta)=\mathrm{true}.\]
special_cases_latex: A first-order inner solver has \(\ell=1\) and uses model gradients or tensor-vector contractions.
A second-order inner solver has \(\ell=2\) and solves quadratic or regularized quadratic local models of \(m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The realization separates outer evaluations of \(f\) from repeated inner evaluations of the already constructed model \(m\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not imply that the nested procedure is polynomial-time.
If evaluation of an inner derivative of \(m\) requires expensive tensor contractions, derivative order alone does not describe arithmetic cost.

notation.meaning: inner solver using local derivative information through order ℓ
outer-compatible terminal certificate for the higher-order model

review_flags: No inspected source in the supplied list formalizes this nested realization and its outer-compatible certificate.

children.title: Polynomial Subproblem Hardness
children.top_down_role: Computational barriers separating evaluation theory from implementability.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Subproblem Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational obstruction to treating exact polynomial-model minimization as a unit-cost operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational quartic polynomial \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), deciding whether \(q(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is NP-hard. Consequently, exact global minimization of general quartic polynomial models, or even deciding whether their global infimum is negative, cannot be assumed polynomial-time solvable unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). Thus an evaluation-complexity result that counts an exact global polynomial-model minimization as one iteration does not by itself yield a polynomial arithmetic-complexity implementation; additional structure, relaxation, or approximate certificates are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General quartic global optimization is NP-hard, so evaluation counts based on exact polynomial subproblem solves do not automatically imply efficient implementations.
assumptions_latex: Polynomial coefficients are rational and encoded in binary.
Complexity is measured in the standard Turing model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A polynomial-time exact solver for all such quartic subproblems would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).
review_flags: An authoritative computational-complexity theorem locator for quartic nonnegativity or global minimization is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf. The quartic nonnegativity and global-minimization consequences require an authoritative theorem and precise reduction, including whether the polynomial is homogeneous, whether boundedness is promised, and exactly which decision problem is NP-hard. No source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Computational hardness of a polynomial model subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[P:\mathbb Q^n\to\mathbb Q\text{ is represented by rational coefficients or an equivalent finite encoding},\qquad D\subseteq\mathbb R^n.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity distinction between solving a regularized polynomial subproblem and counting outer evaluations of a smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a class \(\mathcal P\u0001_p\) of encoded degree-(p) polynomial models, define the decision version of global subproblem solution by
\[\operatorname{PolyMinDec}_p(P,D,\alpha)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{YES},&\inf_{s\in D}P(s)\le\alpha,\\\mathrm{NO},&\inf_{s\in D}P(s)>\alpha.\end{cases}\]
The polynomial subproblem class is computationally hard under a specified reduction when this decision problem is hard for the corresponding complexity class as a function of the bit length of \((P,D,\alpha)\). Approximation hardness instead fixes a gap or accuracy convention and asks whether a polynomial-time procedure can return \(s\) with \(P(s)-\inf_D P\le\eta\). Any hardness designation must state the degree, domain, encoding, approximation criterion, and reduction notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial subproblem hardness is a bit-complexity property of the encoded global minimization problem. Its decision form asks whether the minimum of a degree-p polynomial on a stated domain is at most a rational threshold. An approximation-hardness claim must additionally specify the permitted error or decision gap. This is separate from outer evaluation complexity, which may treat the model solve as conceptual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{PolyMinDec}_p:(P,D,\alpha)\mapsto\mathbf 1\{\inf_{s\in D}P(s)\le\alpha\},\quad\text{with hardness defined relative to an explicit encoding and reduction}.\]
special_cases_latex: Quadratic trust-region subproblems form a structurally special class and should not be identified with unrestricted polynomial minimization.
Fixed-degree and variable-degree inputs define different computational families.
immediate_consequences_latex: An outer evaluation bound that assumes exact global model minimization does not by itself yield an implementable polynomial-time method.
boundary_notes: No particular NP-hardness threshold is asserted here.
Hardness of exact global minimization does not preclude efficient certified approximate steps sufficient for an outer method.

notation.meaning: decision problem associated with global degree-p polynomial minimization

review_flags: A complexity-theory source is required before attaching a specific hardness class or degree threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Computational hardness of a polynomial model subproblem

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R,\quad j\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\quad \nabla^j f(x)\in\operatorname{Sym}^j(\mathbb R^n).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional oracle interfaces for obtaining multilinear derivative information without requiring dense tensor materialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A higher-derivative oracle representation of order \(p\) is a family \(\mathcal O^{(1)},\ldots,\mathcal O^{(p)}\) such that, for every query point \(x\) and admissible vectors, its outputs determine the symmetric multilinear forms \(\nabla^j f(x)\). Permitted interfaces include
\[\mathcal O_{m full}^{(j)}(x)=\nabla^j f(x),\qquad \mathcal O_{m prod}^{(j)}(x;v_1,\ldots,v_{j-1})=\nabla^j f(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_{j-1},\cdot],\]
and
\[\mathcal O_{m dir}^{(j)}(x;v)=\nabla^j f(x)[v]^j.\]
A representation is sufficient for a method only if every contraction and certificate used by that method can be obtained from its permitted queries. Query complexity must therefore name the interface being counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher-derivative oracle representation specifies how an algorithm accesses each symmetric derivative multilinear form. It may return the full tensor, a tensor-vector contraction, or only a repeated-direction scalar derivative. The representation is adequate only when it can supply all quantities used to build the model and verify the stopping conditions. Counts under different interfaces are not automatically comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal O^{(j)}\text{ represents }\nabla^j f(x)\iff\text{its declared query outputs equal the corresponding contractions of }\nabla^j f(x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: By polarization, exact access to all directional values of a symmetric multilinear form determines that form, although the number and cost of queries remain representation-dependent.
special_cases_latex: For \(j=1\), the full and product interfaces both return the gradient.
For \(j=2\), the product interface is a Hessian-vector product.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dense-storage complexity, contraction complexity, and oracle-query complexity become distinct resource measures.
boundary_notes: Noisy, stochastic, finite-difference, and approximate derivative oracles require additional error conditions and are excluded.
Information equivalence does not imply equal computational cost.

notation.meaning: space of symmetric j-linear forms on ℝⁿ
oracle returning a partially contracted jth derivative
oracle returning a repeated-direction scalar contraction

review_flags: The supplied local hints do not establish this complete oracle taxonomy or its exact interfaces.

children.title: Explicit Derivative Tensors
children.top_down_role: Dense, sparse, and structured storage of multilinear derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Derivative Tensors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate storage and contraction of symmetric higher derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) of class \(C^p\), the \(j\)-th derivative at \(x\) is the symmetric tensor \(A^{(j)}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times\cdots\times n}\) with entries \(A^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)=\frac{\partial^j f(x)}{\partial x_{i_1}\cdots\partial x_{i_j}}\). Its multilinear action is \(\nabla^j f(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_j]=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_j=1}^n A^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)\prod_{r=1}^j(v_r)_{i_r}\). Dense storage uses \(n^j\) entries, while symmetry permits storage of at most \(\binom{n+j-1}{j}\) distinct entries; sparsity or structure can reduce this further.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit order-j derivative is a symmetric coordinate tensor whose contraction gives every multilinear derivative value; dense storage grows as the jth power of dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{(j)}(x)\) explicitly represents \(\nabla^j f(x)\), with symmetric storage size at most \(\binom{n+j-1}{j}\).

notation.meaning: coordinate array of the jth derivative
multilinear contraction of the jth derivative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit coordinate representation of derivative tensors
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is }p\text{-times continuously differentiable near }x,\qquad 1\le j\le p.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coordinate storage of exact higher derivatives as dense, sparse, or structured symmetric arrays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The explicit order-(j) derivative tensor of \(f\) at \(x\) in a chosen basis is the symmetric array
\[G^{(j)}(x)=\bigl(G^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)\bigr)_{1\le i_1,ow i_j\le n},\qquad G^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)=\frac{\partial^j f(x)}{\partial x_{i_1}\cdots\partial x_{i_j}},\]
representing the multilinear form through
\[\nabla^j f(x)[v_1,ow v_j]=\sum_{i_1,ow i_j=1}^{n}G^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)(v_1)_{i_1}ow(v_j)_{i_j}.\]
The representation is dense when all entries are stored, sparse when only indexed nonzeros are stored, and structured when entries are encoded by a declared factorization or symmetry-preserving parameterization from which exact contractions can be recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit derivative tensor is the coordinate array of all order-j partial derivatives in a chosen basis. Contracting this array with j vectors reproduces the j-linear derivative. Dense storage lists every entry, sparse storage lists only indexed nonzeros, and structured storage gives an exact factorization or parameterization supporting reconstruction or contraction. Symmetry follows from the stated smoothness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[G^{(j)}_{i_1\ldots i_j}(x)=\partial_{i_1}\cdots\partial_{i_j}f(x),\qquad \nabla^j f(x)[v_1,ow v_j]=\langle G^{(j)}(x),v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_j\rangle.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tensor is equivalently the coordinate representation of the Fréchet derivative \(D^j f(x)\) in the chosen basis.
special_cases_latex: For \(j=1\), \(G^{(1)}\) is the gradient vector.
For \(j=2\), \(G^{(2)}\) is the symmetric Hessian matrix.
immediate_consequences_latex: A dense order-(j) array has \(n^j\) indexed entries, while symmetry permits storage by unordered multi-indices.
Changing basis changes the coordinates but not the represented multilinear map.
boundary_notes: A tensor-vector-product oracle that never materializes coordinates is not an explicit tensor representation.
Approximate compression requires an error model and is not covered by the exact definition.

notation.meaning: coordinate array representing the jth derivative at x
rank-one tensor product of the contraction vectors

children.title: Tensor-Product Oracles
children.top_down_role: Multilinear contractions without full tensor assembly.

knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Product Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free oracle for multilinear contractions of a higher derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(j\)-times differentiable. A product oracle for \(\nabla^j f(x)\) accepts \(x\) and vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\in\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(0\leq r\leq j\), and returns the partially contracted \((j-r)\)-linear form \(\mathcal{O}_{j,r}(x;v_1,\ldots,v_r)=\nabla^j f(x)[v_1,\ldots,v_r,\cdot,\ldots,\cdot]\). For \(r=j\) the output is scalar, and for \(r=j-1\) it is identified with a vector by the Euclidean inner product. The oracle need not assemble or store the full order-\(j\) tensor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tensor-product oracle returns partial or complete contractions of a derivative tensor directly, avoiding construction of the full multidimensional array.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{O}_{j,r}\) exposes the required tensor contraction without requiring explicit tensor assembly.

notation.meaning: order-j derivative product oracle with r contracted arguments

review_flags: A source formalizing the higher-derivative product-oracle model is required.

children.title: Directional Higher-Order Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Higher-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle returning repeated-direction contractions used by Taylor models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(p\)-times differentiable. A directional higher-order oracle accepts \((x,v,j)\) with \(x,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(1\leq j\leq p\), and returns \(D_v^j f(x)=\left.\frac{d^j}{dt^j}f(x+tv)\right|_{t=0}=\nabla^j f(x)[v]^j\). Hence the Taylor polynomial along \(v\) is \(T_p(x,v)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{1}{j!}D_v^j f(x)\). Repeated-direction information alone does not directly provide arbitrary mixed contractions unless additional polarization queries or structural assumptions are supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional oracle returns each derivative contracted repeatedly with one direction, giving the coefficients of the Taylor model along that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_v^j f(x)=\nabla^j f(x)[v]^j\), and these values determine \(T_p(x,v)\).

notation.meaning: order-p Taylor polynomial evaluated at displacement v

source_refs.locator: 1.4.5 The directional derivative of \( f\left( \mathbf{x}\right) \) in the direction \( \mathbf{u} \) p. 23

children.title: Constructed Higher-Order Oracle Family
children.top_down_role: Constructed higher-order information from differentiation systems or lower-order evaluations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be \(p\)-times differentiable, and fix an available primitive oracle \(\mathcal O_{\le q}\), where \(0\le q<p\). Write \(\mathbb S^r(\mathbb R^n)\) for the space of symmetric \(r\)-linear forms with induced norm \(\|T\|=\sup_{\|v_i\|\le1}|T[v_1,\ldots,v_r]|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic construction of derivative information of orders above those returned directly by a primitive oracle; explicit stored derivative tensors, tensor-product primitives, and purely directional oracles are neighboring representations rather than assumptions of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constructed higher-order oracle family of maximum order \(p\) based on \(\mathcal O_{\le q}\) is a collection \(\mathfrak C_p=\{(Q_{r,x},R_{r,x}):x\in U,\ q<r\le p\}\). For every \((r,x)\), \(Q_{r,x}=((z_i,\ell_i))_{i=1}^{N_{r,x}}\) is a finite, possibly adaptive query rule with \(z_i\in U\) and \(0\le\ell_i\le q\), and \(R_{r,x}\) maps the resulting primitive responses to \(B_r(x)\in\mathbb S^r(\mathbb R^n)\). The induced oracle is \[\mathcal O^{\mathfrak C}_p(f,x)=\bigl(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^qf(x),B_{q+1}(x),\ldots,B_p(x)\bigr).\] It is exact on a function class \(\mathcal F\) when \(B_r(x)=D^rf(x)\) for every \(f\in\mathcal F\), \(x\in U\), and \(q<r\le p\); it is \(\boldsymbol\delta\)-accurate when \(\|B_r(x)-D^rf(x)\|\le\delta_r(x)\) for those quantifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constructed higher-order oracle family consists, for each point and each derivative order above the primitive oracle's order, of a finite query rule and a reconstruction map. The rule queries only available lower-order information, and the reconstruction produces a symmetric multilinear form representing the requested higher derivative. The resulting oracle appends these reconstructed forms to the primitive responses. Exactness means that every reconstructed form equals the corresponding derivative on the stated function class; delta-accuracy means that its induced multilinear norm error is bounded by the prescribed order-dependent tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and every query point generated by \(Q_{r,x}\) belongs to \(U\).
\(f\in C^p(U)\), and the primitive oracle returns information only through order \(q<p\).
Each \(Q_{r,x}\) uses finitely many primitive evaluations and each \(R_{r,x}\) has codomain \(\mathbb S^r(\mathbb R^n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak C_p\) defines the induced higher-order information map \(x\mapsto\mathcal O^{\mathfrak C}_p(f,x)\), with exactness characterized by \(B_r(x)=D^rf(x)\) and inexactness by \(\|B_r(x)-D^rf(x)\|\le\delta_r(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accuracy condition is equivalently \(\sup_{\|v_i\|\le1}|(B_r(x)-D^rf(x))[v_1,\ldots,v_r]|\le\delta_r(x)\).
special_cases_latex: When \(q=0\), finite-difference constructions from objective values fit the definition.
When \(q=1\), higher-order forms may be reconstructed from displaced gradient evaluations.
immediate_consequences_latex: For any step \(s\), \(|(B_r(x)-D^rf(x))[s]^r|\le\delta_r(x)\|s\|^r\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a unique construction, query complexity, or stability bound.
Returning only contractions \(D^rf(x)[s]^{r-1}\) without reconstructing an element of \(\mathbb S^r(\mathbb R^n)\) belongs to a directional-oracle variant.

notation.meaning: Finite, possibly adaptive lower-order query rule for constructing order-r information at x.
Reconstruction map from primitive responses to a symmetric r-linear form.
Constructed approximation to the rth derivative.

children.title: Automatic Higher-Order Differentiation
children.top_down_role: Coverage of higher-order information constructed through differentiation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Higher-Order Differentiation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jet propagation for directional derivatives through a computational graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and an integer order \(p\geq1\). Associate each graph variable \(u\) with its truncated jet \(J_pu=(u_0,\ldots,u_p)\), where \(u_j=\left.\frac{d^j}{dt^j}u(x+tv)\right|_{t=0}\). Initialize input jets by \(J_px_i=(x_i,v_i,0,\ldots,0)\). Traverse the computational graph in topological order, applying the exact truncated product and composition rules for every elementary operation. The output jet \(J_pf=(f(x),D_vf(x),\ldots,D_v^pf(x))\) supplies all directional derivatives through order \(p\), up to arithmetic roundoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-order automatic differentiation propagates truncated derivative jets through the program and returns all directional derivatives through the selected order.
assumptions_latex: The computational graph is acyclic and its elementary operations are \(p\)-times differentiable at encountered values.
Exact truncated jet rules are available for every elementary operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output components satisfy \((J_pf)_j=D_v^j f(x)\) for \(0\leq j\leq p\), apart from numerical roundoff.

notation.meaning: order-p univariate derivative jet of graph variable u

review_flags: A higher-order automatic-differentiation reference with jet propagation formulas is required.

children.title: Finite-Difference Higher-Order Oracles
children.top_down_role: Coverage of higher-order information approximated from lower-order evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Higher-Order Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-difference construction of repeated-direction derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an integer derivative order \(j\geq1\), and spacing \(h>0\), query \(f\) at \(x+\ell hv\) for \(\ell=0,\ldots,j\) and return \(\widehat D_{v,h}^jf(x)=h^{-j}\sum_{\ell=0}^j(-1)^{j-\ell}\binom{j}{\ell}f(x+\ell hv)\). If \(t\mapsto f(x+tv)\) has a continuous \((j+1)\)-st derivative on a neighborhood of \([0,jh]\), then \(\widehat D_{v,h}^jf(x)=D_v^jf(x)+O(h)\) as \(h\downarrow0\). The construction uses \(j+1\) function values, some of which may be reused across derivative orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A jth directional derivative can be approximated from j+1 equally spaced function values; the forward formula has first-order truncation error under one additional derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(t\mapsto f(x+tv)\) is \((j+1)\)-times continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \([0,jh]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat D_{v,h}^jf(x)-D_v^jf(x)=O(h)\) as \(h\downarrow0\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3.5. Finite-Difference Approximations to Derivatives p. 54

children.title: Constructed-Oracle Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Coverage of approximation quality available from constructed derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Constructed-Oracle Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-scaled derivative accuracy sufficient to preserve Taylor-model order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let approximate symmetric derivative tensors \(\widetilde A_j(x)\) be used in \(\widetilde T_p(x,s)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{1}{j!}\widetilde A_j(x)[s]^j\). A step-scaled constructed-oracle accuracy condition is that constants \(\kappa_j\geq0\), independent of the current step \(s\), satisfy \(\|\widetilde A_j(x)-\nabla^j f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_j\|s\|^{p+1-j}\) for \(j=1,ldots,p\). Then \(|\widetilde T_p(x,s)-T_p(x,s)|\leq\left(\sum_{j=1}^p\kappa_j/j!\right)\|s\|^{p+1}\), so oracle error has the same order as the regularized Taylor remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the order-j derivative error shrinks like the step norm to power p+1-j, the entire approximate Taylor model remains accurate to order p+1.
assumptions_latex: Tensor errors are measured in the induced multilinear operator norm.
The displayed bounds hold for the candidate step \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde T_p(x,s)-T_p(x,s)|\leq\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{\kappa_j}{j!}\|s\|^{p+1}\).

notation.meaning: constructed approximation to the jth derivative tensor
Taylor model formed from approximate derivatives

review_flags: The bound follows directly from the operator-norm inequalities, but an inexact higher-order regularization source is required for outer-complexity sufficiency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, and the displayed Taylor-model error bound follows consistently from the stated operator-norm inequalities. However, no cited inexact higher-order regularization theorem shows that this step-dependent condition is implementable or sufficient to preserve an outer evaluation-complexity guarantee. The record's broader scope therefore remains source-dependent.

children.title: Oracle Cost Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Coverage of computational tradeoffs between automatic plus finite-difference access.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Cost Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost accounting for a constructed oracle supplying derivatives through order \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N_j\) be the number of calls to an order-\(j\) primitive and let \(c_j>0\) be its prescribed unit cost, for \(j=0,\ldots,p\). The total weighted oracle cost and the unweighted evaluation-complexity vector are respectively
\[
C(N;c)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}c_jN_j,
\qquad
N=(N_0,\ldots,N_p).
\]
Without specified weights, oracle families \(A\) and \(B\) admit only componentwise comparison: \(A\preceq B\) when \(N_j^A\leq N_j^B\) for every \(j\). With fixed weights, their scalar comparison is \(C(N^A;c)\leq C(N^B;c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle costs are compared componentwise unless primitive evaluation weights are fixed; with fixed weights, total cost is the weighted sum of calls by derivative order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(N;c)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}c_jN_j\), with componentwise comparison when the weights are unspecified.

notation.meaning: number of order-j primitive oracle calls
cost assigned to one order-j primitive call

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and componentwise-versus-weighted distinction fit the oracle-cost leaf, but no source supports this particular accounting convention or comparison rule.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of smooth, possibly nonconvex functions on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(\mathcal O_f\) denote exact information, and let \(\widetilde{\mathcal O}(x,\tau,\xi)\) be an approximate response obtained at point \(x\), requested accuracy \(\tau\), and optional random state \(\xi\). Let \(\mu_f(x)\ge0\) be a stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional oracle-complexity framework encompassing deterministic inexact responses and conditionally random responses. A concrete complexity theorem requires a specified algorithm, admissibility relation, cost convention, and stationarity order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An imperfect-information complexity theory is specified by a tuple \(\mathfrak I=(\mathcal F,\widetilde{\mathcal O},\mathcal E,\Pi,c,\mu)\). Here \(\mathcal E(f,x,\widetilde o,\tau)\) is the admissibility predicate relating an approximate response \(\widetilde o\) to exact information about \(f\); \(\Pi\) is a nonanticipating policy selecting requested accuracies from the algorithmic history; and \(c(\widetilde o,\tau)\ge0\) is its information cost. For an algorithm \(A\), define the stopping index \(N_\epsilon=\inf\{k\ge0:\mu_f(X_k)\le\epsilon\}\) and worst-case cost \[\mathcal C_A(\epsilon)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\ \sup_{\widetilde{\mathcal O}:\,\mathcal E\ {m holds}}\ \sum_{k=0}^{N_\epsilon-1}c(\widetilde O_k,\tau_k).\] In the stochastic regime, the inner admissibility requirement is conditional and complexity is recorded through an expectation or tail bound for the same random cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imperfect-information complexity theory is the study of an algorithm relative to a function class, an approximate oracle, an admissibility relation for its errors, a history-dependent accuracy policy, an information-cost convention, and a stationarity measure. Its deterministic evaluation complexity is the largest admissible cumulative information cost incurred before the stationarity measure first falls below the requested tolerance. In a stochastic version, admissibility is conditional on past information and the corresponding cost is summarized by an expectation or probability bound.
assumptions_latex: The policy \(\Pi\) selects \(\tau_k\) using only information available before the current response is generated.
Every oracle response used in the deterministic supremum satisfies \(\mathcal E(f,X_k,\widetilde O_k,\tau_k)\).
The stopping measure \(\mu_f\), response cost \(c\), and convention for an infinite stopping index are fixed before complexity is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_A(\epsilon)\) is the worst-case imperfect-information cost of producing \(X_k\) with \(\mu_f(X_k)\le\epsilon\); stochastic versions replace the deterministic bound by a declared expectation or tail functional of that cost.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every admissible response has unit cost, \(\mathcal C_A(\epsilon)\) reduces to the worst-case number of approximate-oracle calls before \(N_\epsilon\).
special_cases_latex: Fixed absolute error, dynamically requested error, random model accuracy, and inexact inner solves arise by changing \(\mathcal E\), \(\Pi\), and \(c\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two complexity bounds are comparable only after aligning their stationarity measure, response units, and probability interpretation.
boundary_notes: This definition itself asserts no finite bound and no convergence result.
Arithmetic work, sample complexity, derivative evaluations, and outer iterations need not coincide and must be assigned separate cost functions when distinguished.

notation.meaning: First index satisfying the prescribed stationarity tolerance.

children.title: Inexact Information Classes
children.top_down_role: Classifies imperfect information by what is approximated and how its accuracy is controlled.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be smooth. At iteration \(k\), exact information may include \(f(X_k)\), derivatives \(D^jf(X_k)\), trial-point values, and an exact solution of an auxiliary model subproblem. Let \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\) be the history preceding the current information request.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of imperfect information by the object approximated, the mathematical form of its error certificate, and the mechanism controlling accuracy; it does not impose one common norm or probability model on all components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact information class is a triple \(\mathfrak E=(I,E,\Pi)\). The index set \(I\subseteq\{f,Df,D^2f,\ldots,D^pf,{\rm sub}\}\) identifies the exact objects replaced by approximate responses \(\widetilde Z_{k,i}\). For every \(i\in I\), \(E_{k,i}(Z_{k,i},\widetilde Z_{k,i};\tau_{k,i})\le0\) is a declared deterministic error condition, or \[\mathbb P\bigl(E_{k,i}(Z_{k,i},\widetilde Z_{k,i};\tau_{k,i})\le0\mid\mathscr F_{k-1}\bigr)\ge1-\alpha_{k,i}\] is a declared conditional-probability condition. The nonanticipating policy \(\Pi\) selects \((\tau_{k,i},\alpha_{k,i})_{i\in I}\) from \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\) and current computable algorithmic quantities. Two response mechanisms belong to the same class only when they share \(I\), the error predicates and norms encoded by \(E\), and the accuracy-control type encoded by \(\Pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact information class specifies which exact optimization objects are replaced, the error predicate used for each replacement, and the history-dependent rule controlling its tolerance and, when relevant, its failure probability. An error predicate may be deterministic or may be required to hold with a stated probability conditional on the previous algorithmic history. Mechanisms are in the same class only if the approximated components, error metrics, and accuracy-control type agree.
assumptions_latex: Every exact object \(Z_{k,i}\) and approximate response \(\widetilde Z_{k,i}\) lies in a declared common ambient space.
Each error predicate specifies its norm, scaling, or optimality residual explicitly.
The policy \(\Pi\) is measurable with respect to information available before the associated random response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak E=(I,E,\Pi)\) partitions imperfect-information mechanisms according to approximated objects, certified error relations, and accuracy-control rules.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A deterministic class is recovered from the conditional formulation by taking \(\alpha_{k,i}=0\) for all \(k\) and \(i\).
special_cases_latex: \(I=\{f\}\) gives objective-value inexactness.
\(I\subseteq\{Df,D^2f\}\) gives low-order derivative inexactness.
\(I=\{{\rm sub}\}\) gives inexact auxiliary-subproblem solution information.
immediate_consequences_latex: Absolute, relative, model-scaled, dynamically controlled, and probabilistic errors are distinct classes unless their predicates and policies coincide.
boundary_notes: The classification does not by itself imply convergence or an evaluation-complexity rate.
Bias, dependence, and simultaneous-event requirements must be stated inside the relevant error predicate rather than inferred from a marginal bound.

notation.meaning: Set of exact information components replaced by approximations.
Sigma-field representing the algorithmic history before iteration k information is generated.

children.title: Inexact Objective Information

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Objective Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic objective errors controlled relative to the predicted decrease used for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), suppose the algorithm uses approximate values \(\bar f_k\) at \(x_k\) and \(\bar f_k^+\) at \(x_k+s_k\), with predicted model decrease \(D_k>0\). Objective information has acceptance-compatible accuracy with parameter \(\omega\in[0,1)\) when
\[
|\bar f_k-f(x_k)|+|\bar f_k^+-f(x_k+s_k)|\leq \omega D_k.
\]
Consequently, the error in the computed actual reduction \(\bar f_k-\bar f_k^+\) is at most \(\omega D_k\), so acceptance comparisons possess an explicitly bounded additive perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined error in the two objective values is bounded by a fixed fraction of the predicted decrease, controlling error in the acceptance ratio numerator.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite at the evaluated points.
\(D_k>0\) is computable before the acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\big| (\bar f_k-\bar f_k^+)-(f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k))\big|\leq\omega D_k\).

notation.meaning: inexact objective values at the current and trial points

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). An evaluation routine takes a point \(x\in U\) and requested tolerance \(\omega\ge0\), and returns a scalar \(\bar f(x;\omega)\). Acceptance tests may compare values at a current point \(x_k\) and a trial point \(x_k+s_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic absolute objective-value errors used in acceptance and complexity analysis. Relative, biased stochastic, and interval-valued evaluations require separately declared variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The routine supplies \(\omega\)-accurate inexact objective information at \(x\) when \[|\bar f(x;\omega)-f(x)|\le\omega.\] For two evaluations \(\bar f_k=\bar f(x_k;\omega_k)\) and \(\bar f_k^+=\bar f(x_k+s_k;\omega_k^+)\), define the computed objective reduction \(\overline{\Delta f}_k=\bar f_k-\bar f_k^+\) and true reduction \(\Delta f_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\). The pair is admissible inexact objective information when each pointwise bound holds, in which case its defining reduction-error certificate is \[|\overline{\Delta f}_k-\Delta f_k|\le\omega_k+\omega_k^+.\] A dynamically accurate pair additionally requires a declared computable scale \(q_k>0\) and \(\omega_k+\omega_k^+\le\kappa_f q_k\) for a fixed \(\kappa_f\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact objective evaluation with requested absolute accuracy omega returns a scalar within omega of the true objective value. A current-point and trial-point pair is admissible when both individual bounds hold. Its computed reduction then has a certified error no larger than the sum of the two requested tolerances. In the dynamically accurate subclass, that sum must also be bounded by a fixed fraction of a declared positive algorithmic scale, such as a predicted reduction.
assumptions_latex: Both \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) belong to the domain \(U\).
The evaluation tolerances \(\omega_k\) and \(\omega_k^+\) are nonnegative.
For the dynamically accurate subclass, \(q_k\) is computable before the acceptance decision and is strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible objective information satisfies \(|\bar f(x;\omega)-f(x)|\le\omega\), and an admissible evaluation pair satisfies \(|\overline{\Delta f}_k-\Delta f_k|\le\omega_k+\omega_k^+\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The pointwise condition is equivalent to the interval enclosure \(f(x)\in[\bar f(x;\omega)-\omega,\bar f(x;\omega)+\omega]\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\omega_k=\omega_k^+=\omega\), then \(|\overline{\Delta f}_k-\Delta f_k|\le2\omega\).
Exact objective information is the case \(\omega=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\overline{\Delta f}_k>\omega_k+\omega_k^+\), then the true objective reduction is positive.
boundary_notes: A bound on each value is stronger than a bound only on their difference.
No independence or stochastic interpretation is implied.

notation.meaning: Approximate objective value requested with absolute tolerance omega.
Objective reduction computed from inexact values.
Declared positive scale for dynamic accuracy.

review_flags: The reduction-error relation is standard, but no inspected supplied locator supports the complete dynamic-accuracy definition and its exact scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolutely inexact objective information

children.title: Inexact Derivative Information Classes
children.top_down_role: Approximate low-order derivatives and derivative products.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. At \(x\in U\), let \(g(x)\in\mathbb R^n\) approximate \(\nabla f(x)\) and let \(B(x)\in\mathbb S^n\) approximate \(\nabla^2f(x)\). A derivative-product routine may instead return \(B(x)v\) only for requested directions \(v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first- and second-order derivative or derivative-product information. Approximation of derivatives of order three and above is excluded and treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An absolute inexact low-order derivative class with tolerances \((\delta_1,\delta_2)\) consists of responses satisfying \[\|g(x)-
abla f(x)\|\le\delta_1(x),\qquad \|B(x)-
abla^2f(x)\|_{m op}\le\delta_2(x)\] at every queried \(x\). A product-only second-order class is specified by a direction set \(V_x\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and responses \(w(x,v)\) satisfying \[\|w(x,v)-
abla^2f(x)v\|\le\delta_{2,v}(x)\|v\|\quad	ext{for every }v\in V_x.\] The class is model-scaled at radius \(\Delta>0\) when tolerances are chosen so that \(\delta_1(x)\Delta\le\eta_1 q\) and \(\delta_2(x)\Delta^2/2\le\eta_2 q\) for a declared model scale \(q>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-order inexact derivative class provides a gradient approximation and, when second-order information is used, a symmetric Hessian approximation with declared norm-error bounds. A product-only class instead bounds the error in each requested Hessian-vector product over a declared set of directions. A model-scaled subclass chooses the errors so that their possible contributions over steps of radius Delta are controlled relative to a positive model scale.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at every queried point.
Vector errors use the ambient norm and matrix errors use its induced operator norm.
The full-matrix class requires \(B(x)\) to be symmetric; the product class declares the set of directions on which its certificate holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The class is determined by the certificates \(\|g-\nabla f\|\le\delta_1\), \(\|B-\nabla^2f\|_{\rm op}\le\delta_2\), or the explicitly declared product certificate on \(V_x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Hessian operator-norm condition is equivalent to \(\sup_{\|v\|=1}\|(B(x)-\nabla^2f(x))v\|\le\delta_2(x)\).
For symmetric errors, it is also equivalent to \(\sup_{\|v\|=1}|v^\top(B(x)-\nabla^2f(x))v|\le\delta_2(x)\).
special_cases_latex: First-order-only information omits \(B\) and \(\delta_2\).
Exact low-order derivatives correspond to \(\delta_1=\delta_2=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(\|s\|\le\Delta\), \(|(g-\nabla f)^\top s|\le\delta_1\Delta\) and \(|s^\top(B-\nabla^2f)s|/2\le\delta_2\Delta^2/2\).
boundary_notes: Product accuracy on a finite set \(V_x\) does not imply a full operator-norm bound.
This definition does not impose unbiasedness, independence, or probabilistic accuracy.

notation.meaning: Directions covered by a derivative-product certificate.

review_flags: No inspected source was found that supports both the full-tensor and product-only classes with the stated model scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-order inexact derivative information classes

children.title: Inexact Gradient Information
children.top_down_role: Coverage of approximate first-derivative information in complexity analyses.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Gradient Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise deterministic accuracy for a computed first derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a vector \(\bar g(x)\) is a \(\delta_g\)-accurate gradient at \(x\) in norm \(\|\cdot\|\) when
\[
\|\bar g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|_*\leq\delta_g,
\]
where \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is the dual norm. It follows that every directional derivative prediction satisfies
\[
|\langle \bar g(x)-\nabla f(x),s\rangle|\leq\delta_g\|s\|.
\]
Thus \(\delta_g\leq\theta\varepsilon\), with \(0\leq\theta<1\), makes the gradient error a controlled fraction of a target first-order tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact gradient has bounded dual-norm error, which bounds every directional linearization error and can be tied directly to the requested stationarity tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is dual to the step norm \(\|\cdot\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\bar g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|_*\leq\delta_g\) implies \(|\langle\bar g(x)-\nabla f(x),s\rangle|\leq\delta_g\|s\|\) for all \(s\).

children.title: Inexact Hessian Information
children.top_down_role: Coverage of approximate second-derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Hessian Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean operator-norm accuracy for a computed Hessian matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a twice differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a symmetric matrix \(\bar H(x)\) is a \(\delta_H\)-accurate Hessian at \(x\) in the Euclidean operator norm when
\[
\|\bar H(x)-\nabla^2 f(x)\|_2\leq\delta_H.
\]
For every step \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the resulting error in the quadratic Taylor term obeys
\[
\left|\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}(\bar H(x)-\nabla^2f(x))s\right|\leq\tfrac12\delta_H\|s\|_2^2.
\]
Consequently, if \(\delta_H\leq\kappa_H\Delta\) and \(\|s\|_2\leq\Delta\), then this quadratic-term error is at most \(\tfrac12\kappa_H\Delta^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean operator-norm Hessian error controls the quadratic-model error; an error budget proportional to the step radius gives a cubic-order bound within that radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|s^{\mathsf T}(\bar H(x)-\nabla^2f(x))s\right|\leq\delta_H\|s\|_2^2\) for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: radius-scaling constant for the Hessian-error budget

children.title: Inexact Hessian Products
children.top_down_role: Coverage of approximate curvature access through matrix-free products.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Hessian Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free accuracy expressed directly on Hessian-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable at \(x\). A possibly matrix-free oracle \(\mathcal B_x\) supplies \(\delta_{Hv}\)-accurate Hessian products when
\[
\|\mathcal B_x(v)-\nabla^2f(x)v\|\leq\delta_{Hv}\|v\|
\qquad\text{for every queried }v\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
If \(\mathcal B_x\) is linear and the inequality holds for every \(v\), then it is equivalent to
\[
\|\mathcal B_x-
abla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\delta_{Hv}.
\]
For a finite query set, the condition certifies only those products and does not imply a global operator-norm bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each computed Hessian-vector product has error proportional to the vector norm; global operator accuracy follows only for a linear oracle controlled on every vector.
assumptions_latex: The same vector norm defines the induced operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\mathcal B_x(v)-\nabla^2f(x)v\|\leq\delta_{Hv}\|v\|\) on the specified query domain.

children.title: Joint Derivative Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage of coordinated gradient plus curvature accuracy requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Derivative Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled derivative budgets preserving an order-\(p\) model over radius \(\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(p\)-times differentiable, and let \(\overline{\nabla^j f}(x)\) approximate its symmetric order-\(j\) derivative tensor. A radius-scaled joint accuracy regime is
\[
\|\overline{\nabla^j f}(x)-\nabla^j f(x)\|_{[j]}\leq\kappa_j\Delta^{p+1-j},
\qquad j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
For every \(s\) with \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\), the discrepancy between the exact and approximate derivative portions of the degree-\(p\) Taylor polynomial is at most
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{\kappa_j}{j!}\Delta^{p+1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative errors are coupled to the step radius so every derivative order contributes at most order \(p+1\) to the model error.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|_{[j]}\) is the tensor norm induced by the step norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{1}{j!}(\overline{\nabla^j f}(x)-\nabla^j f(x))[s]^j\right|\leq\Delta^{p+1}\sum_{j=1}^{p}\kappa_j/j!\).

notation.meaning: induced norm for order-j multilinear forms

children.title: Inexact Higher Derivatives

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Higher Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tensor-norm control of errors in derivatives of arbitrary finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(p\)-times differentiable at \(x\), and suppose tensors \(\overline{\nabla^j f}(x)\) satisfy
\[
\|\overline{\nabla^j f}(x)-\nabla^j f(x)\|_{[j]}\leq\delta_j,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
If \(\bar T_p(x,s)\) and \(T_p(x,s)\) are the approximate and exact degree-\(p\) Taylor polynomials with the same constant term, then
\[
|\bar T_p(x,s)-T_p(x,s)|\leq
\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{\delta_j}{j!}\|s\|^j.
\]
Thus derivative-order budgets translate directly into a computable polynomial model-error budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tensor-norm errors in higher derivatives yield a sum of order-specific bounds on the discrepancy between exact and approximate Taylor models.
assumptions_latex: Each approximate derivative tensor is symmetric.
The tensor norms are induced by \(\|\cdot\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\bar T_p(x,s)-T_p(x,s)|\leq\sum_{j=1}^{p}\delta_j\|s\|^j/j!\) for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: evaluation of an order-j tensor on j copies of s
