knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact derivatives of orders three through p
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\ge3\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, and let \(f\in C^p(U)\). For \(3\le j\le p\), the exact derivative \(D^jf(x)\) is a symmetric \(j\)-linear form, and \(B_j(x)\) denotes an approximation in the same space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic absolute or step-scaled errors for derivative orders at least three. Low-order gradient and Hessian errors are outside this slot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A \(p\)th-order inexact higher-derivative response at \(x\) is a tuple \((B_3(x),\ldots,B_p(x))\) for which declared tolerances \(\delta_j(x)\ge0\) satisfy \[\|B_j(x)-D^jf(x)\|\le\delta_j(x),\qquad j=3,\ldots,p,\] where the norm is the induced multilinear norm. Relative to a step radius \(\Delta>0\) and scale \(q>0\), the response is model-scaled with constants \(\eta_j\ge0\) when \[\frac{\delta_j(x)}{j!}\Delta^j\le\eta_j q,\qquad j=3,\ldots,p.\] A directional response for a particular step \(s\) is weaker: it need only satisfy \(|(B_j(x)-D^jf(x))[s]^j|\le\widehat\delta_j(x,s)\|s\|^j\), and must be identified as directional rather than tensor-norm accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact higher-derivative information consists of symmetric multilinear forms approximating derivatives of orders three through p, each with a declared induced-norm error. A model-scaled response additionally makes the maximum Taylor-term error over a ball of radius Delta a controlled fraction of a positive scale. A bound only on repeated application to one step is a weaker directional certificate and is not a full tensor-norm guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B_j(x)\) belongs to the same symmetric multilinear space as \(D^jf(x)\).
All tolerances, the radius \(\Delta\), and the scale \(q\) are declared, with \(\Delta>0\) and \(q>0\) in the model-scaled class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Higher-derivative inexactness is certified by \(\|B_j(x)-D^jf(x)\|\le\delta_j(x)\) for every \(j=3,\ldots,p\), optionally strengthened by \(\delta_j(x)\Delta^j/j!\le\eta_jq\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tensor certificate is equivalent to \(\sup_{\|v_1\|,\ldots,\|v_j\|\le1}|(B_j-D^jf)[v_1,\ldots,v_j]|\le\delta_j\).
special_cases_latex: For \(p=3\), the response contains only an approximate trilinear third derivative.
Exact higher derivatives correspond to \(\delta_j=0\) for every \(j\ge3\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(\|s\|\le\Delta\), the order-\(j\) Taylor-term error is at most \(\delta_j\Delta^j/j!\).
boundary_notes: A repeated-direction certificate need not control mixed arguments.
No regularity of \(x\mapsto B_j(x)\) follows from pointwise error bounds.

notation.meaning: Evaluation of a j-linear form on j copies of s.

children.title: Inexact Subproblem Solutions
children.top_down_role: Controlled auxiliary-solver error within outer complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subproblem Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable decrease and residual conditions for terminating an inner model solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be a differentiable regularized or trust-region model, let \(\mathcal S_k\) be its feasible step set, and let \(D_k^{\mathrm{ref}}>0\) be a computable reference decrease. An inexact subproblem solution \(s_k\in\mathcal S_k\) is acceptable when
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{dec}}D_k^{\mathrm{ref}},
\qquad
\|\nabla m_k(s_k)\|_*\leq	au_k,
\]
where \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dec}}\in(0,1]\) and \(\tau_k\geq0\). The first inequality supplies sufficient model decrease; the second bounds inner first-order residual without requiring an exact global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solve is acceptable when it achieves a fixed fraction of a computable reference decrease and meets a prescribed model-gradient residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is differentiable on the feasible step set \(\mathcal S_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\) satisfies both sufficient model decrease and the residual tolerance \(\tau_k\).

The cited conjugate-gradient convergence section does not support this generic combined stopping interface; a method-specific source and an appropriate constrained residual are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified inexact solution of a model subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous model and let \(S_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed feasible-step set containing \(0\). Define \(m_k^*=\inf_{s\in S_k}m_k(s)\) and \(\Delta m_k(s)=m_k(0)-m_k(s)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic inner-solver accuracy expressed through objective decrease and first-order residual certificates; the outer method must separately specify which certificate its complexity analysis requires.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A step \(s_k\in S_k\) is a \((\kappa_{\rm dec},\omega_k)\)-inexact solution of the model subproblem when \[\Delta m_k(s_k)\ge\kappa_{\rm dec}\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k^*\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial m_k(s_k)+N_{S_k}(s_k)\bigr)\le\omega_k,\] where \(0<\kappa_{\rm dec}\le1\), \(\omega_k\ge0\), \(\partial\) is the declared limiting or convex subdifferential appropriate to the model, and \(N_{S_k}\) is the corresponding normal cone. If \(m_k^*=-\infty\) or the optimal value is not available, an algorithm may use a named computable benchmark decrease \(d_k^{\rm ref}>0\), replacing the first inequality by \(\Delta m_k(s_k)\ge\kappa_{\rm dec}d_k^{\rm ref}\); that benchmark defines a distinct certified subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact subproblem solution is a feasible step carrying two explicit certificates: it achieves a fixed fraction of the globally available model decrease and has a bounded first-order stationarity residual for the constrained model. When the global optimal value cannot be used, a declared computable reference decrease may replace it, but the reference must be part of the class definition rather than left implicit.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\) is nonempty, closed, and contains the zero step.
The model has finite \(m_k(0)\), and the global-decrease form requires \(m_k^*>-\infty\).
The subdifferential and normal-cone conventions are fixed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is certified by a decrease fraction and the residual bound \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial m_k(s_k)+N_{S_k}(s_k))\le\omega_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable \(m_k\) and unconstrained \(S_k=\mathbb R^n\), the residual condition becomes \(\|\nabla m_k(s_k)\|\le\omega_k\).
special_cases_latex: An exact global solution has \(\kappa_{\rm dec}=1\) and \(\omega_k=0\), provided the infimum is attained.
For a trust-region set \(S_k=\{s:\|s\|\le\Delta_k\}\), the normal cone incorporates the boundary optimality condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(m_k(0)>m_k^*\), the decrease certificate forces \(m_k(s_k)<m_k(0)\).
boundary_notes: A small stationarity residual alone does not imply a prescribed fraction of global decrease for a nonconvex model.
The number of inner iterations or Hessian-vector products needed to obtain the certificate is a separate complexity quantity.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the model over the feasible-step set.
Required fraction of benchmark model decrease.
Normal cone to the feasible-step set at the returned step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dynamic accuracy policy for imperfect information
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), an optimization method has history \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\), a trial step \(s_k\), an approximate model \(m_k\), a predicted reduction \(q_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\), and requested error tolerances for objective, derivative, model, or subproblem information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic adaptive precision coordinated with current predicted decrease or criticality. Sampling implementations and probabilistic model events are separate subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic accuracy framework is a nonanticipating policy \(\Pi\) that selects iteration-dependent error budgets \(\tau_k=(\omega_k^f,\delta_{k,1},\ldots,\delta_{k,p},\omega_k^{\rm sub})\) and may repeatedly tighten them until a declared computable certificate holds. In the predicted-reduction form, admissibility requires \[\omega_{k,0}^f+\omega_{k,+}^f+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{\delta_{k,j}}{j!}\|s_k\|^j+\omega_k^{\rm sub}\le\kappa_{\rm acc}q_k,\] with fixed \(0\le\kappa_{\rm acc}<1\). In a criticality form, selected derivative tolerances additionally satisfy \(\delta_{k,j}\le\psi_j(\chi_k)\), where \(\chi_k\ge0\) is a computable criticality estimate and each \(\psi_j(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). The framework consists of the policy, the scale, and the certificate; changing any of these defines a different accuracy regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic accuracy framework is a history-based policy that chooses and, if necessary, tightens evaluation and inner-solve tolerances during the run. In its predicted-reduction form, the combined worst-case influence of all admitted errors on the trial comparison must be at most a fixed fraction of the positive predicted reduction. A criticality-based form also requires derivative tolerances to vanish according to declared functions as the computable criticality estimate approaches zero.
assumptions_latex: The policy uses only available history and computable current quantities.
The predicted-reduction form is applied only when \(q_k>0\).
Every error component is measured in units compatible with objective reduction before it enters the combined certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted information budgets satisfy a computable iteration-dependent certificate, such as the combined inequality bounded by \(\kappa_{\rm acc}q_k\), and tighten as the chosen reduction or criticality scale decreases.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The combined certificate may be written \(e_k^{\rm tot}\le\kappa_{\rm acc}q_k\) after defining \(e_k^{\rm tot}\) as the displayed sum of certified error contributions.
special_cases_latex: Objective-only dynamic accuracy retains only \(\omega_{k,0}^f+\omega_{k,+}^f\).
A fixed-accuracy method is recovered when \(\Pi\) returns iteration-independent budgets, but it is dynamically adequate only while the certificate holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever \(q_k\to0\) along certified iterations, the total admitted comparison error also tends to zero.
boundary_notes: The framework does not guarantee that a requested tolerance can be achieved at finite cost.
Error cancellation may not be used unless the certificate explicitly models dependence or signed errors.

notation.meaning: Positive computable scale, typically predicted model reduction.

review_flags: No inspected source was available for the unified combined-error and criticality-scaled definition.

children.title: Implicit Dynamic Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy control expressed through computable model and criticality interfaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Dynamic Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation accuracy selected through current model-decrease and criticality interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(D_k>0\) be the computed predicted decrease and let \(\chi_k>0\) be a computed criticality measure. An implicit dynamic-accuracy interface accepts objective and gradient approximations when
\[
|e_{f,k}(x_k)|+|e_{f,k}(x_k+s_k)|\leq\omega_fD_k,
\qquad
\|e_{g,k}(x_k)\|_*\leq\omega_g\chi_k,
\]
for fixed \(\omega_f,\omega_g\in[0,1)\). The evaluator may choose its internal work adaptively; only these computable, iteration-dependent inequalities are exposed to the optimization method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy is certified against the current predicted decrease and criticality measure, while the evaluator's internal mechanism remains unspecified.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k>0\) and \(\chi_k>0\) are computable from available information.
The error quantities can be bounded or certified by the evaluator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|e_{f,k}(x_k)|+|e_{f,k}(x_k+s_k)|\leq\omega_fD_k\) and \(\|e_{g,k}(x_k)\|_*\leq\omega_g\chi_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit dynamic accuracy through an a posteriori certificate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(Y_k(\ell)\) be information produced at refinement level \(\ell\), let \(C_k(Y_k(\ell))\ge0\) be a computable error certificate, and let \(Q_k(Y_k(\ell))\ge0\) be a computable model-reduction or criticality scale derived from the same response and current algorithmic state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori accuracy control in which no final numerical error tolerance is fixed before the response is computed; refinement is driven by a computable interface between information quality and current criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An implicit dynamic accuracy mechanism is a refinement rule that generates levels \(\ell=0,1,\ldots\) and accepts the first response \(Y_k=Y_k(\ell_k)\) satisfying \[C_k(Y_k)\le\kappa_{\rm imp}Q_k(Y_k),\qquad 0\le\kappa_{\rm imp}<1.\] The certificate is valid only if there exists a true-information error functional \(e_k\) such that \(e_k(Y_k(\ell))\le C_k(Y_k(\ell))\) for every generated level. If \(Q_k(Y)=0\), acceptance requires \(C_k(Y)=0\), unless the method invokes a separately defined termination test. The mechanism is implicit because its accepted effective tolerance \(C_k(Y_k)\) is determined a posteriori by the response-dependent inequality rather than prescribed as a numerical budget before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Implicit dynamic accuracy repeatedly refines an approximate response until a computable upper bound on its true error is small relative to a computable reduction or criticality scale obtained from the current response. The effective tolerance is therefore discovered after evaluation. A zero scale requires a zero certificate unless a separate stopping rule applies.
assumptions_latex: \(C_k\) and \(Q_k\) are computable from current algorithmic data and the candidate response.
The certificate dominates the declared true-information error: \(e_k(Y)\le C_k(Y)\).
The refinement decision at each level uses no future information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted response satisfies \(e_k(Y_k)\le C_k(Y_k)\le\kappa_{\rm imp}Q_k(Y_k)\), with its effective accuracy fixed by this a posteriori certificate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Defining \(\tau_k=C_k(Y_k)\), implicit accuracy yields an accepted tolerance \(\tau_k\le\kappa_{\rm imp}Q_k(Y_k)\), but \(\tau_k\) is not an input to the initial evaluation.
special_cases_latex: An interval-evaluation routine fits the definition when the interval radius is \(C_k\).
An iterative inner solver fits when its computable residual bounds the model-solution error relevant to the outer method.
immediate_consequences_latex: If accepted scales \(Q_k(Y_k)\) tend to zero, the certified true-information errors tend to zero.
boundary_notes: A residual that does not upper-bound the relevant true error is not a valid certificate.
Termination of the refinement loop is not part of the definition and needs an attainability assumption.

notation.meaning: Approximate information at refinement level ell.

children.title: Explicit Dynamic Accuracy

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Dynamic Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct iteration-dependent error budgets for objective and derivative evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a model order \(p\geq1\) and an iteration radius \(\Delta_k>0\). Explicit dynamic accuracy prescribes numerical budgets before evaluation, for example
\[
|\bar f_k-f(x_k)|\leq\kappa_{0}\Delta_k^{p+1},
\qquad
\|\overline{\nabla^j f}(x_k)-\nabla^j f(x_k)\|_{[j]}\leq\kappa_j\Delta_k^{p+1-j},
\quad j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
For every \(s\) with \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\), these budgets make the aggregate error in the degree-\(p\) model at most
\[
\left(\kappa_0+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\frac{\kappa_j}{j!}\right)\Delta_k^{p+1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method directly assigns evaluation tolerances from the current radius, ensuring that total model error has order \(p+1\).
assumptions_latex: The derivative tensor norms are induced by the step norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{aggregate model error}\leq(\kappa_0+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\kappa_j/j!)\Delta_k^{p+1}\) on \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\).

source_refs.locator: 3.1.2 Derivatives and Taylor's Theorem p. 27

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z_{k,i}\) be an exact information component at iteration \(k\), with approximate evaluation routine \(\widetilde Z_i(x;\tau)\). Let \(q_k>0\) and \(\chi_k\ge0\) be computable reduction and criticality scales available before each requested evaluation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A priori dynamic accuracy: numerical error budgets are explicitly selected before the corresponding evaluation. Response-dependent a posteriori acceptance is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit dynamic accuracy policy is a nonanticipating map \[\Pi_k:\mathscr F_{k-1}\times(q_k,\chi_k)\longmapsto(\tau_{k,i})_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R_+^{|I|}\] that supplies each tolerance to its evaluation routine before the response is generated. The returned information is admissible when \(d_i(\widetilde Z_{k,i},Z_{k,i})\le\tau_{k,i}\) for every \(i\in I\). The policy is reduction-scaled when declared weights \(a_{k,i}\ge0\) satisfy \[\sum_{i\in I}a_{k,i}\tau_{k,i}\le\kappa_{\rm exp}q_k,\qquad 0\le\kappa_{\rm exp}<1,\] and criticality-scaled when \(\tau_{k,i}\le\psi_i(\chi_k)\) with \(\psi_i(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). Re-evaluation with a newly selected smaller budget remains explicit because each new tolerance precedes its associated response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit dynamic accuracy is a history-dependent rule that calculates numerical error budgets from currently available reduction or criticality scales and passes those budgets to the evaluation routines before they run. Returned information must satisfy its componentwise requested bounds. Weighted contributions may be required to stay below a fixed fraction of predicted reduction, and individual budgets may be required to vanish with criticality.
assumptions_latex: Each distance or error measure \(d_i\) and weight \(a_{k,i}\) is declared.
The requested tolerance is selected before randomness or numerical error in the corresponding response is observed.
The reduction-scaled form uses \(q_k>0\), and \(0\le\kappa_{\rm exp}<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted component satisfies \(d_i(\widetilde Z_{k,i},Z_{k,i})\le\tau_{k,i}\), with budgets chosen a priori and coordinated by the displayed reduction or criticality inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A common explicit budget \(\tau_k\) is obtained by setting \(\tau_{k,i}=b_i\tau_k\) for fixed \(b_i\ge0\) and choosing \(\tau_k\) to satisfy the weighted inequality.
special_cases_latex: For two objective evaluations with unit weights, the rule may impose \(\tau_{k,0}+	au_{k,+}\le\kappa_{\rm exp}q_k\).
A prescribed derivative schedule \(\tau_{k,1}=c\chi_k\) is an explicit criticality-scaled policy.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(q_k\to0\) and the corresponding weights remain bounded away from zero, the associated requested tolerances tend to zero.
boundary_notes: A routine that only reports an error estimate after computation is implicit unless a new explicit request is issued.
Requested accuracy and achieved accuracy must not be conflated when the evaluation routine can fail.

Declared error measure for information component i.
Weight converting component error into the common reduction scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Sample Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal sample selection from confidence radii and current deterministic accuracy budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), choose target errors \(\delta_{j,k}>0\) and failure probabilities \(\alpha_{j,k}\in(0,1)\) for orders \(j=0,\ldots,p\). For each \(j\), let \(r_j(n,\alpha)\) be a valid nonincreasing confidence radius for an \(n\)-sample estimator \(\widehat D_k^j(n)\). Select
\[
n_{j,k}=\min\{n\in\mathbb{N}:r_j(n,\alpha_{j,k})\leq\delta_{j,k}\},
\]
compute \(\widehat D_k^j(n_{j,k})\), and return these estimators. If each confidence statement is conditionally valid, then all returned errors meet their budgets simultaneously with conditional probability at least \(1-\sum_{j=0}^{p}\alpha_{j,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the smallest sample size whose confidence radius meets each current accuracy budget; a union bound gives simultaneous conditional accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_j(n,\alpha)\) is a valid conditional confidence radius.
For each requested budget, the defining set for \(n_{j,k}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(\|\widehat D_k^j-D^jf(x_k)\|\leq\delta_{j,k}\text{ for all }j\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq1-\sum_{j=0}^{p}\alpha_{j,k}\).

notation.meaning: information available before iteration k sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection rule and conditional union-bound conclusion are internally coherent and algorithmic content fits the leaf, but no source supports this adaptive sampling procedure. The confidence radii and conditional validity assumptions depend materially on the sampling model.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Suppose an information component is an expectation \(Z(x)=\mathbb E[\zeta(x,\xi)]\). At iteration \(k\), an estimator \(\widehat Z_{k,N}=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^N\zeta(X_k,\xi_{k,r})\) is formed from samples generated conditionally on the history \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-size control driven by current model, reduction, or termination accuracy. The definition states a conditional accuracy target but does not assume a particular concentration inequality or sampling distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive sample accuracy policy is a nonanticipating rule selecting a tolerance \(\tau_k>0\), failure budget \(\alpha_k\in[0,1)\), and sample size \(N_k\in\mathbb N\) from the available history and current computable scale, such that \[\mathbb P\bigl(d(\widehat Z_{k,N_k},Z(X_k))\le\tau_k\mid\mathscr F_{k-1}\bigr)\ge1-\alpha_k.\] It is model-scaled when \(a_k\tau_k\le\kappa_s q_k\) for a declared coefficient \(a_k\ge0\), predicted-reduction scale \(q_k>0\), and \(\kappa_s\ge0\). It is termination-scaled when \(\tau_k\le\psi(\chi_k)\) with \(\psi(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). A uniform-reliability policy additionally allocates \(\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k\le\bar\alpha\) for a prescribed total failure budget \(\bar\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive sample accuracy chooses the estimator tolerance, conditional failure probability, and number of samples using the past and the current algorithmic scale. The selected sample size must make the estimator meet its tolerance with the stated conditional probability. Model-scaled policies tie estimation error to predicted reduction, while termination-scaled policies tighten it with criticality. A uniform-reliability version also assigns a summable sequence of failure probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The sample-size decision is measurable with respect to information available before the selected samples are observed.
The estimator's distance \(d\) and conditional probability model are declared.
Any concentration or variance condition needed to make a finite \(N_k\) possible is part of the implementation-specific subclass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \((\tau_k,\alpha_k,N_k)\) satisfy the conditional accuracy inequality, with \(\tau_k\) coordinated to the declared model or termination scale.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The sample size may equivalently be defined as the smallest admissible integer \(N_k=\inf\{N:\mathbb P(d(\widehat Z_{k,N},Z(X_k))\le\tau_k\mid\mathscr F_{k-1})\ge1-\alpha_k\}\), when this set is nonempty.
special_cases_latex: For a sub-Gaussian scalar sample mean with variance proxy \(\sigma^2\), a valid subclass may choose a sample size proportional to \(\sigma^2\tau_k^{-2}\log(1/\alpha_k)\), with constants determined by the stated tail bound.
Fixed-batch sampling is recovered when \(N_k\) is constant.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\sum_k\alpha_k\le\bar\alpha\), the probability that every per-iteration accuracy event holds is at least \(1-\bar\alpha\) under the corresponding union-bound interpretation.
boundary_notes: Marginal, unconditional accuracy is weaker than the displayed conditional requirement.
Optional stopping, sample reuse, and dependence require a concentration statement valid for that sampling protocol.
review_flags: No inspected source was provided for the conditional adaptive-sampling definition, particularly its model-scaled and uniform-reliability variants.

children.title: Probabilistic Model Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Random model-quality frameworks and their complexity interpretations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(X_k\) and \(\Delta_k>0\) be random iterates and radii, and let \(M_k\) be a random model generated after the past sigma-field \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\) is fixed. Let \(A_k\) denote a declared deterministic model-accuracy event on \(B(X_k,\Delta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random model-quality framework stated conditionally on the full past. The deterministic event may encode fully linear, fully quadratic, derivative, or regularized-model accuracy, but must be specified before a complexity interpretation is attached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random model sequence \((M_k)\) is \(p\)-probabilistically accurate with respect to events \((A_k)\) when, for every \(k\), \[\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathscr F_{k-1})\ge p\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad p\in(0,1].\] Each event \(A_k\) must be a measurable statement comparing \(M_k\) with \(f\) on the declared region and in declared norms. For example, a first-order event may require constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\ge0\) such that \[|f(x)-M_k(x)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(x)-\nabla M_k(x)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\] for every \(x\in B(X_k,\Delta_k)\). The conditional probability, rather than an unconditional marginal probability, is part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random sequence of optimization models is probabilistically accurate when, after conditioning on the entire preceding algorithmic history, the declared deterministic model-quality event occurs with probability at least p at every iteration. The event must specify the region, norms, and error scales. A fully linear event, for example, controls function errors by the squared radius and gradient errors by the radius throughout the current ball.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) is measurable relative to the sigma-field containing the newly generated model and current state.
\(\mathscr F_{k-1}\) contains all algorithmic randomness and decisions preceding construction of \(M_k\).
The region, norms, constants, and deterministic inequalities defining \(A_k\) are fixed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathscr F_{k-1})\ge p\) almost surely for every iteration \(k\), where \(A_k\) is the declared model-accuracy event.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalent to \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{A_k}\mid\mathscr F_{k-1}]\ge p\) almost surely.
special_cases_latex: \(p=1\) gives almost-sure deterministic model accuracy conditional on the past.
The displayed fully linear event is a first-order special case.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition permits dependence across iterations, provided the conditional lower bound remains valid.
boundary_notes: An unconditional statement \(\mathbb P(A_k)\ge p\) alone does not satisfy the conditional definition.
Probabilistic model accuracy alone gives neither convergence nor a complexity bound; algorithmic drift and acceptance conditions are additional hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Declared deterministic accuracy event for the kth random model.
Full history before the kth model is generated.
Uniform conditional lower bound on model-accuracy probability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional fully linear and fully quadratic model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) denote the past, and let the random model coefficients at \(x_k\) be \(\bar f_k\), \(g_k\), and, when \(q=2\), \(H_k\). The model is probabilistically \(q\)-accurate on radius \(\Delta_k\) with probability \(p_0\) if, conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\), the event
\[
|\bar f_k-f(x_k)|\leq\kappa_0\Delta_k^{q+1},
\quad
\|g_k-
abla f(x_k)\|_*\leq\kappa_1\Delta_k^q,
\quad
\|H_k-
abla^2f(x_k)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_2\Delta_k
\]
has probability at least \(p_0\), with the Hessian condition omitted for \(q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random first- or second-order model is accurate when radius-scaled coefficient errors hold with a stated probability conditional on the algorithm's past.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable for \(q=1\) and twice differentiable for \(q=2\).
\(\Delta_k>0\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal A_k^{(q)}\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p_0\), where \(\mathcal A_k^{(q)}\) is the displayed coefficient-accuracy event.

notation.meaning: sigma-field generated by the algorithmic past

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probabilistically accurate first- and second-order models
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(U)\), let \(X_k\in U\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let the random quadratic model be \(M_k(X_k+s)=F_k+G_k^\top s+\tfrac12s^\top H_ks\), where \((F_k,G_k,H_k)\) is generated conditionally on \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional random affine or quadratic models with explicitly scaled coefficient errors. The definition separates first-order and second-order accuracy events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the first-order coefficient event \[A_k^{(1)}=\{|F_k-f(X_k)|\le\kappa_0\Delta_k^2,\ \|G_k-\nabla f(X_k)\|\le\kappa_1\Delta_k\}.\] Define the second-order coefficient event \[A_k^{(2)}=A_k^{(1)}\cap\{\|H_k-\nabla^2f(X_k)\|_{\rm op}\le\kappa_2\Delta_k\}.\] The models are probabilistically accurate of order \(r\in\{1,2\}\) with probability parameter \(p_r\) when \(\mathbb P(A_k^{(r)}\mid\mathscr F_{k-1})\ge p_r\) almost surely for every \(k\). An affine first-order model omits \(H_k\). A quadratic model intended only for fully linear accuracy may retain \(H_k\) under a separate uniform boundedness condition without requiring \(A_k^{(2)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random low-order model is first-order accurate when its center value error is of squared-radius size and its gradient coefficient error is of radius size. It is second-order accurate when, in addition, its Hessian coefficient error is of radius size. Probabilistic accuracy requires the appropriate joint coefficient event to hold with a uniform probability lower bound conditional on all previous algorithmic information.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(U)\) and the current trust region lies in \(U\).
\(H_k\) is symmetric whenever a quadratic model is used.
The constants \(\kappa_0,\kappa_1,\kappa_2\) are deterministic and independent of \(k\).
The probability statement is conditional on \(\mathscr F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\mathbb P(A_k^{(r)}\mid\mathscr F_{k-1})\ge p_r\) almost surely at every iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With normalized errors \(E_{k,0}=|F_k-f(X_k)|/\Delta_k^2\), \(E_{k,1}=\|G_k-\nabla f(X_k)\|/\Delta_k\), and \(E_{k,2}=\|H_k-\nabla^2f(X_k)\|_{\rm op}/\Delta_k\), the events impose uniform bounds on the relevant normalized errors.
special_cases_latex: Exact coefficients give \(A_k^{(2)}\) with \(\kappa_0=\kappa_1=\kappa_2=0\).
A random gradient model uses \(F_k\) and \(G_k\) only and is governed by \(A_k^{(1)}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: On \(A_k^{(1)}\), center-value and gradient-coefficient errors vanish at the scales required as \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\).
boundary_notes: Separate marginal probability bounds for coefficient errors do not imply the stated joint event without an allocation argument.
Second-order coefficient accuracy is distinct from merely detecting a direction of negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Curvature Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized eigensolver interface for detecting sufficiently negative Hessian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix or Hessian operator \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), tolerance \(\epsilon_H>0\), and failure level \(\delta\in(0,1)\), draw a unit vector \(v\) from a distribution absolutely continuous on the unit sphere. Apply a randomized Lanczos-type eigensolver that, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), returns a unit vector \(d\) satisfying \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\leq \lambda_{\min}(H)+\epsilon_H/2\). If \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\leq-\epsilon_H/2\), output \(d\) as a negative-curvature direction; otherwise output INCONCLUSIVE. Whenever \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\leq-\epsilon_H\), the method detects negative curvature with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized eigensolver returns a certified negative-curvature direction with prescribed confidence whenever the smallest Hessian eigenvalue is sufficiently negative.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) is accessible through matrix-vector products.
The eigensolver satisfies its stated additive Ritz-value accuracy with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\leq-\epsilon_H\Longrightarrow \mathbb{P}(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\leq-\epsilon_H/2)\geq1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: unit Ritz vector returned by the randomized eigensolver

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) be a symmetric matrix accessible through matrix-vector products, and let \(\epsilon_H>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\) be requested spectral accuracy and failure probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A randomized spectral-probe or eigensolver interface for detecting negative curvature. It defines the accuracy event but does not prescribe Lanczos, power iteration, or another implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized \((\epsilon_H,\delta)\)-curvature detector is a random procedure returning \((\widehat\lambda,v)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\), with \(\|v\|=1\), such that for every symmetric input \(H\), \[\mathbb P\left(\lambda_{\min}(H)\le\widehat\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(H)+\epsilon_H\ \text{ and }\ v^\top Hv\le\lambda_{\min}(H)+\epsilon_H\right)\ge1-\delta.\] On this accuracy event, the detector reports negative curvature when \(v^\top Hv< -\epsilon_H\), returning \(v\), and may report approximate nonnegative curvature when \(\widehat\lambda\ge-\epsilon_H\). The latter report certifies only \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-2\epsilon_H\) under the displayed accuracy convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized curvature detector receives a symmetric matrix through a spectral interface and returns an approximate smallest eigenvalue and a unit vector. With probability at least one minus delta, the reported eigenvalue lies between the true smallest eigenvalue and that value plus epsilon, and the vector's Rayleigh quotient is no larger than the same upper approximation. A sufficiently negative Rayleigh quotient supplies a negative-curvature direction; an approximate nonnegative report supplies only the stated tolerance-dependent lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric and the detector can perform its declared matrix-vector operations.
The probability is over the detector's internal randomness for each fixed input \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(\widehat\lambda\in[\lambda_{\min}(H),\lambda_{\min}(H)+\epsilon_H]\) and \(v^\top Hv\le\lambda_{\min}(H)+\epsilon_H\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The eigenvalue condition is \(0\le\widehat\lambda-\lambda_{\min}(H)\le\epsilon_H\).
special_cases_latex: If \(v^\top Hv<0\), the returned unit vector is a genuine direction of negative curvature.
If \(\delta=0\) were attainable, the interface would be deterministic; the present definition restricts \(\delta\) to \((0,1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: On the accuracy event, \(\widehat\lambda\ge-\epsilon_H\) implies \(\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge-2\epsilon_H\).
boundary_notes: A random vector with a negative Rayleigh quotient but no failure-probability certificate is not a randomized curvature detector in this sense.
Iteration or matrix-vector complexity depends on spectral range and the chosen eigensolver and is not included.

notation.meaning: One-sided additive approximation to the smallest eigenvalue.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected and high-probability complexity guarantee pair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a randomized optimization method, let \(N_\epsilon=\inf\{k\ge0:\mu_f(X_k)\le\epsilon\}\) be the random hitting time of an \(\epsilon\)-stationary point, and let \(C_\epsilon=\sum_{k=0}^{N_\epsilon-1}c_k\) be the associated nonnegative random evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two distinct interpretations of randomized complexity: an expectation bound and a confidence-parameterized tail bound. The pair is definitional and asserts neither bound without a supporting theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probabilistic complexity guarantee pair for cost \(C_\epsilon\) is a pair of functions \((B_{\rm exp},B_{\rm hp})\) satisfying \[\mathbb E[C_\epsilon]\le B_{\rm exp}(\epsilon),\qquad \mathbb P\bigl(C_\epsilon\le B_{\rm hp}(\epsilon,\delta)\bigr)\ge1-\delta\quad\text{for every }\delta\in(0,1).\] The expectation and probability are taken over all algorithmic, oracle, and sampling randomness under the declared problem class. A worst-case pair additionally places a supremum over \(f\in\mathcal F\) on the left side of each relation. The two entries remain distinct because an expected bound does not specify the desired confidence dependence, while a high-probability family must state its dependence on \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A probabilistic complexity guarantee pair records both an upper bound on expected cost to reach the requested stationarity tolerance and a family of cost bounds that hold with probability at least one minus delta. All sources of randomness and the problem class must be fixed. The two guarantees are distinct: an expectation bound alone does not state a confidence-sensitive rate, and a high-probability statement must expose its failure-probability parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(C_\epsilon\) is a nonnegative measurable extended random variable under the declared randomness.
The stationarity measure \(\mu_f\), cost units \(c_k\), problem class, and stopping convention are fixed.
The high-probability function is declared for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guarantee pair consists precisely of \(\mathbb E[C_\epsilon]\le B_{\rm exp}(\epsilon)\) and \(\mathbb P(C_\epsilon\le B_{\rm hp}(\epsilon,\delta))\ge1-\delta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The high-probability relation is equivalently \(\mathbb P(C_\epsilon>B_{\rm hp}(\epsilon,\delta))\le\delta\).
special_cases_latex: Unit iteration cost \(c_k=1\) gives \(C_\epsilon=N_\epsilon\).
A deterministic bound \(C_\epsilon\le B(\epsilon)\) almost surely yields both entries with \(B_{\rm exp}=B\) and \(B_{\rm hp}=B\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If only \(B_{\rm exp}\) is known, Markov's inequality supplies the generic but potentially loose choice \(B_{\rm hp}(\epsilon,\delta)=B_{\rm exp}(\epsilon)/\delta\).
boundary_notes: An asymptotic almost-sure convergence statement is not a finite-time complexity guarantee.
Expected cost and expected stationarity at a fixed budget are different performance criteria.

notation.meaning: Random accumulated cost up to the stationarity hitting time.

children.title: Expected Complexity Guarantees

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Complexity Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected stopping-time bound under conditionally successful random models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) be the algorithmic filtration and let \(I_k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether iteration \(k\) supplies one required successful iteration. Suppose \(\mathbb{P}(I_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p>0\) before termination, and at most \(M(\epsilon)\) successful iterations are required to reach the prescribed \(\epsilon\)-criticality condition. For \(T_\epsilon:=\inf\{t:\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}I_k\geq M(\epsilon)\}\), adaptive Bernoulli domination gives \(\mathbb{E}[T_\epsilon]\leq M(\epsilon)/p\). Thus a deterministic successful-iteration bound transfers to expected randomized complexity with multiplicative penalty at most \(p^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every pending iteration succeeds conditionally with probability at least p, the expected trials needed for M successful iterations are at most M divided by p.
assumptions_latex: Termination requires no more than \(M(\epsilon)\) successful iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[T_\epsilon]\leq p^{-1}M(\epsilon)\).

notation.meaning: indicator of a required successful iteration
deterministic bound on required successful iterations
random stopping time for reaching the accuracy target

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expected M/p bound is standard, but an authoritative locator is absent. A sourced version should also state that M(epsilon) is a positive integer and that I_k is measurable after iteration k while the conditional success probability is evaluated using the pre-iteration sigma-field.

children.title: High-Probability Complexity Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Coverage of guarantees holding outside a controlled failure event.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Complexity Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative exponential tail bound under uniformly positive conditional success probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq0}\) be a filtration, let \(I_k\in\{0,1\}\) be \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable, and suppose \(\mathbb P(I_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p\) almost surely before termination, where \(p\in(0,1]\). Let \(M(\epsilon)\in\mathbb N\) successful iterations suffice for the prescribed \(\epsilon\)-criticality condition, and define \(T_\epsilon:=\inf\{t\geq0:\sum_{k=0}^{t-1}I_k\geq M(\epsilon)\}\). For \(\delta\in(0,1)\), set \(N:=\left\lceil p^{-1}\bigl(2M(\epsilon)+8\log(1/\delta)\bigr)\right\rceil\). Conditional Bernoulli domination and a multiplicative Chernoff lower-tail bound give \(\mathbb P(T_\epsilon>N)\leq\delta\), and hence \(\mathbb P(T_\epsilon\leq N)\geq1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each pending iteration succeeds conditionally with probability at least p, then a conservative iteration budget proportional to p inverse times M plus the logarithm of the inverse failure probability attains the required number of successes with probability at least one minus delta.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable and \(\mathbb P(I_k=1\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p\in(0,1]\) holds before termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\!\left(T_\epsilon\leq\left\lceil p^{-1}\bigl(2M(\epsilon)+8\log(1/\delta)\bigr)\right\rceil\right)\geq1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on conditional success probability
positive integer bound on the required successful iterations
stopping time for accumulating the required successes

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional Bernoulli domination and multiplicative Chernoff lower-tail inequality

children.title: Confidence-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coverage of computational overhead associated with stronger confidence levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch-size tradeoff between conditional model reliability and total component-oracle work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a randomized model built from a batch of size \(b\in\mathbb N\) costs exactly \(b\) component-oracle calls and has conditional failure probability at most \(e^{-\kappa b}\), where \(\kappa>0\). For a target conditional success probability \(p\in(0,1)\), it suffices to choose \(b\geq\kappa^{-1}\log(1/(1-p))\). If \(M(\epsilon)\in\mathbb N\) successful trials suffice and the conditional success bound holds before termination, then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), the total component-oracle cost \(C_{\epsilon,\delta}\) is at most \(b\left\lceil p^{-1}\bigl(2M(\epsilon)+8\log(1/\delta)\bigr)\right\rceil\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the batch size exponentially improves the conditional model reliability but linearly increases each trial's component-oracle cost; the corrected high-probability trial bound gives an explicit total-cost tradeoff.
assumptions_latex: The conditional model-failure probability is at most \(e^{-\kappa b}\), with \(\kappa>0\) and \(b\in\mathbb N\).
Each trial costs exactly \(b\) component-oracle calls.
\(M(\epsilon)\in\mathbb N\) successful trials suffice, and the conditional success bound holds before termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\geq\kappa^{-1}\log(1/(1-p))\Longrightarrow\mathbb P\!\left(C_{\epsilon,\delta}\leq b\left\lceil p^{-1}\bigl(2M(\epsilon)+8\log(1/\delta)\bigr)\right\rceil\right)\geq1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: batch size and component-oracle cost per trial
exponential concentration rate for model failure
target lower bound on conditional success probability
component-oracle cost through termination at the stated accuracy and confidence targets

children.title: Tail-Guarantee Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage of probabilistic assumptions insufficient for high-confidence complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Guarantee Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite expectation alone does not imply exponential stopping-time tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be integer-valued with \(\mathbb{P}(T=m)=c\bigl[m^2\log^2(m+1)\bigr]^{-1}\) for \(m\geq1\), where \(c>0\) normalizes the probabilities. Then \(\mathbb{E}[T]=c\sum_{m\geq1}[m\log^2(m+1)]^{-1}<\infty\), but \(\mathbb{P}(T>t)\) decays only on the order of \(1/(t\log^2 t)\), not exponentially. An algorithm that performs its sole successful update at time \(T\) therefore has finite expected complexity but no bound \(\mathbb{P}(T>t)\leq Ae^{-at}\) with fixed \(A,a>0\). The missing assumption is a uniform positive conditional success probability or comparable tail control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heavy-tailed stopping time can have finite mean while violating every exponential high-probability complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[T]<\infty\), while for every \(A,a>0\) there exists \(t\) such that \(\mathbb{P}(T>t)>Ae^{-at}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit distribution has finite mean and a polynomial-logarithmic rather than exponential tail, so the failure-boundary content is mathematically appropriate. No inspectable source is supplied for the tail asymptotics or their complexity interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structured objective and inexpensive-constraint problem family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^m\) be smooth on a neighborhood \(U\supseteq X\), let \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be smooth on \(F(U)\), and let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional extension family retaining exploitable composite objective structure and constraints enforceable by a declared inexpensive primitive. General nonlinear constraints requiring their own restoration or multiplier-complexity theory are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The structured objective-constraint extension family consists of problems \[\min_{x\in X}\ \Phi(x):=h(F(x))+g(x),\] equipped with two declared computational interfaces. First, derivatives of \(F\) and \(h\), or their required contractions, are available to build regularized local models of \(h\circ F\), while \(g\) is handled without replacing it by an unjustified smooth Taylor expansion. Second, feasibility in \(X\) is enforced by an exact primitive \(P_X\), retraction, or model-step set \(S(x)\) satisfying \(s\in S(x)\Rightarrow x+s\in X\). Membership in the family requires the cost of this enforcement primitive and of the structural operation for \(g\) to be counted separately and assumed bounded by the declared per-iteration implementation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This extension family contains composite optimization problems whose objective is a smooth outer function applied to a smooth mapping, plus a proper lower-semicontinuous structured term, over a closed feasible set. The family includes explicit interfaces for building models from the smooth composition, handling the structured term without pretending it is smooth, and enforcing feasibility exactly through a projection, retraction, or feasible-step mechanism. The cost convention for those structural operations is part of the family definition.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and closed, and \(F\) and \(h\) possess the derivative order required by the chosen regularization model.
\(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and the algorithm declares the exact structural operation used to handle it.
The feasibility primitive returns points in \(X\), or the step interface satisfies \(s\in S(x)\Rightarrow x+s\in X\).
The complexity accounting explicitly states whether structural and feasibility operations have unit, bounded, or separately measured cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A problem belongs to the family exactly when it has the form \(\min_{x\in X}h(F(x))+g(x)\) together with declared model-construction, structured-term, feasibility, and cost interfaces satisfying the stated domain conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constraint may be absorbed into the structured term as \(g+\iota_X\), where \(\iota_X(x)=0\) for \(x\in X\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise, only when the resulting structural operation remains available under the declared cost model.
special_cases_latex: Smooth constrained optimization is obtained with \(g=0\).
Composite unconstrained optimization is obtained with \(X=\mathbb R^n\).
A simple bound-constrained problem uses a componentwise projection as its feasibility primitive.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every generated trial point is feasible when the algorithm restricts steps to \(S(x)\) or applies an exact feasibility primitive.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover arbitrary nonlinear constraints merely because they can be written as a set \(X\); the enforcement interface must satisfy the declared complexity model.
Nonsmooth stationarity and regularity conditions must be chosen for the particular structural subclass.
No evaluation-complexity rate is asserted by membership alone.

notation.meaning: Set of steps that preserve feasibility from x.
Extended-valued indicator function of the feasible set.

The proposed composite-plus-simple-constraint scope may need narrowing once authoritative evidence is available.

children.title: Structured Objective Complexity
children.top_down_role: Objective structures that change model construction, derivative cost, or evaluation accounting.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be represented by finitely many elements \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{q_i}\to\mathbb{R}\) and linear maps \(U_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{q_i}\), with \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(U_i x)\). Fix a derivative order \(p\geq 0\), an algorithm \(\mathcal A\), and a termination test \(\chi(x)\leq\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic evaluation complexity for smooth structured objectives; the definition does not itself assert a convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The structured-objective complexity of \(\mathcal A\) at tolerance \(\epsilon\) is the array \(\mathcal N_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon)=(N_{i,r}(\epsilon))_{1\leq i\leq m,\,0\leq r\leq p}\), where \(N_{i,r}(\epsilon)\) is the number of evaluations of \(\nabla^r f_i(U_i x)\) made before \(\mathcal A\) first returns an iterate satisfying \(\chi(x)\leq\epsilon\). Given nonnegative primitive costs \(c_{i,r}\), its realized evaluation cost is \(C_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon;c)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{r=0}^{p}c_{i,r}N_{i,r}(\epsilon)\). A scalar undifferentiated oracle count is the special convention \(c_{i,r}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an objective represented as \(f(x)=\sum_i f_i(U_i x)\), structured-objective complexity records separately how many values or derivatives of each element function are requested before the prescribed criticality tolerance is attained. A chosen cost model converts this count array into \(C_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon;c)=\sum_{i,r}c_{i,r}N_{i,r}(\epsilon)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(U_i x)\) is the representation exposed to the algorithm.
Every primitive evaluation is assigned unambiguously to an element \(i\) and derivative order \(r\).
The stopping time is the first returned iterate satisfying the fixed test \(\chi(x)\leq\epsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon)=(N_{i,r}(\epsilon))_{i,r}\) and \(C_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon;c)=\langle c,\mathcal N_{\mathcal A}(\epsilon)\rangle\) define respectively the structured oracle count and its cost-weighted realization.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Grouping only by derivative order gives \(N_r(\epsilon)=\sum_iN_{i,r}(\epsilon)\).
Grouping only by element gives \(N_i(\epsilon)=\sum_rN_{i,r}(\epsilon)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=1\), the definition reduces to the usual order-separated oracle count for an unstructured objective.
If a full objective evaluation always evaluates every element once, then one full pass contributes \(N_{i,0}=1\) for every \(i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Two algorithms with the same total oracle count may have different realized costs when the \(c_{i,r}\) are nonuniform.
Subsampling and elementwise derivative reuse can be represented without changing the termination criterion.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes inner linear-algebra work unless that work is incorporated through additional cost coordinates.
A decomposition not exposed to the algorithm does not induce structured complexity under this definition.

notation.meaning: Number of order-\(r\) evaluations of element \(i\) before termination.
Cost assigned to one such primitive evaluation.
Fixed criticality measure used for termination.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). For each element \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(U_i\in\mathbb{R}^{q_i\times n}\) and \(\phi_i:\mathbb{R}^{q_i}\to\mathbb{R}\), where usually \(q_i\ll n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth partial separability with fixed linear element-variable maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially separable objective is a sum \(f(x)=\sum_i\phi_i(U_i x)\) of element functions, each depending only on the lower-dimensional element variables \(U_i x\). For twice continuously differentiable elements, the gradient and Hessian are sums of lifted element gradients and Hessians.

equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(f_i(x)=\phi_i(U_i x)\), each element satisfies \(f_i(x+d)=f_i(x)\) for every \(d\in\ker U_i\).
Coordinate partial separability is obtained when each \(U_i\) selects a subset of the components of \(x\).

A sparse-Hessian element representation is obtained when every \(U_i\) selects only a few coordinates.

The global Hessian can be applied through the sum of lifted element-Hessian products without forming every dense entry.

The decomposition is representation-dependent and may not be unique.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Least-Squares Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual representation, derivatives, and Gauss–Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a continuously differentiable residual map \(r:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\), a nonlinear least-squares objective has the form \(f(x)=	frac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\). With Jacobian \(J(x)\), its gradient is \(
abla f(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}r(x)\). If every residual is twice continuously differentiable, then \(
abla^2f(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)
abla^2r_i(x)\). The residual-linearization model is \(m_x(s)=	frac12\|r(x)+J(x)s\|_2^2\); its quadratic curvature matrix is \(J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)\), giving the Gauss–Newton trust-region or regularization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear least squares admits residual-based gradient, Hessian, and Gauss–Newton model formulas obtained by linearizing the residual vector.
assumptions_latex: The Hessian identity additionally requires twice continuously differentiable residual components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla f=J^{\mathsf T}r\) and \(
abla^2f=J^{\mathsf T}J+\sum_i r_i
abla^2r_i\), with Gauss–Newton model \(m_x(s)=	frac12\|r+Js\|_2^2\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be a residual map with components \(c_i\), and let \(J(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) denote its Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained finite-dimensional nonlinear least squares with the Euclidean residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonlinear least-squares objective is \(f(x)=	frac12\|c(x)\|_2^2=	frac12\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i(x)^2\). If \(c\in C^1\), then \(
abla f(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). If \(c\in C^2\), then \(
abla^2f(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i(x)
abla^2c_i(x)\). The Gauss--Newton model at \(x\) is \(m_x(s)=	frac12\|c(x)+J(x)s\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear least-squares objective minimizes half the squared Euclidean norm of a nonlinear residual, \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\). Its gradient is \(J(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)\), and its Hessian separates into the Gauss--Newton term \(J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)\) and a residual-weighted second-derivative term.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable for the gradient and model formulas.
\(c\) is twice continuously differentiable for the Hessian formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2\), with residual-linearized model \(m_x(s)=\tfrac12\|c(x)+J(x)s\|_2^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Minimizing \(f\) is equivalent to minimizing \(\|c(x)\|_2\), since squaring is increasing on \([0,\infty)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x)=Ax-b\), the problem is linear least squares and \(\nabla^2f=A^{\mathsf T}A\).
At a zero-residual point, \(c(x)=0\), the exact Hessian equals \(J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Trust-region and regularization models can be constructed from residual and Jacobian products.
The objective is a finite sum whose components are the squared residuals \(c_i(x)^2/2\).
boundary_notes: Using a norm other than \(\ell_2\) defines a different residual minimization class.
Robust losses \(\sum_i\rho(c_i(x))\) are not ordinary nonlinear least squares unless \(\rho(t)=t^2/2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-oracle representation and unbiased subsampled derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-sum objective has the form \(f(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x)\), where each component \(f_i:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) is accessible through a component oracle. If \(I_1,\ldots,I_b\) are sampled independently and uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), then \(g_b(x)=b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b
abla f_{I_j}(x)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[g_b(x)\mid x]=
abla f(x)\). When the components are twice differentiable, \(B_b(x)=b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b
abla^2f_{I_j}(x)\) likewise satisfies \(\mathbb E[B_b(x)\mid x]=
abla^2f(x)\). These estimators define subsampled regularization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform component sampling gives unbiased gradient and Hessian estimators for a finite-sum objective, enabling subsampled models.
assumptions_latex: Component indices are sampled independently and uniformly.
Gradient identities require differentiability; Hessian identities require twice differentiable components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[g_b(x)\mid x]=\nabla f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[B_b(x)\mid x]=\nabla^2f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(N\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), and fix a derivative order \(p\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth finite sums with component-level deterministic or randomized access.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-sum objective averages finitely many component functions, \(f(x)=N^{-1}\sum_i f_i(x)\). Complexity may therefore be counted in component-oracle calls rather than only full evaluations. Uniform sampling with replacement gives the component average over a sample as an unbiased estimator of the corresponding full derivative.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Plus-Simple Composite Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized Taylor model retaining a tractable nonsmooth term exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+h(x)\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), where \(f\) is \(p\)-times continuously differentiable and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and computationally tractable through its proximal map. At \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\), a composite regularization model is \(m_x(s)=T_p^f(x;s)+h(x+s)+\frac{\sigma}{p+1}\|s\|^{p+1}\), with \(\sigma>0\), where \(T_p^f(x;s)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\frac1{j!}\nabla^j f(x)[s]^j\). The nonsmooth component is retained exactly rather than Taylor expanded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth-plus-simple objective is modeled by Taylor expanding only the smooth term while retaining the proximable nonsmooth term exactly.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_x(s)=T_p^f(x;s)+h(x+s)+\frac{\sigma}{p+1}\|s\|^{p+1}\) is the composite regularization model.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional first-order evaluation bound over a coordinate box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\), and define \(\chi_C(x)=\|x-P_C(x-\nabla f(x))\|_2\). Suppose a feasible trust-region or regularization method produces, whenever \(\chi_C(x_k)>\epsilon\), a successful iteration satisfying \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\geq c\chi_C(x_k)^2\), and its total iterations are at most \(\kappa\) times its successful iterations plus \(q\). Then it reaches \(\chi_C(x_k)\leq\epsilon\) within at most \(\kappa\left\lceil(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/(c\epsilon^2)\right\rceil+q\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease proportional to squared projected criticality yields an order epsilon-to-minus-two bound for bound-constrained first-order criticality.
assumptions_latex: Successful iterations decrease \(f\) by at least \(c\chi_C(x_k)^2\).
Total iterations are bounded by \(\kappa\) times successful iterations plus \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_\epsilon\leq\kappa\left\lceil\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{c\epsilon^2}\right\rceil+q=O(\epsilon^{-2})\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(x\in C\), and let \(f\in C^1\). Define \(N_C(x)=\{v:\langle v,y-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall y\in C\}\) and \(T_C(x)=N_C(x)^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order Euclidean criticality for a smooth objective on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The projection criticality residual is \(R_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}(x-P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x)))\) for \(\alpha>0\). The following zero conditions define the same first-order critical points: \(R_\alpha(x)=0\) for one, equivalently every, \(\alpha>0\); \(-
abla f(x)\in N_C(x)\); and \(\langle
abla f(x),dangle\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x)\). A continuous scalar termination measure is \(\chi_C(x)=\|R_1(x)\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective over a closed convex set, vanishing projected-gradient residual, membership of the negative gradient in the normal cone, and nonnegative directional derivative along every tangent direction describe the same exact first-order criticality condition. The norm of the unit-step projection residual supplies a continuous termination measure.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in C\) and \(f\) is continuously differentiable at \(x\).
Projection and polarity use the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\alpha(x)=0\iff-\nabla f(x)\in N_C(x)\iff\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle\geq0\ \forall d\in T_C(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P_C(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))=x\) for every \(\alpha>0\).
The variational inequality \(\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) holds for every \(y\in C\).
special_cases_latex: If \(x\in\operatorname{int}C\), then \(N_C(x)=\{0\}\), so criticality reduces to \(\nabla f(x)=0\).
For a box, the condition becomes the familiar coordinatewise sign conditions at active bounds.

The tangent-projected gradient norm may be discontinuous at changing active faces, whereas the projection residual remains continuous.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Criticality Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projected-gradient residual for convex-set stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f\) be differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\), and let \(\alpha>0\). The projected criticality measure at \(x\in C\) is \(\chi_{C,\alpha}(x)=\alpha^{-1}\|x-P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x))\|_2\), where \(P_C\) is the Euclidean projection onto \(C\). It is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(x=P_C(x-\alpha
abla f(x))\), equivalently when \(-
abla f(x)\in N_C(x)\). Thus \(\chi_{C,\alpha}(x)=0\) is equivalent to first-order stationarity for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected criticality is the scaled distance from a point to its projected gradient step; it vanishes exactly at convex-set first-order stationary points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_{C,\alpha}(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow-\nabla f(x)\in N_C(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Criticality Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order feasible-descent measure for a closed convex constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f\) be differentiable near \(x\in C\), and let \(T_C(x)\) be the Bouligand tangent cone. The tangent criticality measure is
\[
\chi_T(x):=\max\{-\nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}d:d\in T_C(x),\ \|d\|\leq 1\}=\|\Pi_{T_C(x)}(-\nabla f(x))\|.
\]
Thus \(\chi_T(x)\geq0\), and \(\chi_T(x)=0\) exactly when \(-\nabla f(x)\in T_C(x)^\circ=N_C(x)\), equivalently \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The measure is the greatest unit feasible directional decrease, equivalently the norm of the negative gradient projected onto the tangent cone; it vanishes precisely at first-order stationary points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_T(x)=\|\Pi_{T_C(x)}(-\nabla f(x))\|\), and \(\chi_T(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla f(x)+N_C(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Tangent Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinitesimal equivalence, with exact finite-step equivalence on affine feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\alpha>0\), define \(G_\alpha(x):=\alpha^{-1}(x-\Pi_C(x-\alpha\nabla f(x)))\). If \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex, then
\[
\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\|G_\alpha(x)\|=\|\Pi_{T_C(x)}(-\nabla f(x))\|.
\]
If, locally along every sufficiently short projected step, \(C\) agrees with \(x+T_C(x)\), the equality holds for all sufficiently small \(\alpha\). In particular, for an affine set \(C=x+L\), it holds for every \(\alpha>0\): \(\|G_\alpha(x)\|=\|\Pi_L(-\nabla f(x))\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected-gradient and tangent measures agree infinitesimally. They agree exactly for finite steps when local feasible geometry is affine, particularly on affine constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\|G_\alpha(x)\|=\chi_T(x)\), with exact finite-step equality in the stated locally affine regime.

direction subspace of an affine feasible set

children.title: Boundary Geometry Effects

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Geometry Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature prevents finite projected steps from being determined solely by the tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^2:\|z\|\leq1\}\), \(x:=(1,0)\), and \(\nabla f(x):=(0,1)\). Then \(-\nabla f(x)\in T_C(x)\), so \(\chi_T(x)=1\). For every \(\alpha>0\), however,
\[
\Pi_C(x-\alpha\nabla f(x))=\frac{(1,-\alpha)}{\sqrt{1+\alpha^2}},
\]
and consequently
\[
\|G_\alpha(x)\|^2=\frac{(1-(1+\alpha^2)^{-1/2})^2}{\alpha^2}+\frac{1}{1+\alpha^2}<1.
\]
Hence curved boundary geometry changes every finite projected-gradient measure although its zero-stepsize limit equals the tangent measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a curved boundary, finite projected-gradient measures can differ from tangent measures at every positive stepsize, even though they converge to the tangent measure as the stepsize vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|G_\alpha(x)\|<\chi_T(x)=1\) for every \(\alpha>0\), while \(\|G_\alpha(x)\|\to1\) as \(\alpha\downarrow0\).

children.top_down_role: Marks where inexpensive-set complexity ceases to represent the cost and geometry of constrained optimization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\) are nonlinear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming contrasted with optimization over a fixed inexpensive convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A problem crosses the boundary from inexpensive convex-set complexity to general nonlinear-constraint complexity when its feasible set \(\mathcal F=\{x:c(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\) is accessed through evaluations or derivatives of \((c,g)\), rather than through a fixed cost-free convex-set oracle. Its evaluation complexity must then include constraint calls \(N_c,N_g\) and derivative calls, and termination must control both violation \(v(x)=\|c(x)\|+\|[g(x)]_+\|\) and an appropriate constrained-stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General nonlinear constraints lie beyond the inexpensive-set model when feasibility and local geometry must be discovered by evaluating constraint functions and derivatives. Complexity must then account for these calls, while termination must address both constraint violation and constrained stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are explicitly evaluated nonlinear maps.
No fixed inexpensive projection oracle for \(\mathcal F\) is assumed.
The norm used in the violation measure is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relevant complexity object includes \((N_f,N_c,N_g,N_{\nabla f},N_{J_c},N_{J_g},\ldots)\), and success requires \(v(x)\leq\epsilon_v\) together with a declared stationarity tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Slack variables can convert inequalities into equalities plus bounds, but evaluations of the transformed nonlinear equalities remain part of the cost.
Penalty and augmented-Lagrangian reformulations move constraints into an objective without eliminating their evaluation cost.
special_cases_latex: Affine constraints with a reusable factorization may still be treated as an inexpensive fixed set under an explicit cost convention.
Nonlinear equations are included by taking \(m_i=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Objective-only evaluation bounds do not characterize total evaluation complexity.
Feasible-iterate methods and infeasible-iterate methods require different enforcement primitives but remain on the general-constraint side of the boundary.
boundary_notes: The distinction is computational, not solely set-theoretic.
Convexity of \(\mathcal F\) does not restore inexpensive-set complexity if constraint evaluation or projection is expensive.

children.title: Nonconvex Feasible-Geometry Boundary
children.top_down_role: Higher-order criticality dependence on nonlinear feasible curves and tangent geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Feasible-Geometry Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Higher-order constrained criticality depends on feasible-curve curvature beyond the tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(C:=\{(t,t^2):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\), \(x_*:=(0,0)\), and \(f(x,y):=y\). The tangent space is \(T_C(x_*)=\operatorname{span}\{(1,0)\}\), and \(\nabla f(x_*)^{\mathsf T}d=0\) for every \(d\in T_C(x_*)\). Moreover, \(\nabla^2f(x_*)=0\), so an ambient-Hessian test restricted to the tangent space detects no curvature. Nevertheless, along the feasible curve \(\gamma(t)=(t,t^2)\),
\[
(f\circ\gamma)'(0)=0,\qquad (f\circ\gamma)''(0)=2,
\]
and \(x_*\) is a strict constrained local minimizer. Thus tangent data and the ambient objective Hessian alone do not characterize higher-order criticality on nonlinear feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curved feasible set can create second-order growth absent from both the tangent restriction and ambient objective Hessian, so higher-order tests must incorporate feasible-curve or constraint curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tangent geometry and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\) alone are insufficient to determine second-order constrained behavior.

notation.meaning: tangent space to the feasible curve at the reference point
smooth parametrization of the feasible curve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parabola example correctly exhibits feasible-curve curvature that is absent from the ambient objective Hessian and tangent restriction, and failure_boundary fits the container. No cited source or explicit standard-field rationale supports the nontrivial higher-order interpretation.

children.title: Penalty Criticality-Transfer Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of transferring higher-order criticality through penalty reformulations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Define \(h(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-\) and \(\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order transfer from a nonsmooth exact penalty to the original smooth nonlinear program; higher-order transfer is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The penalty criticality-transfer interface is the implication from penalty stationarity to constrained stationarity. A point \(\widehat x\) is penalty-stationary when \(D\phi_1(\widehat x;\mu;p)\geq0\) for every \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Transfer to the original problem is valid only after feasibility and the relevant regularity or parameter conditions are imposed: a feasible penalty-stationary point may satisfy the KKT conditions, whereas an infeasible penalty-stationary point is only an infeasible stationary point. The boundary is therefore the failure of the unconditional implication \(0\in\partial\phi_1(\widehat x;\mu)\Rightarrow\widehat x\text{ is constrained-critical}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty stationarity transfers to constrained stationarity only under additional conditions, notably feasibility. A stationary point of the penalty that remains infeasible is classified as an infeasible stationary point and is not thereby a KKT point of the original nonlinear program.
assumptions_latex: The constraint functions and objective possess the derivatives required by the selected KKT conditions.
Directional stationarity is tested in every direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty stationarity plus feasibility can transfer to KKT criticality under the stated regularity regime; penalty stationarity alone does not imply constrained criticality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Directional stationarity may be written \(0\in\partial\phi_1(\widehat x;\mu)\) using the appropriate nonsmooth subdifferential.
Failure may occur through \(h(\widehat x)>0\) together with stationarity of the infeasibility measure.
special_cases_latex: For a strict local KKT solution, sufficiently large \(\mu\) can make the solution a local minimizer of the \(\ell_1\) penalty.
Quadratic penalties are smooth but generally not exact for any finite penalty parameter.
immediate_consequences_latex: An evaluation-complexity result for reducing a penalty residual must also control feasibility before it is interpreted as constrained complexity.
Higher-order criticality of the penalty requires separate transfer conditions.
boundary_notes: Exactness of local minimizers is not identical to equivalence of all stationary points.
This record does not claim second- or higher-order criticality transfer.
